In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Truthful Lord, may He be exalted, says, opening the Surah of al-Anfal:

﴿They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: "The spoils of war belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah, set right what is between you, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers."﴾ (8:1):

The question presupposes a questioner: they are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It presupposes one who is asked, namely the Messenger (peace be upon him). And it presupposes a subject about which the question is asked, which is the matter raised in the question.

The subject of the question may exist in itself, just as we ask our friend: "What did you eat today?" This question defines the scope of the answer, and the answer likewise defines that scope.

The subject of the question in the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: "It is a harm, so keep away from women during menstruation and do not approach them until they are purified."﴾ (2:222), the answer indicates it. They did not ask about the causes of menstruation, or why it stops for a pregnant woman or for one who has reached old age. Rather, the subject of the question, which is clear from the answer of the Truthful and Blessed Lord, is: may a man have intercourse with a woman during menstruation or not?

Another question they asked the Messenger (ﷺ) concerned orphans, and the answer defines the subject of the question. Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿They ask you about orphans. Say: "Setting right their affairs is good. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers. Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer. And had Allah willed, He would have put you in difficulty. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise."﴾ (2:220).

This was because they were apprehensive about mixing with orphans in their wealth, eating with them, and other forms of dealing, out of scrupulousness and distance from doubtful matters. The answer came to define the subject of the question. Sometimes the question comes with the scope of the answer already defined, because the answer is general, such as the words of the Truthful and Blessed Lord:

﴿They ask you about the crescent moons. Say: "They are timings for the people and for the Hajj."﴾ (2:189).

They asked Muhammad (ﷺ): why does the crescent begin small, why does it grow, and then why does it disappear in the waning phase? This is a question of astronomy. The Messenger (ﷺ) answered them only within the limits from which they benefit, which is the practical, utilitarian value. The answer came: ﴿Say: they are timings for the people and for the Hajj.﴾ For although we live in this twentieth century, some people still deny a scientific fact that has been established beyond any doubt. We tell the layman: the crescent resembles the paring of a fingernail, then it grows until it becomes round, then it gradually disappears. On this, the poet says:

"The utmost light of the moon I had hoped for
is like the paring cut from the fingernail."

Had he told them that the crescent appears when the earth comes between the sun and the moon, and then begins to become full in succession, their minds could not have grasped this matter. So he gave them the direct, useful wisdom that their minds fully comprehend. Then minds advanced through knowledge, and we reached the study of the motion of the celestial spheres, which clarifies all astronomical details.

There is also a question that comes about a specific matter, such as the words of the Truthful:

﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: "Fighting therein is grave, but barring from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him, and the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people from it, is graver in the sight of Allah."﴾ (2:217). Thus we know that the subject of the question is the ruling on fighting in the sacred month, not a request to specify the sacred months themselves.

The Truthful and Blessed Lord says here: ﴿They ask you about the spoils (al-anfal)﴾. Al-anfal is the plural of nafl (with a fatha on the first and second letters), like sabab and asbab. What is meant by nafl here is booty, because it is from the bounty of Allah, the Exalted, and one of the distinctions of our master Muhammad (ﷺ), a distinction this Ummah has been given over the earlier nations. Nafl with a sukun means an addition, and from it comes prayer of nafl (voluntary prayer), because it is an addition beyond the obligatory prayer. Our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, says in another verse with this meaning: ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it as a nafilah (extra) for you﴾. Nafilah means an additional matter that is not obligatory. Therefore we say: nafl is additional worship, and its condition is that it be of the same kind as what has been obligated upon you, because a person does not worship his Lord according to his personal whim; rather, the servant worships his Lord in whatever form of worship Allah has prescribed. If he wishes to add to it, let it be of the kind that Allah has prescribed, so that the servant does not invent acts of worship that are not legislated. Therefore the Truthful and Blessed Lord said to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And from the night, awake for prayer as an additional (nafilah) for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾ (17:79). Nafl, then, is an act of worship beyond the basic obligation.

When Allah tested our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him) by commanding him to slaughter his son Isma'il, the test came not by explicit revelation but by a dream, and it was a severe trial. The test was not, for example, that someone else would slaughter Isma'il and Ibrahim would endure his loss; rather, he himself was to slaughter his son. Thus the trial was great, especially since it came only at the end of his life. This matter was a harsh burden upon the soul. Therefore our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, made clear that Ibrahim was an ummah (a community), meaning that the qualities of faith required of a complete community were gathered in him.

﴿And when Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾ (2:124). Observe the mercy of prophethood in the conduct of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he came to carry out the command of the dream to slaughter his son, because the dreams of prophets are revelation. Therefore he did not wish to take his son without informing him of the truth, for had he done so, he would have exposed his son for a moment to the thought of disobedience to his father, and the son might have said: "What kind of man is this who slaughters his son?" Ibrahim also wished that his son share in the reward and that the son submit to the command of the Truthful and Blessed Lord just as his father did. So he said to him:

﴿O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so consider what you think﴾ (37:102).

Thus Ibrahim (peace be upon him) explained the trial that had come to him as a dream. Then what does the son say in answer to his father's question?

﴿He said: "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the steadfast"﴾ (37:102). That is, Isma'il (peace be upon him) surrendered his reins to the command of the Truthful and Blessed Lord. The Lord, may He be exalted, continues describing the trial of Ibrahim with the slaughter of the son, saying:

﴿So when they both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead (103), We called out to him: "O Ibrahim, (104) you have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, We thus reward the good-doers." (105)﴾ (37:103–105). After both Ibrahim and his son Isma'il were content, submitted their matter to Allah, and complied with the command to carry out the decree, Allah in His mercy lifted this decree. Therefore the Truthful and Blessed Lord describes this trial and His honoring of it with the ransom, saying:

﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial (106), and We ransomed him with a great sacrifice (107)﴾ (37:106–107).

This event teaches us, O Muslim, that when Allah's decree comes to you, beware of despairing, beware of resentment, beware of anger, beware of rebelling, for by doing so you prolong the decree upon yourself. But submit to the decree of Allah and it will be lifted, for a decree is not lifted until it is accepted. Thus the reward of Ibrahim's patience with the decree was not merely the ransoming of Isma'il with a great sacrifice; beyond that, the Lord gives him good news of further bounty, saying:

﴿And We gave him good news of Ishaq, a prophet among the righteous﴾ (37:112). That is, not only did He give him a second son, but a son who would be a prophet and righteous. Another increase in the Lord's bounty to Ibrahim comes in His saying:

﴿And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub as an additional gift (nafilah), and We made them all righteous﴾ (21:72). Thus the bounty of the Truthful and Blessed Lord to Ibrahim is manifested: He gives him not only a son who preserves his remembrance, but a son who also preserves the trust of the call. All of this is a nafilah from Allah, a generous additional gift and great favor to the father of the prophets.

So nafl is a matter additional to the basic. An example is what Allah specially granted to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"I have been given five things which none before me was given: I was helped with terror (for a distance of a month's journey); the earth was made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification, so whoever of my Ummah reaches the time of prayer, let him pray; spoils were made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and every prophet was sent to his own people specifically, while I was sent to all people generally."(1)

So Allah's legislation of spoils in Islam is an addition beyond the basic, because spoils were not lawful for any prophet before our Messenger (ﷺ).

There is nafl, there is ghanimah (spoils), there is fay' (returned property), and there is qabad.

We will summarize the meaning of each:

Ghanimah: what the Muslims take from defeated enemies, and it is divided among them in specific proportions: a fighting man has one share, and a horseman has two shares. This is only an example; its division follows the legislation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The distinction between nafal and nafl, with the middle letter vowelled or sukun, has been explained above. Fay' is all that comes to the Muslims without war or compulsion. "Qabad" with the middle letter vowelled means the thing seized, which is what has been gathered of the spoils before it is divided.

But if the ruler (wali al-amr) declares to the fighters, encouraging them to press the battle, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did when he said: "Whoever kills a disbeliever, his spoils are for him" (2), that is an addition to his share in the spoils.

A commander may send a detachment and encourage it to face hardships, saying to its members: "For you is half of what you capture," or a quarter or a fifth. This means they have the right to take the proportion the commander has specified for them as an addition, and then the spoils are divided afterward. When the fighters take the plunder, goods, equipment, and money from prisoners, these are called ghanaim; but when the spoils are gathered before the ruler, it becomes qabad, which has been explained.

On the day of Badr, an incident occurred which the noble Companion Sa'd ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying:

"I said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has today healed me of the polytheists, so give me this sword." The Messenger (peace be upon him) said: "This sword is neither yours nor mine, so put it down." I said: So I put it down, then I returned and said: Perhaps this sword will be given to one who does not have a trial like mine. Then the Messenger of Allah called me from behind me. The Companion said: Has Allah revealed anything about me?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You had asked me for the sword, but it is not mine; it has been given to me, so it is yours." He said: Allah then revealed this verse: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾ (8:1). That is, the Messenger (ﷺ) would not rule on the matter of the sword until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down His ruling. We all know that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out for the battle of Badr not intending to fight, but intending to intercept the caravan carrying the goods of Quraysh coming from Syria, guarded by only forty men. Therefore the Muslims set out, and their number was three hundred and thirteen men, with neither equipment nor

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 2:**

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) comes after this to clarify who the believers are, saying:

﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely.﴾

In these two noble verses there are five attributes, arranged in a doctrinal, behavioural and bodily order, and by them the identification of the word "the believers" is determined. These attributes are: first, that when Allah is mentioned their hearts tremble; second, that when Allah's verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith; third, that upon their Lord they rely; fourth, that they establish the prayer; and fifth, that they spend from what Allah has provided them.

The first attribute of the believers is: ﴿when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾ (part of verse 2 of surah al-Anfal). Wajal (trembling) is fear accompanied by a shock that produces goose-bumps and agitation in the heart. When the poets wanted to give an image of this feeling, one of them said:

*"It is as if the heart, on the night it was said that it would be sent out in the morning or the evening with Layla al-'Amiriyya, were a dove whose foot a snare had caught, struggling with the snare while its wing was caught."*

The poet depicts the state of his heart when he hears the news of his beloved's departure: it has become like a dove trying to free itself from a net or a trap in which it has fallen. It struggles against the trap until it escapes, and it trembles in such a situation. This is the state of the heart at the moment of separation from the beloved, according to the poet.

If the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, drives the hearts of the believers to trembling, does this not contradict the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah. Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.﴾ (surah al-Ra'd, 28)

In truth, there is no contradiction between the two statements, because the remembrance of Allah, exalted be He, comes in various states. If a person is wasteful toward himself, he trembles when he remembers Allah, whose method he has opposed. If a person observes the right of Allah in every action to the extent of his ability, then his heart must find rest at the moment of remembering Allah, because he has followed the method of Allah as far as he is able, as in: ﴿as far as he is able to find a way﴾.

Therefore fear or trembling arises from awe and the overpowering presence of the attributes of majesty (jalal). Tranquillity comes from the radiance and tenderness of the attributes of beauty (jamal). For this reason one verse combines them, the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted be He:

﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book consistent and repeating, whereat shiver the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah.﴾ (part of verse 23 of surah al-Zumar)

So the skins shiver with fear, trembling and awe before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; then they soften in tranquillity and in hope of the tenderness of the Bestower, glorified and exalted be He, because our Lord said:

﴿Inform My servants that I am indeed the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ (surah al-Hijr, 49)

Therefore let no one say that there is a contradiction between trembling and tranquillity, for both come from the remembrance of Allah in the various states of a human being. When a person trembles, he turns toward doing good and finds tranquillity, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted be He:

﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ (part of verse 114 of surah Hud)

**Does faith increase or decrease?**

The scholars have differed on this matter. When we look at the saying of the Truth, we find that it affirms the increase of faith. When we ask, "What is iman (faith)? And what is Islam? ... etc.," we find the answer in the clarification of the Messenger (ﷺ) and his response to the questioner in the following hadith, which is narrated by the noble companion, our master Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting out among the people, when a man came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is iman?" He said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His Book, His meeting, His messengers, and that you believe in the Resurrection, the Last Day." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Islam?" He said: "Islam is that you worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, that you establish the prescribed prayer, pay the obligatory zakat, and fast Ramadan." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is ihsan (excellence)?" He said: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him; for if you do not see Him, He sees you." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" He said: "The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking; but I will tell you of its signs: when the slave-girl gives birth to her mistress, that is one of its signs; when the barefoot, naked ones become the leaders of the people, that is one of its signs; and when the shepherds of the flocks compete in building tall buildings, that is one of its signs. [These are] among five things that none knows but Allah." Then the Messenger (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ Then the man turned away, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Bring the man back to me." They went to bring him back but saw nothing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That was Gabriel; he came to teach people their religion."(1)

When Gabriel (peace be upon him) came asking, in order to teach some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Messenger (peace be upon him) told him about iman: that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day. In another narration he mentioned belief in qadar (divine decree), its good and its evil.

All of these are matters of the unseen (ghayb). One does not say of a perceptible matter that it is iman. No one says, "I believe that I am moving on the ground," because this is a sensory matter, and iman is only in unseen matters. The first of them is that you believe in one God whom eyes cannot perceive, and He is unseen; and in His angels, who are unseen, and we affirm their existence because He informed us of that existence. Likewise, we believe in the Books sent down to the messengers, and in the messengers. It is true that the Book is a sensory matter and the messenger likewise has a sensory existence, but we have not witnessed the revelation as it descended upon the messenger with the Book. Therefore it is an unseen matter. Likewise belief in the Last Day is an unseen matter, and belief in qadar, whose wisdom is hidden from us. All of these, then, are unseen matters.

This is iman at its peak. But there is another iman that arises because we know that legislation did not come all at once; rather it came in stages. A legislation descends first, and we believe that it is from Allah. Thus what increases and decreases in iman is belief in the obligations and that they proceed from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Whenever a verse descended with new legislation, it increased the believers in faith. When the command to pray descended, they believed in establishing it, responded and carried it out; then fasting came, and they complied with its command; then the command of zakat came, and there was obedience and implementation. Of course there is a difference between believing in a thing and doing a thing. Faith is one thing, and its performance is another, for Islam is the outward submission to the method, and applying everything that Islam brings is a continuous and increasing faith, because we believed that what comes from the method is from Allah. Thus what increases is the consequences of faith: the obligations and the compliance with these obligations. An example of this is what we all know, the saying of the Truth:

﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able to make their way to it.﴾ (part of verse 97 of surah Al 'Imran)

But there are people who cling to the literal wording of the saying of the Truth:

﴿And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.﴾ (part of verse 97 of surah Al 'Imran)

Those who cling to the literal wording of the saying of the Truth have not asked: disbelief in what? Did he disbelieve because he did not perform the pilgrimage? No. His disbelief in this matter occurs only if he denies that the pilgrimage is a pillar of Islam. What is required of us as iman is to acknowledge the pilgrimage as a pillar of Islam within the limits of ability. If a person performs it, he has carried out the ruling; but if he does not perform it, that may be due to lack of ability.

The Truth, blessed and exalted be He, concludes this noble verse that we are discussing with His saying:

﴿And upon their Lord they rely.﴾

The prepositional phrase (al-jar wa al-majrur) that is the complement of the verb is always placed after it, but here the prepositional phrase comes first. Therefore the style contains restriction and limitation (hasr wa qasr), as when we say: "To Zayd is the wealth," meaning that the wealth belongs to no one else. The saying of the Truth, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, means that they do not rely on anyone else; rather they have restricted their reliance (tawakkul) to Allah, glorified and exalted be He. Tawakkul means that you believe you have a deputy (wakil) who takes charge of your affairs. The evidence is that for something you cannot manage, you say: "I have entrusted so-and-so to accomplish it for me in the best manner." And in order to choose the one you entrust, who is suitable to perform that task, you declare with tranquillity that you have entrusted so-and-so.

Thus the meaning of ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾ is that they entrust their affairs to the one whom they have trusted with their interests, namely the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, the Mighty and Great, who created the universe and placed in it causes that lead to effects, the causes being the means and the effects the result. Then He left matters that have no causes, except that we always observe the Causer, who is Allah, exalted be He. So whenever any matter is difficult for you in its causes, beware of despairing that it will not happen. Rather say: "That is the matter of causes; as for me, I have a Lord who created the causes, and He is Able over all causes."

In our daily lives we notice that people confuse the work of the limbs with the work of the hearts. A person may think that he is relying on Allah and not taking the causes, and he inclines to laziness, saying: "I rely on Allah." To him we say: No. This is from you a reliance on others (tawakul), not tawakkul, because tawakkul is not the work of the limbs; tawakkul is the work of the hearts.

The believer who receives the method of Allah with understanding finds the causes he must take. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, is the Supreme Causer, and iman confirms that the limbs work and the hearts rely. The limbs must plough the land, choose good seed, scatter it on the ground, water it and tend it. These processes are called causes. Then you do not rest only on causes; rather you must say: above all causes there is the Causer. It is possible that the crop becomes green and grows, and then a calamity of rain or heat comes and destroys it.

As for one who transfers tawakkul to the limbs, we say to him: you have relied on others, that is, you transferred the work of the heart to the limbs. Whoever says this is lying to himself and to people, because he has been lazy in taking the causes and claimed that he relies on Allah. If one of these people were truthful in his reliance on Allah, he would take the causes. Often I say to whoever claims tawakkul together with laziness: Why do you not let food come to your mouth? Why do you extend your hands to it? The one who is lazy is lying about tawakkul. For example, no one lets a piece of meat leap from the plate into his mouth; rather he takes it with his hand, chews it with his teeth, and swallows it after chewing. If he were truthful that tawakkul means that his limbs do not work, he would not have done any of that. But he lies and relies on others in what concerns him, and he employs his limbs in what comforts him, and does not use them in matters that tire him. The saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, is:

﴿And upon their Lord they rely.﴾

This saying means that they believe the causes are from the creation of Allah. When the believer takes the causes, he believes that he turns to Allah and depends upon Him; but if the causes are difficult for him, he knows that he has a Lord. That is why He said: ﴿and upon their Lord﴾. The Lord (rabb) is the One who creates from nothing and provides from non-existence. Since He created you and sustained you from non-existence before He obligated you, is it reasonable that He would wrong you? Certainly not. But you must realise that He created the limbs for you, so use the limbs for what they were created for.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 3:

﴿Those who establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them.﴾ (8:3)

The following verse comes to clarify the work of the limbs (al-jawarih), and it carries the fourth and fifth of the attributes of the believers: ﴿Those who establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).

Standing, sitting, recitation, glorification and takbir in prayer are works of the limbs. Likewise, zakat is a work that results from an earlier work. So, in order for zakat to be paid, one must exert effort and take the means (al-asbab) to produce what supports you and your close circle of wife, children, and then relatives. After that, there flows from wealth that from which zakat is deducted. This is, of course, not the zakat on crops, which is paid on the day of harvest.

﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ (part of verse 141 of Surat al-An'am).

We always find prayer and zakat mentioned together, and you will not find a verse that mentions prayer without also mentioning zakat, because prayer means your life affairs in which you strive for the means of this world, and you turn to the Truth, glory be to Him, and stand before Him. That is, you have set aside a portion of the time you spend in the movement of your life to stand in it before your Lord, the Creator of the means.

Zakat means that you set aside a portion of your wealth. That is why we said: prayer contains zakat and more. You pay about two and a half percent of what remains with you of wealth that reaches the nisab and is in excess of the basic need. But by prayer you sacrifice some of the time you spend in the work that brings you the principal of wealth. So in prayer there is zakat and more. In zakat you give up some wealth, but in prayer you give up the time which is the place of work, and in which you produce sustenance, and sustenance is the vessel of zakat.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, concludes this verse saying:

﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾. We know that sustenance, as the scholars mentioned, is everything from which a person benefits. Even the thief who steals and benefits from his theft, this is considered sustenance for him, but it is unlawful sustenance, and he has a punishment in this world if he is caught, and he will not escape the punishment of God, the just Judge, in this world and the Hereafter. This is, of course, not the lawful sustenance that comes from a permissible work. The true believer is one who spends from this lawful sustenance, whether for the requirements of his life or for the care of the community of faith.

Then the Blessed and Exalted Truth says:

﴿Those are the believers in truth. For them are degrees with their Lord and forgiveness and noble provision﴾ (8:4).

"Those" refers to those whom God has favored with the five attributes mentioned earlier. These are the ones whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned, whose faith is increased by the verses, who put their trust in their Lord, establish prayer and give zakat. These are the believers in truth: ﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾.

Let us know that the truth is that which is firm and does not change, which is not carried away by transient things, and to which all people submit because it relates to the interests of their lives. If falsehood comes to dislodge the truth, you find the truth firm and unshakable because it is strong. Let us read the saying of the Truth, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿He sends down from the sky water, so the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire seeking an ornament or utensil is a foam like it. Thus does God present the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it will vanish away as scum on the bank; but as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus does God present parables﴾ (13:17).

When rain falls from the sky, every valley takes from its water according to its width and depth, and fills up. You see the foam, which is scum, floating on top of the torrent; it is a froth caused by the presence of impurities such as chaff and other things. This is an example we see in our lives: we find the earth, the people, and all creatures benefit from water, but they do not benefit from the scum or froth. Then in the same verse the Truth moves from the parable of the fire, saying:

﴿And from that which they heat in the fire seeking an ornament or utensil is a foam like it﴾ (part of 13:17).

When you see a piece of iron turning to liquid by melting in the fire, you see sparks flying from it, and floating on the surface of the molten iron; this is what is called "the dross of iron" (khabath al-hadid), and this dross is removed so that the iron remains pure, so that swords, daggers and other things can be made from it. This same process happens to gold when the goldsmith melts it to remove any impurities and reshape it into jewelry.

The foam of water, the foam of iron, and the foam of gold gather at the edges, and what remains is clear water, and likewise iron and gold. That is why the Truth says:

﴿Thus does God present the truth and falsehood﴾ (part of 13:17). That is, the truth remains clear and firm, while falsehood rises up to gather at the edges, to be carried away without benefit.

God, glory be to Him, clarifies the elevation of His word in another verse, saying:

﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of God is the highest﴾ (part of 9:40).

We note that the Blessed and Exalted Truth attributed the lowering to the word of the disbelievers, while His word, glory be to Him, has firm elevation.

Here the Truth makes clear that the believers who possess these five attributes are believers in true faith. He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾. The meaning of this is that there are believers who are not at a high level of faith, meaning that there are stations and degrees of faith that vary, and for each measure of attributes there is a corresponding station and bounty.

We see that people, when one of them loves another, pour out their goodness upon him. You find the one who is not a scholar taking some knowledge from the scholars he loves; the weak man who gives his affection to a strong man is helped by the strong man with some of his strength; the poor man who gives his affection to a rich man is given some wealth by the rich man; and the foolish man takes from the sensible people he loves some measure of reasoning about matters.

So, those who are people of affection, closeness and piety are granted abundance from the Master, and they are among those whom God has singled out for bounties. Whoever has these attributes and is a believer in truth will have degrees with his Lord proportionate to his share of the truth and his share of purity. Let us know that walking the path of truth gives much. The example we offer for this is that we find someone who prays the five times at their appointed times, and this is the general requirement; if he prays twice that at night, or persists in prayer in congregation and binds himself to God's way, he will take a share of purity he did not have before, and he will find in his heart illuminations and manifestations, and the affairs of his life will go with ease and facility. It may be that a person of this sort, for example, when leaving the house is asked by his wife: "What shall we cook today?" and he answers: "Let us pass this day with what we have left from yesterday."

When he returns he may be surprised to find that his brother has come from the countryside and brought him a gift of duck, cream and pastries. His wife asks him: "Did you know your brother was coming?" He says: "I did not know." This is merely an example, but the bounties of purity are greater than that, materially and spiritually, and whoever persists in worship and adds to it and performs all of that with its due, God's bounty to him will increase, for God never tires of giving to the people of purity. Whoever tries such worship and increases it will find God's bounty increasing.

I always give this example, and to God belongs the highest likeness, and He is exalted above comparison: suppose a person wanted to travel from Cairo to Alexandria, and asked another person, who said to him: "If you go by such-and-such road you will find a good rest stop, unlike such-and-such road."

The traveler follows the advice of the one who guided him, finds him truthful, and is thereafter at ease with his opinion. Likewise the people of purity are the people of giving, and according to their purity is this giving. What encourages people who go to extremes in worship is this illumination, and there are those who describe one of them as "majdhub" (one drawn in by divine attraction). Whoever applies this description to the devout ascetic sees the high station pulling this worshipper toward it. On the other hand, this ascetic looks at those who stumble in the pursuit of worldly life, and describes them to himself as "al-ghallaba" (the simple, poor folk), and prays for them.

I say to whoever sees one of these people: you have no concern with any of these people; beware of troubling them and leave them in their state, so long as none of them asks you for anything. ﴿For them are degrees with their Lord﴾.

Degrees among people are advancements one strives for, so what of the degrees that are with the Lord? Since God, glory be to Him, has promised them high degrees with Him, they have guaranteed forgiveness, because each of them will be purified by forgiveness. The Truth bestowed the degrees before the forgiveness because He, glory be to Him, created creatures and knows that they are people of change; He knows that there are those who have been wasteful toward themselves and who try to do good deeds, because they believe that good deeds erase bad deeds. He, glory be to Him, has taught us that the markers of the religion take their share from those who are wasteful toward themselves, because whoever is not wasteful toward himself is found obeying God with a quiet, monotonous obedience, with nothing behind him to lash his back. As for those who committed sins, these sins keep them awake at night. The one who is wasteful toward himself, at the moment of his excess, thinks he has taken one thing from God by stepping outside His method, so our Lord makes clear to him: beware of thinking that anyone can deceive God. You will work much and eagerly to serve God's method. And we find the one who is wasteful toward himself, at the moment of awakening and repentance, rushing to do good deeds. In confirmation of the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Indeed, God supports this religion through the corrupt man﴾ (1).

Because the corruption of the corrupt man takes shape before him and shows him the evil outcome, so he rushes to do good deeds to erase the bad deeds. As for the one who has not erred, you find him calm of heart, at peace in soul, with nothing lashing his back.

1 Jami' al-Ahadith by al-Suyuti, vol. 2, p. 325, narrated by al-Tabarani.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 8, verse 4:

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Those are the true believers. For them are ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness and generous provision.﴾ (8:4)

"Those" (ulaika) refers to those whom God has favored with the five qualities mentioned earlier. These are the ones whose hearts tremble at the mention of God, whose faith is increased when the verses are recited to them, who put their trust in their Lord, who establish the prayer and give the zakat. These are the true believers: ﴿Those are the true believers.﴾

Let us know that the truth (al-haqq) is the thing that is firm and unchanging, which is not swept away by passing circumstances, and to which all people submit because it is tied to the interests of their lives. If falsehood comes to dislodge the truth, we find the truth firm and immovable, because it is strong. Let us read the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking ornaments or goods, there is a foam like it. Thus God strikes the parable of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but that which benefits people remains on the earth. Thus God sets forth parables.﴾ (13:17)

When rain falls from the sky, every valley takes from its water according to its width and depth, and it fills up. You see the froth, which is foam, floating on top of the torrent. It is the result of air caused by the presence of impurities such as straw and other things. This is an example we see in our lives: the land, the people and all creatures benefit from the water, but they do not benefit from the foam or froth. Then the Truth, in the same verse, moves from the parable of water to the parable of fire, saying:

﴿And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking ornaments or goods, there is a foam like it.﴾ (part of 13:17)

When you see a piece of iron turning into a liquid by melting in the fire, you see sparks flying from it, and floating on the surface of the molten iron. This is what is called "the dross of iron" (khabath al-hadid). This dross is removed so that the iron remains pure, to make swords, daggers and other things from it. The same process happens with gold when the goldsmith melts it to remove any impurities and reshapes it to become an ornament.

The foam of water, the foam of iron and the foam of gold gather at the sides, and what remains is pure water, pure iron and pure gold. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Thus God strikes the parable of truth and falsehood﴾ (part of 13:17), meaning that the truth remains pure and firm, while falsehood rises up to gather at the sides, to pass away without benefit.

God, glorified and exalted, clarifies the supremacy of His word in another verse, saying:

﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of God is the highest.﴾ (part of 9:40)

We note that the Truth, blessed and exalted, made the word of the disbelievers "lowest" (by a making/ja'l), whereas His word, glorified and exalted, has lasting supremacy.

The Truth here shows that the believers who possess these five qualities are believers in the true sense of faith, so He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Those are the true believers.﴾ This means that there are believers who are not at a high level of faith; that is, there are stations and degrees of faith that vary, and for each measure of these qualities there is a corresponding station and bounty.

We see people, when one of them favors another with his affection, pour out of their goodness upon him. The non-scholar takes some knowledge from scholars whom he loves; the weak person who gives his affection to a strong person is helped by the strong with some of his strength; the poor man who gives his affection to a rich man is given some money by the rich; and the fool takes from the wise who love him a measure of reasonableness in matters.

So the people of affection, nearness and piety are overflowed upon by the Lord, and they are among those whom God has singled out for gifts. Whoever has these qualities, and is a true believer, will have degrees with his Lord corresponding to his share of the Truth and his share of purity. Let us know that walking the path of truth gives much. The example we offer for this is that we find someone who prays the five prayers at their times, which is the general requirement; if he prays double that at night, or persists in congregational prayer and binds himself to God's way, he will take a share of purity he did not have before, and he will find in his heart illuminations and manifestations, and the affairs of his life will go with ease and facility. It may be that a person of this kind, for example, is going out of the house, and his wife asks him: "What shall we cook today?" and he answers: "Let us get through this day with what we have left from yesterday."

When he returns he may be surprised to find that his brother has come from the countryside and brought him a gift of duck, cream and pastries. His wife asks him: "Did you know your brother was coming?" He says: "I did not know." This is merely an example, but the gifts of purity are more than that, materially and spiritually. Whoever persists in worship, adds to it, and performs all of it with its due, God's gift to him will increase, because God never tires of giving to the people of purity. Whoever tries such worship and increases it will find God's gift increasing.

I always give this example, and to God belongs the highest likeness, for He is exalted above comparison. Suppose a man wanted to travel from Cairo to Alexandria, and asked another man, who said to him: "If you take such-and-such road, you will find a good resting place, unlike the other road." The traveller follows the advice of his guide, finds him truthful, and is at ease afterward with his opinion. Likewise, the people of purity are the people of giving, and according to their purity is this giving. What encourages those who go to extremes in worship is this illumination. There are those who describe such a person as "majdhub" (drawn in by spiritual attraction), and whoever applies this description to the ascetic worshipper sees the high station pulling this worshipper toward it. On the other hand, this ascetic looks at those who stumble in pursuit of the world, describes them to himself as "the poor wretches" (al-ghallaba), and prays for them.

I say to whoever sees one of these people: you have no business with any of them; beware of troubling them, and leave them to their state, so long as none of them asks anything of you. (They have degrees with their Lord.)

Degrees among people are advancements one strives for, so what of the degrees that are with the Lord? Since God, glorified and exalted, has promised them high degrees with Him, they are assured forgiveness, because each of them will be purified by forgiveness. The Truth gave the bestowal of degrees before forgiveness, because He, glorified, created creation and knows that they are people of change, and He knows that there are those who have transgressed against themselves and try to do good deeds, because they believe that good deeds erase bad deeds. He, glorified, has taught us that the landmarks of the religion take their share from those who have transgressed against themselves, because whoever has not transgressed against himself you find obeying God with calm, steady obedience, with nothing behind him to lash his back. As for those who have committed evil deeds, these deeds keep them from sleep. The one who transgresses against himself, in the moment of transgression, thinks he has taken from God one thing and gone behind His way, so our Lord clarifies to him: beware of thinking that anyone can deceive God. You will work much and with longing for serving God's way, and we find the one who transgressed against himself, at the moment of awakening and repentance, rushing to do good. In confirmation of the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿Indeed God supports the religion through the wicked man.﴾(1)

For the wickedness of the wicked man takes shape before him and shows him the evil of his end, so he rushes to do good to erase his bad deeds. As for the one who has not erred, you find him calm of heart and tranquil of soul, with nothing to lash his back.

﴿For them are degrees with their Lord, and forgiveness and generous provision﴾ (part of 8:4). Is this provision produced by something generous? The answer is no, because generosity was transferred from the noble source until the provision itself became generous, as if this provision were fond of its owner. When our Lord gives a person a blessing and the servant then uses it in obedience, the blessing feels glad to go to this person, because he has used it in obedience and in what pleases God, mighty and majestic.

And you should know that provision knows your location better than you know its location. No one knows the address of the provision God has decreed for him, but the provision knows the address of its owner, and searches for him everywhere until it finds him. Thus we understand that generosity extends to the provision itself, so the provision becomes generous.

All this discussion came in connection with the dispute over the spoils and the bounties. Our Lord judged and decided, and made clear that the spoils belong to God and to the Messenger, and no one has any word after the word of God. This incident concerning the spoils occurred at the time of going out to war: when the Messenger (ﷺ) wanted to go out to battle, there was a group among them who disliked this going out, then accepted it. But their situation changed regarding the spoils, and some of them demanded more than they deserved. Therefore the Lord, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, though a party of the believers were truly averse.﴾ (8:5)

1. Jami' al-Ahadith by al-Suyuti, vol. 2, p. 325; narrated by al-Tabarani.

"Kama" indicates a comparison of one situation with another: they accepted the division of God over the spoils after having rejected it, and likewise they accepted, earlier, to go out to meet the caravan (nafir) after their aversion to that. But they went out, fought and were victorious, then disagreed over the spoils, and finally were content with the division of God the Exalted and His Messenger, may blessings and peace be upon him.

Does the mention of their aversion to going out to war constitute a criticism of them? No. This statement has a human dimension, because one who wants to enter a battle must have a strong expectation that he will win; otherwise he will regard the act of going out to fight as a gamble. The Muslims at that time were few in number and had no equipment; indeed they had only two horses among them. Their going out was for the merchandise and the caravan, not to meet a large army. Thus the aversion regarding this matter did not stem from defiance of the commands of God the Exalted or the demands of the Messenger, may blessings and peace be upon him, but they viewed the whole matter by human measures and found in it no probable balance. God wanted to establish for them that if they had gone and triumphed over the caravan alone, they would have been called a band of highwaymen who had pounced upon their merchandise and plundered it. The caravan had only forty men, while the Muslims were three hundred and more, and it was reasonable that they would be victorious. But our Lord willed to give them victory over the army (nafir) that the disbelievers had summoned from Mecca, a mighty host in number and equipment, comprising the champions and chieftains of Quraysh, so that the will of the Truth might be realized in bringing falsehood to nothing. ﴿Just as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, while a party of the believers were indeed averse﴾.

The "going out of the house" here refers to the Messenger's departure from Medina to meet the disbelievers. This group of believers was not carried by their aversion outside of faith, because the meaning of "firq" (group) is a company that separates from another company while being joined together by a single bond; the army, for example, consists of divisions (firaq) gathered under one army.

The groups spoken of here are those who disliked going out to fight, although they were also believers. We know that aversion to fighting is a natural human reaction, and He, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah: 216).

The Almighty then says:

﴿They argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear, as though they were being driven to death while they watch.﴾ (8:6)

"They argue with you concerning the truth," that is, they dispute with you over the matter of going out to meet the armed force (al-nafir), after the true promise from Allah, mighty and majestic, had become clear to them. That promise was that one of the two groups would be yours: either the caravan (al-'ir) or the great armed host that Quraysh had assembled to meet them. Since the Truth has promised you one of the two groups, why do you not take the promise with the strongest of the two groups? Why do you want the promise with the weakest of the two groups?! Allah, the Truth, glorified and exalted, has promised you that one of the two groups will be yours. Logic and reason confirm that, since Allah, mighty and majestic, has promised us one of the two groups, we should advance toward what is most beneficial for Islam and for the truth for which we fight, and that we should confront the group possessing strength, might and power. For it may be true that victory over the caravan is certain, but that victory would afterwards remain merely a victory of which it is said: "It is the victory of highwaymen, not of people of a cause of faith and religion."

For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the one without thorns (i.e., the unarmed one) would be yours. But Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers.﴾ (8:7)

So logic requires that, since Allah, mighty and majestic, promised His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one of the two groups, a group in the caravan and the other in the armed host, logic required that the believers turn to face the strong group, because victory over the armed host is more honourable than victory over the caravan. ﴿They argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear, as though they were being driven to death while they watch.﴾

We note that there is "sawq" (driving) and there is "qiyada" (leading). Leading means being at the front to guide people along the way, while "sawq" comes from behind, urging the one who advances to shorten the distance and the time, such that instead of covering the distance in an hour, for example, one covers it in half an hour.

As for His saying, ﴿they are being driven to death while they watch﴾ (part of 8:6), it means that they were not willingly setting out, but were being pushed toward it forcibly, while they looked at the horror of death. For they imagined that facing a thousand warriors of Quraysh was a difficult matter, since a thousand against three hundred is no small matter, as it would require every Muslim to face three men who had the equipment and the arms. So the image that presented itself to them was a hideous one. But when they looked at it this way, they did not consider that they had with them a Lord who would give them victory over all of these.

The Word of Truth says next:

﴿And [remember] when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours; but Allah wills to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the last of the disbelievers.﴾ (8:7)

The promise from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, must be received by the one promised as true. This is because what casts doubt on the promises people make to one another is that a human being is subject to changes. You may promise someone something, and then you try to fulfil what you promised but you are unable to keep the promise; or you had power and it came to an end; or your opinion may change. Thus the promise of a created being, who is weak, is not guaranteed. But the promise of the One who is capable and strong, before whom no obstacles stand in the way of carrying out what He wills, is a true promise, and they must receive this promise as true. ﴿And [remember] when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours﴾.

That is, if you were inclined and loved that the group without strength (al-shawka), which guards the caravan, would be yours. The shawka (thorn, spike; here, "strength") is something defined at its tip, which penetrates easily beyond other things. You find the thorn sharp and fine at its point, and then its width increases from its base so that its thickness is proportionate to the base, so that it penetrates with force. Dhāt al-shawka means the strong group that reaches its intended target, and no aim is beyond its reach; for this reason one says "shākī al-silāḥ" (armed, literally "possessing the weapon's point"). So if you wished and desired to avoid meeting the army of the disbelievers in battle, the Mighty and Majestic Lord says to you: ﴿But Allah wills to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the last of the disbelievers﴾.

That is, Allah, exalted is He, wills to support Islam with a small, weak force, without equipment, against a strong army, so that they will know that our Lord is their supporter; and thereby the truth is established by His words, that is, by His promise. There is the word of Allah in which He said:

﴿And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit the eastern and western parts of the land, which We had blessed; and the fair word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel﴾ (part of verse 7:137).

Thus was the promise of Allah fulfilled. ﴿And to cut off the last of the disbelievers﴾: al-dābir and al-dubur mean the remainder, the last; and one says "qaṭa'tu dābirahu," meaning I left him no descendant.

Then He, glorified and exalted, says after that:

﴿That He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood, even though the criminals dislike it.﴾ (8:8)

We note that He, glorified and exalted, had said earlier "and Allah wills to establish the truth by His words," and here He says "that He might establish the truth." The truth meant in the first instance is the granting of victory to the small group, the weak few, over the strong many. This is the first truth which the Real promised by His words, so that the whole method of Islam may be established, even though the criminals dislike it.

The Exalted Lord then says:

﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ (8:9)

The root **استغاث** (istaghatha) indicates seeking relief (ghawth), just as **استسقى** (istasqa) means seeking water (saqya) and **استفهم** (istafhama) means seeking understanding (fahm). The **ألف** (alif), **السين** (sin) and **التاء** (ta) in these forms indicate the sense of seeking. **استغاث** means to seek relief from a strong one who is able to give relief. Its origin is from **الغيث** (al-ghayth), which is rain. When the land is parched because no rain falls and people cannot find water, they are said to have sought relief. Because water is the origin of life, the word was used for everything that provides relief, which is the sustaining of life. In war, fighters may perish, so they seek relief from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿when you sought help from your Lord﴾.

The phrase **تستغيثون ربكم** ("you seek help from your Lord") uses the plural pronoun, as though they all sought help together at one time. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also sought help when the people had lined up for battle. Abu Jahl had said: "O Allah, grant victory to the one of us who is more upright in the truth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raised his hands, faced the qibla and said: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You have promised me. O Allah, bring me what You have promised me. O Allah, if this small band of the people of Islam is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on the earth." (1)

The words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) show that he was seeking help from the Creator who had promised victory. The people behind him responded: "Amin." Anyone who says "Amin" to a supplication made by an imam or a leader is, by this saying, as though he were making the supplication just as the imam or leader does. Whoever says "Amin" is one of those who supplicate with the same supplication. The Exalted Lord also said:

﴿And Moses said: "Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment."﴾ (10:88) (Surah Yunus), and this is what the Noble Qur'an related on the tongue of Moses (peace be upon him).

Then the Exalted Lord says after it: ﴿Your supplication has been answered, so go both of you straight﴾ (from 10:89). Although it was Sayyidna Moses (peace be upon him) who made the supplication, His saying afterwards, "Your supplication has been answered," is evidence that Moses supplicated and Aaron said "Amin," so Aaron became a supplicant like his brother Moses.

﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you﴾ (from 8:9).

In ﴿فاستجاب لكم﴾ ("and He answered you"), the **ألف** (alif), **السين** (sin) and **التاء** (ta), as we have learned, indicate seeking. The Exalted Lord's words **فاستجاب** ("and He answered") mean that He asked the soldiers of truth on earth to be with Muhammad and his companions. This is because Allah, the Exalted, created the universe and created within it causes. We see the causes as apparent, and behind them are hidden powers of the angels. The angels are Allah's hidden creation, which we do not see or perceive, except that Allah has informed us that He has angels.

The angels are not among the created beings visible to us. Rather, our faith in Allah and our affirmation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in conveying from Allah, the Exalted, have made us know that He, the Exalted, created the angels. He also informed us that He created the jinn, and we affirmed that. So the proof of our faith in the existence of angels and jinn is the report of the truthful Messenger, who conveys from Allah, the Exalted. As for the one whose intellect stops before this matter and asks: "How can a thing exist and not be seen?" we say to him: "These are reports from Allah." There are some who denied the existence of the angels and jinn and said: "They are the mechanical forces within causes." They did not consider that when the Exalted Lord speaks of an unseen matter, He, the Exalted, leaves in the scenes of His existence and His universe something that brings this unseen matter closer to the mind, so that you do not know the existence of things whose effects you feel. Then, with the passing of time, you come to know their existence. These things were not created when you discovered them; rather they were already present, but you had not recognized them. There is a difference between the existence of a thing and the perception of its existence. An example of this is the discovery of the microbe in the seventeenth century. It existed before it was discovered, and it used to enter people's bodies and pass through the skin. When they discovered it, this showed that it had existed, but we did not have the instruments to perceive it. So if you are told that Allah has a creation that exists even though you do not perceive it, then take from what you have perceived after you were not perceiving it as evidence of affirmation of what you do not perceive.

The Exalted Lord informed us of the existence of the angels, and everything has angels that manage it. They are "those who manage affairs" (al-mudabbirat amran) and the guardian angels. The Exalted also said:

﴿For him are successive angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah.﴾ (13:11) (from Surah al-Ra'd).

He, the Exalted, also said:

﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer ready.﴾ (50:18) (Surah Qaf)

These angels are entrusted with the affairs of man on earth. The rain, for example, has its angel; the crops, for example, have their angel; and everything has its angel. This is a hidden cause, not seen, which moves the thing. ﴿So He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels."﴾

**الإمداد** (al-imdad) is the reinforcement that comes to an army, because when an army faces battles that the existing number of men or equipment cannot handle, the army's commander asks for reinforcements of men and supplies. ﴿I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another.﴾

We know that when our Lord commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, the command did not apply to every kind of angel. Rather, the command was issued to the angels entrusted with the affairs of the earth. As for the angels not entrusted with this, they were not included in this matter. That is why we say that when the Exalted Lord rebuked Iblis, He said to him:

﴿Have you grown arrogant, or were you of the exalted?﴾ (from 38:75) (Surah Sad). What is meant by **العالين** (al-'alin, "the exalted") is the angels who were not included in the command to prostrate.

In this verse, the Blessed and Exalted Lord explains that He reinforced the fighting Muslims at the Battle of Badr with ﴿a thousand of the angels, following one another.﴾ **الردف** (al-radf) is that which comes after you. That is why it is said: "So-and-so mounted his mount and made so-and-so ride behind him," meaning he placed him behind him. **المُردِف** (al-murdif) is the one who is in front, and **المَردَف** (al-mardaf) is the one who is behind him. The verse makes clear to us that the angels were in front of the Muslims, because the army of the Muslims was small in number, while the army of the disbelievers was large in number. The angels came to increase the number of the Muslim army. If the number was a thousand fighters, Allah sent angels in the same number, and thereby the army of the believers was increased by the number of the believers. It would have been enough for Allah to send one angel, as the narrations recount concerning the people of Lut. It is reported that Jibril (peace be upon him) placed one of his wings beneath the cities of the people of Lut, lifted them up to the sky until the people of heaven heard the braying of donkeys, the barking of dogs and the crowing of roosters, and no jar of theirs was overturned and no vessel of theirs was spilled. Then he overturned them all at once and struck them on the ground.

A single cry shook the people of Thamud. Why, then, did the Blessed and Exalted Lord send here a thousand angels? It happened to increase the number before the enemy, and to be of benefit in two matters. The first matter: that the enemy would be seized with dread. The second matter: that the believers would gain strength. But did the angels have any action in this matter, or did they have no action? Here a difference of opinion arose.

1 Narrated by Muslim from Umar ibn al-Khattab.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 8, verse 10:

We find that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿And Allah made it not but as good tidings and so that your hearts might be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (8:10)

That is: the angels are a glad tiding for you, and you are the ones who fight your enemies. And He, glorified and exalted, is the One who said:

﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people.﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 9:14)

The Truth, glorified be He, said this to the believers as they were entering their first battle and facing their first armed encounter between them and the disbelievers, because if they knew that the angels would fight and take part, they might grow lax in fighting and enter the war with unprepared hearts and without zeal. So our Lord made clear: I made the entry of the angels a glad tiding for you, and "so that your hearts might be assured thereby." That is, the number of the angels corresponds to the number of the disbelievers' army, and the increase in number is you, O you who went out to fight. And know that the angels are for the reassurance of hearts. But the Truth wants to punish them by your hands, because Allah wants to instill awe for this particular group, such that people will reckon a thousand reckonings for it.

The narrations differ regarding the role of the angels in the Battle of Badr. We find Abu Jahl saying to Ibn Mas'ud: "What are these voices I hear in the battle?" There were indeed voices that terrified the disbelievers at the Battle of Badr. Ibn Mas'ud replied to Abu Jahl: "They are the voices of the angels." He said: "Then it is by the angels that you prevail, not by yourselves."

So beware lest you be tempted even by the angels, for victory is neither from you nor from the angels, but victory is from Me, because the one whom you want to support you must be one whose ability to support you you are certain of. Humans with humans assume victory before the war, and it is possible that the other side will prevail; but true victory comes from the One who is never overcome, and He is Allah, glorified and exalted: ﴿And victory is not except from Allah.﴾

When you seek the help of someone to support you against your enemy, that one whom you seek help from, if he is of your kind, may prevail with you, and it may be that you and he are both defeated; but you enter the war supposing that you will prevail with the one who supports you, and defeat may befall you both together. As for the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, He alone is the One who is not overcome and is not defeated. ﴿And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾

He, glorified and exalted, is the Supporter. Thus is the believer who fights with the zeal of faith, confident of victory. But beware lest you think that Allah's victory issues from no wisdom. Behind Allah's victory for the believers there is wisdom; if you are negligent in any matter, victory will be taken from you, for Allah does not change His ways with His creation. We have seen what happened at the Battle of Uhud when they faltered and did not carry out the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they did not triumph, for wisdom required that they not triumph. Had Allah given them victory, they would afterwards have made light of the commands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and some of them would have said: "We disobeyed him and we won." Thus we find that obedience to Allah and the Messenger and taking the means are an important matter. When the command came from the Messenger of Allah at the Battle of Uhud, with the meaning: "O archers, do not leave your positions, even if you see us being routed toward Madinah; you have no concern with us, and each of you must take up his role and duty. If he sees a brother of his in his station routed, he has no concern with him, and every fighter must carry out what is incumbent upon him." But they disobeyed, so Allah took victory from them. Thus it becomes certain to them that victory is from Allah, the Mighty who is not overcome.

Al-Bukhari narrated from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "We met the polytheists that day, and the Prophet ﷺ had seated a force of archers and appointed over them 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Do not leave your place, even if you see us prevailing over them; and if you see them prevailing over us, do not come to our aid.'" (1)

We note that the reinforcement by angels is mentioned once as a thousand and once as three thousand, in the words of the Truth, glorified be He:

﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:124)

So if three thousand does not suffice you, Allah will increase the number, therefore the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says:

﴿Yes, if you are patient and mindful of Allah, and they come upon you suddenly from this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:125)

So the reinforcement is proportionate to the condition of the believers, and His words, glorified be He, show this: ﴿Yes, if you are patient and mindful of Allah.﴾

Patience alone, then, is not enough; there must also be the fear of Allah, and there must likewise be steadfastness (muṣābara) in outlasting the enemy in patience. Therefore the Lord, blessed and exalted, says elsewhere: ﴿Be patient and vie in patience.﴾ (3:200), because the enemy may also possess the quality of patience; so Allah increases the patient one. If the enemy is patient in something, then you, O believer, must be more patient than him.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the reinforcement by angels a glad tiding, to reassure hearts and as confidence that the victory is from Allah, the Exalted:

﴿And Allah made it not but as good tidings and so that your hearts might be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (Verse 10 of Surah al-Anfal)

As soon as the battle began, there followed a succession of blessings that would bring victory: reinforcement by angels, a glad tiding to assure the hearts, and confidence that victory is from Allah, the Mighty and Wise.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 8, verse 11:

Then comes the reminder of the evidence for this, and the Lord, glory be to Him, says:

﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him, and sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it, and to remove from you the defilement of Satan, and to strengthen your hearts and make your feet firm thereby.﴾ (8:11)

The nu'as (drowsiness) is the first light sleep that seizes a person when he wants to sleep. The common people in Egypt call it "ta'sīla," and they say, "So-and-so is mu'assal," meaning drowsiness has taken him. It is not sleep itself but a slackening of the nerves that is followed by sleep. This is among the signs of God, the Exalted, in that He grants a person temporary rest that is not sleep. And He, glory be to Him, says of His exalted Essence:

﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾ (2:255), meaning that He, exalted and high is He, is not seized by light sleep nor by deep sleep. For drowsiness is an insistence from the body to seek sleep, and it is a light sleep. And He, glory be to Him, is not like anything; He, mighty and majestic, does not take on a body or form in anything. Neither drowsiness seizes Him nor sleep approaches Him. We observe that when a person is spoken to while drowsiness has taken him, he wakes and becomes alert, whereas one who is in deep sleep may not wake. So drowsiness is, then, the light call to rest, while sleep is the heavy call. Here God sent down drowsiness upon them as a prelude to sleep, so that they might rest a little.

We know that sleep is one of the signs of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in His creation. For the body, when it expresses itself through movement and energy, eats food, drinks water and breathes air, all of this is converted into energy, then into fuel for movement. This energy is formed through the interaction of various elements: the assimilation of food and the transformation of food into different kinds so that each cell of the body is nourished with what suits it, then the extraction of "oxygen" through breathing and the expulsion of carbon dioxide, and tens of thousands of chemical reactions in which no waste is left to be expelled, unlike other reactions from which waste exits by one of the two passages, or from the ear canal or otherwise.

Such waste comes out of the combustions that we call "exhaust" in mechanical machines. Exhaust is the result of combustion, gases that are separated off so that movement can proceed. In the human being we find exhaust represented in feces, what comes out of the ear canal, "eye discharge," and sweat; all of these are exhausts. But there is a kind of this chemical composition that produces energy and has no exhaust.

The basic means of restoring the proper chemical balance for a human being is to rest the body, so that the body's substances interact with themselves and return to their natural state. This only happens through sleep. Therefore, when a person stays up late for a long time and then goes to sleep, he feels his legs have become "numb" (khadilat), or as it is said, "pins and needles" (namilat). This is the result of the body's substances being unable to perform the reactions that wakefulness requires. All of these are involuntary matters, as evidenced by the fact that a person sometimes wishes to sleep and sometimes tries to trick himself into sleep but it does not come, because sleep is one of the processes specific to the Truth, glory be to Him, and it is one of the signs of God in this universe, and among the wondrous signs. Read the word of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen﴾ (30:23).

When scholars who researched the phenomenon of sleep tried to explain it, they proposed dozens of theories. Among the most recent experiments conducted, they brought a person, suspended him like a lever from his middle, as if he were a stick lifted from its center in balance, and made each half equal in weight. When sleep came upon this person under test, they found that one side tilted, as if some weight had come to it from the other half, so its mass increased. This is the latest they have studied about sleep. This experiment proved that sleep is one of the wonders that deserve the Truth, blessed and exalted, to say of it: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.﴾

Look at the word "and by day," and you will see the reserve contained in the verse about sleep, for He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night﴾.

In this statement there is a reserve for whoever, in some circumstance, does not sleep at night, so that this is compensated and he sleeps by day. It is among God's wisdom that He concluded this verse with His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.﴾

This is because sleep suspends all the body's powers: when a person sleeps, his body cannot move by voluntary movement, except for hearing, which remains in its function, because by it one is summoned. The eye, for example, does not see during sleep, but the ear hears and never abandons hearing at all, because by the ear summoning takes place. If a father calls his son while he is sleeping, he hears the call. That is why we said earlier that when God willed to make the People of the Cave sleep for three hundred years and nine more, He said:

﴿So We struck upon their ears in the cave for a number of years﴾ (18:11).

For if the hearing of the People of the Cave had not been struck, hearing would have remained, and then the storms, the howling of wolves and the roaring of lions would have stirred them, and they would not have been able to sleep throughout this period.

And here, in the verse whose reflections we are now discussing: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾ (8:11).

A question may come to mind: is there drowsiness other than as a security? The answer is yes, because mere rest from fatigue so that one becomes active afterward is also drowsiness. This teaches us that "security" came for a particular task, which is to calm the depths of the believers amid the agitating circumstances surrounding them. Here is an enemy of great number, while they are without equipment; therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, willed not to waste the energy needed for the confrontation, nor to let that energy be dissipated in thought. So He made their drowsiness a specific drowsiness that overcame them, namely "the drowsiness of security," and the Lord, mighty and majestic, made this drowsiness a sign, since it came upon them all together. This alone is one of His signs, glory be to Him. Had deep sleep overcome them, the enemies would have fallen upon them in a single onslaught, but they took some rest in which there was some wakefulness. ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness﴾.

Here "drowsiness" is the object, and it is a security from God. And He, glory be to Him, says in another verse:

﴿Then He sent down upon you after grief a security, drowsiness overtaking a group of you﴾ (3:154).

In the verse of al-Anfal there is "drowsiness" and "security," while in the verse of Al 'Imran it is "security" and "drowsiness," because the two situations differ. The verse of Al 'Imran shows that drowsiness overtook one group of the fighters at the Battle of Uhud after grief had afflicted them in that battle, and these were the sincere believers gathered around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In Surat al-Anfal, however, the verse shows that drowsiness overtook the whole army, since all were of one heart and faith filled their hearts entirely, with no hypocrite or doubter among them. So this security by drowsiness covered them all, because it removes fear and is one of the evidences of safety, tranquility, and trust in God's victory.
