The Truth, blessed and exalted, goes on in the same verse, saying:

﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it and remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾ (8:11).

The meaning of purification is that there was an event from which purification was required, and they found no water with which to purify themselves, for they found no water to purify themselves with, since the polytheists had at first gained control over the water, so the Muslims were thirsty and occupied with thirst and with the desire to purify their bodies. This shows that the believer must remain clean even while in battle, for if one of them remained a day or two without bathing, no one would have blamed him for that. This statement came to show the believer's concern for cleanliness if any discharge or sweat came out, or it was purification from the defilement of Satan, because Satan imagined to them sexual dreams and began to whisper, saying to them: "You claim that you are upon the truth; how can you pray while you are in a state of major impurity?" The mere occurrence of this matter to all of them was another sign among the signs. So God enraged Satan and sent down water upon them that they might drink and purify themselves.

The Lord, glory be to Him, says in the same verse: ﴿And that He may strengthen your hearts and make your feet firm thereby.﴾

The Truth, blessed and exalted, willed to reassure the believers so that their feelings would not be scattered or dispersed. As soon as the rain fell, they dug pits so the water would gather in them; thus He, glory be to Him, protected them from lack of water. Moreover, the falling of rain on sandy ground is a great blessing from another standpoint, since it binds the sand to the earth so that it raises no dust. We know that when a person walks on the ground, his weight tramples what is beneath him, to a degree that corresponds to his weight. When a small child walks on sand, the trace of his walking is slight, unlike a large man; and if you measure it against the weight of a boy or lad, and against the weight of a full-grown man, you will find that the earth has sunk in proportion to the mass that has come upon it. When people walk without any work and intend only to walk, the weight is light; but when men enter war, the feet may sink into the sand, and a part of a fighter's body may be rendered unable to move, because it is the foot that achieves balance.

This is from God's wisdom, and we see it in our own lives. We find the people of the countryside placing over water channels a palm trunk or a plank of wood so that a person may walk across it between the two banks. If the walker thinks about this matter, he may fall into the water; but if he leaves his legs to walk spontaneously, he walks achieving balance. Something similar happens in the making of house stairs: we find their steps equal in height so that a person climbs steadily without thinking; if one step is off, its height differing from the rest, the balance is disturbed and the person falls, because the leg has automatically adjusted itself to this arrangement.

For this reason, climbing spiral staircases is tiring, because spiral staircases have one side wide and another narrow. A person may become confused while climbing. For these reasons, armies medically examine recruits, and they select only the person with straight feet, so that his feet can bear all conditions and he can face unusual circumstances. And among the greatness of the Creator, glory be to Him, is that He made each organ have its own specific characteristics.

He, glory be to Him, concludes this verse with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And make your feet firm thereby.﴾

The firming of the feet is, on one hand, a moral matter; on the other hand, the firming of the feet means "that the falling of rain made the earth firm," so that it does not raise dust or sand. And He, glory be to Him, is the One who says in another context:

﴿And how many a prophet fought, with him many devoted followers. They did not weaken for what befell them in the way of God, nor did they falter, nor did they submit. And God loves the steadfast. And their words were only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people."﴾ (3:146–147)

Thus we understand that the firming of the feet has multiple aspects, sensory and moral.

The Truthful One, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, so strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them."﴾

Here the Lord, glorified be He, explains that He inspired the angels through *ilham* (inspiration, divine insertion into the heart): "I am with you, with victory and support," ﴿so strengthen those who believe﴾.

That is, strengthen the resolve of the believers and make their hearts firm. In other words, make their hearts as if they were bound fast, so that they fear no change from their enemy. And for the believers the clarification is increased: beware lest you think that the multitude of numbers or the strength of equipment is what produces victory. Rather, victory is always from God, exalted be He, who says:

﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by God's permission﴾ (Qur'an 2:249).

This is because the ratio between the believers and the disbelievers is unbalanced and needs a great reinforcement from God, exalted be He. We have said that heaven intervenes when the matter is beyond the means of creation, and for this reason He, glorified be He, says:

﴿Or who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him﴾ (Qur'an 27:62).

If someone says, "I call upon God more than once and He does not answer me," we respond to him and say: you did not make the supplication of the distressed one (*al-mudtarr*), but rather you made the supplication of the pampered (*al-mutraf*). It is like one who lives in an apartment praying that God grant him a small palace, or one who walks on his feet and is carried by a work vehicle asking for a private car, or one who owns a "television" asking that God give him a "video" device. All of these are not a supplication of necessity, because the distressed one is the one who has lost his means.

The Truth continues the speech in the same verse:

﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, so strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them﴾ (Qur'an 8:12).

When God, mighty and majestic, casts fear and dread into the hearts of the enemy, whatever his number and whatever his equipment, this enemy will leave everything he has and flee from the state of terror and panic. Some of the disbelievers have indeed done this. God, glorified be He, has bestowed favour upon the believers by reinforcing them with angels as good news and reassurance, and He prepared water for them, purified them, and removed from them the defilement of Satan. All of these are the preliminaries of the battle, completed on the part of the Truth, blessed and exalted, as reinforcement for you. Nothing is required of you, O believers, except that you turn to the battle with a sincere resolve, the resolve of the brave warrior who has the intellect to think and to plan in arrangement, in attack and in retreat.

The instruments of combat in the past were swords, spears and arrows, and the fighter needed his head to plan with, and his hands and fingers to grip the sword. For this reason the Truth alerts the believers to these two influential points, saying: ﴿so strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them﴾. Striking above the necks means striking the head, so that he loses the capacity to think, or his life is taken and he ends; and if he remains alive he will witness the slaughter and humiliation of his comrades. Striking every fingertip of them means striking them with swords in their hands, because striking the hands wounds them and renders them incapable of fighting.

Why? The Truth answers in the following verse:

﴿That is because they opposed God and His Messenger; and whoever opposes God and His Messenger, indeed God is severe in punishment﴾ (Qur'an 8:13).

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, makes clear that this decisive victory for the Prophet and his companions, and the defeat of the polytheists, is because they opposed (shāqqū) God and His Messenger. "Shāqqū" comes from "al-shaqq" (splitting), and its meaning is that you divide one thing into two. It was incumbent upon the human being among them to accept the method of God, which organised his movement in this universe, and there was no reason to dissipate energy by splitting into two groups: a group with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and a group with disbelief and polytheism. This is because the energy that was prepared for setting right the affairs of humanity and the universe, for the sake of the caliphate (khilāfah, vicegerency), is partly squandered in wars between truth and falsehood. Had the wars ceased, all of human energy would have been directed toward reform, progress, advancement, and the realisation of good for the children of Adam. But they opposed God and His Messenger, so they placed themselves on a side facing the side of those who believe in God and the Messenger. Therefore they deserved the punishment and retribution of God, and because they opposed God and His Messenger, it is incumbent upon them to bear severe punishment from God. So He, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Whoever opposes God and His Messenger, indeed God is severe in retribution﴾ (part of verse 13, Surah al-Anfal). This is a general matter and a sunnah (established way) of God in His universe, encompassing those who opposed God and His Messenger from the beginning of the message until the Hour is established.

Almighty Allah says next:

﴿That is [your due], so taste it; and that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire (14)﴾:

"That" refers to what happened at the Battle of Badr: the believers striking the disbelievers above the necks and striking every fingertip of them. Indeed, our Lord is severe in punishment, and this is what the disbelievers were bound to taste. Dhawq (tasting) is the sensing of food or drink, whether liquid or solid, but it extends beyond anything sensed by taste even when it is not food or drink. Our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says:

﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble (49)﴾ (Surat al-Dukhan). That is: taste the humiliation and abasement, [even though it is] not something eaten or drunk, but [something] perceived. For the tasting of food is the apparent sense in a person; he may find by tasting that it is pungent, sweet, rough, smooth, and so on.

Here the Truth (al-Haqq) gives us an example to generalize a matter, saying, Mighty and Majestic:

{And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and at rest, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the favors of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do (112)} (Surat al-Nahl).

Hunger is the removal of food, so how can hunger be made to be tasted? Hunger is not something tasted, nor is clothing something tasted. From the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted, we understand that idhaqa (making to taste) is the intense sensing of what is eaten, and clothing, as we know, covers the whole body. So it is as if the tasting envelops the whole body: the fingertips taste, the chest tastes, the neck tastes, and it is as if hunger has come to encompass the entire human being. Here the Lord, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿That, so taste it.﴾

Tasting is other than swallowing and being satisfied. We see this in our commercial and trading world: when you buy, for example, a guava, or unripe dates, or figs, the seller tells you, "It is a sweet fruit, taste some of it," and he does not tell you, "Eat each of them and be full." He only asks you to try the taste of the fruit, and then you buy to eat afterward according to your desire and capacity. What we see in this world is merely a tasting, to which the rustic proverb applies: "On my tongue, and do not forget me." The punishment the disbelievers witnessed at the hands of the believers is merely a very slight taste compared with what they will see in the Hereafter of severe punishment and painful torment. Satiety from punishment will come in the Hereafter. Why? ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger, and whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾. This kind of tasting of humiliation and disgrace in this world for these obstinate disbelievers is merely a simple example of the severity of Allah's punishment for disbelief. On the Day of Resurrection the clear law stated in His saying, Glorified and Exalted, will apply to them: ﴿And that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire.﴾

Thus the defeat of the camp of disbelief and their abasement is merely a light sample of what will happen to them on the Day of Resurrection of painful torment. The Truth, Glorified and Exalted, is the One who says:

﴿And indeed, for those who did wrong there is a punishment besides that﴾ (part of verse 47, Surat al-Tur).

The punishment of the Hereafter will be terrifying. "Adhab" (punishment) is the causing of pain to the sense; if you wish to make its pain continue, keep in it the instrument of sensing pain. That is why you find the Truth, Glorified and Exalted, when He speaks of Sulayman and the hoopoe, says:

﴿And he inspected the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or was he among the absent? I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority."﴾ (Surat al-Naml, 20–21).

It is as if slaughter ends the punishment, as is evident from the fact that the counterpart of punishment in this situation is slaughter. And what of the punishment of the Fire? The fire known in our lives burns whatever is put into it, but the Fire of the Hereafter differs greatly, because the Truth says:

﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ (part of verse 56, Surat al-Nisa').

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing [in battle], do not turn your backs to them [in retreat].﴾ (8:15)

We know that Allah's address to the believers with His words ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is either followed by a command concerning what faith requires and demands, or followed by faith itself. An example of this is Allah's words: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ (4:136). Some people ask: how can He address them as believers and then say to them, "Believe"? Those who raise this question have not noticed that when Allah addresses the believers, He knows that they are believers in fact, but changeable circumstances in choice may lead some of them to slacken in what faith requires. The second "believe" means: renew your faith constantly, that is, continuous faith that connects present faith with future faith, so that faith may remain with you.

If what follows ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is a command to what faith requires, such as a legal ruling or a moral admonition, then its command is binding, and the meaning is: O you who have believed in Me as a powerful, wise God, trust in everything I command you, for I do not command you to anything that benefits Me, because the attributes of perfection belong to Me eternally; My creating you has not produced any attribute of perfection. If I obligate you to something, then My obligation returns to you with benefit and advantage. Let us give an example, and to Allah belongs the highest example, exalted above every comparison: you go to the doctor after consulting your family and colleagues, and you are confident that this is the doctor who will benefit you in the condition you complain of. When you go to him, he diagnoses the illness for you and writes the medicine for you. Whether you use the medicine or not, you are free, and its effect returns to you; your not using the medicine will not harm the doctor at all, rather it is you who harm yourself. Likewise is the method of Allah, which He made for the soundness of the movement of life. If you follow it and apply it, you benefit yourself, and if you leave it and do not apply it, you will harm yourself. Therefore the Lord, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve."﴾ (18:29)

So the choice is yours, and Allah, glorified and exalted, created you, and created the universe that serves you before you existed. You are a newcomer to this universe, a newcomer to the sun, the moon, the earth, the mountains, the water, and everything in this existence. He who created what preceded you must have absolute attributes of perfection. Glorified and exalted is He: He created everything with wisdom and order, and since He, glorified and exalted, possesses comprehensive absolute attributes of perfection, He does not require of you through obligations that you produce for Him a new attribute of perfection, and He is free of need of you. If you are convinced of faith, it is for your own benefit, and He has obligated you only with the rulings that correct your condition. The rationale (haythiyyah) of every ruling is its being introduced with ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Beware of seeking a cause (ʿillah) for the ruling, because if you go to the ruling seeking its cause, you will share with non-believers. The believer, for example, when he heard of the command to avoid wine, complied with the ruling because it came from Allah. Afterwards, non-believers came to know, through scientific analysis, that wine is harmful, so they abstained from it. Is their abstention a faithful abstention? No.

Therefore the believer takes the command from Almighty Allah not for the cause of the command but simply because it has been issued from Allah, so he complies with the command and carries it out. The Muslim obeys Allah's commands and performs righteous deeds without inquiry or questioning about their cause. When it is said, for example, that among the benefits of fasting is that the rich man tastes the pain of hunger and shows compassion to the poor, I say to the one who says so: your statement is correct, because it contains a touch of understanding; but what about the fasting of the poor man who has nothing to give to others? Does he not fast too?

The believer fasts because the command has come from Allah to fast. Most of Allah's rulings come preceded by His words ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: O you who have believed in Me as God, turn to Me. If you seek the cause and then carry out the ruling for its cause, you are not believers in the Commanding and Legislating God, but you are believers in the cause of the commanded act. Allah wants you to submit to Him alone, and therefore He commands you with commands and forbids you with prohibitions. For example, when you perform Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, you greet the Black Stone by command of Allah, and circumstances may allow you to kiss this stone as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did; yet in all of that you are not submitting to the stone, but to the Supreme Commander who sent Muhammad to wage war against idols and stones. You follow the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) with complete submission and faith, and then you go on to stone the stones which are the symbol of Iblis, doing so in submission to the commands of Allah, Exalted, which have reached you from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Here Almighty Allah says:

﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing [in battle], do not turn your backs to them.﴾ (8:15)

So since you have believed in God, you must defend the way of God, because this too is for your benefit. By your faith in Allah, O believer, all of society benefits from your goodness, and He, glorified, will command you only with good. You will not steal, you will not commit adultery, you will not drink wine, you will not rampage among people, you will not take bribes, and through all this conduct society benefits, because society is harmed when there exists within it a group that is not guided. When you fight to impose the word of faith upon these people, this returns to your own benefit. Therefore your being characterized by faith is not realized unless you extend it to others. Out of love for yourself, you should extend the faith and the values you hold to others, so that you benefit from the conduct of one who believes, and others benefit from your conduct toward them. It is in your interest that everyone believes.

When Almighty Allah obligates you to jihad in the way of Allah, you do so for your own good.

﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing﴾ (8:15). "Zahfan" (advancing) is a verbal noun from zahafa. Az-zahf (advancing) originally means moving from one place to another by means of the upper half of the body. You say, "The child zahafa," meaning he moved from his place by moving his hands and drawing the rest of his body along with them, as we say "habā" (crawled), meaning he used his hips and knees to move his body over the ground. Then we say "mashā" (walked), meaning he stood on his feet and went. These are then stages beginning with zahf, then habw, then mashy. The infant begins his first movement with zahf, after he has gained control of his head and the ability to move it by his will, and strengthens his upper half, so he sits, then crawls; after that his thighs strengthen and he crawls on his knees, and after that his legs strengthen and he walks.

So the strength of the child begins from above.

But what is the matter with "zahfan" here in this noble verse? And why did He not say "harwalū" (run) to the fighting? We say: zahf is the movement of a mass in which the one moving cannot be seen, so whoever sees it thinks the whole mass is moving.

It is as if Almighty Allah means: I want you to move toward the battle as one mass, tightly joined together, so the matter appears as though you are advancing. "Zahfan" originally is "zāḥifīn" (advancing ones), but Allah, glorified and exalted, departed from the active participle and used the verbal noun, just as we say of a just person: he is justice ('adl), meaning his justice is embodied. Therefore we find the poet saying of an advancing army:

A great army (khamīs)¹ in the East and West of the earth, its advance,
and in the ears of the neighbours from it is a rumbling (zamāzim)²

The khamīs is the massive army, and the poet wishes to depict the advance as one solid, interlocked mass, such that you cannot distinguish one soldier's movement from another's, until it seems to you that the whole mass moves together. Whoever wants to confirm this, we ask Allah to grant him Hajj, and to ascend to the second floor of the Sacred Mosque in Mecca and see the circumambulators, finding them all bound together as one moving mass; that is why they call it "the flood" (as-sayl).

"Sālat bi-aʿnāq al-maṭiyy al-abāṭiḥ" (the valleys flowed with the necks of the mounts).

They are like the torrent in its flow, where no drop is distinguished from another.

Almighty Allah makes clear to us that the meeting with the disbelievers must be zahfan, that is, one solid mass, so the sight strikes the disbelievers with terror when they see this enormous mass in which no one distinguishes among its members. Thus is the true confrontation.

Almighty Allah continues the warning, saying: ﴿So do not turn your backs to them﴾ (8:15), that is, do not give them your backs. In another verse He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, for you would be [turned] into losers﴾ (5:21).

Allah wants to give a hideous image in the ears of the people, because "adbār" is the plural of "dubr," and dubr is understood as the rear, opposite to "qubul" (front). This is a warning to you not to let your enemy reach your back, that is, your rear, because this is a shameful matter. Therefore we find Imam ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, responding to those who said to him that his armour had a front covering but no back covering, meaning it covered the chest but had no back. Imam ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "May my mother be bereaved of me if I let my enemy reach my back." It is as if the Imam's nobility and bravery compelled him to leave his back without protection.

In the words of Almighty Allah, ﴿So do not turn your backs to them﴾, there is a warning against fleeing from confronting the enemy.

¹ The army was named thus because it consists of five divisions: the vanguard, the centre, the right wing, the left wing, and the rear.
² Zamāzim: plural of zamzama, which is the sound of thunder.

Al-Sha'rawi says, after this, the Most High, may He be exalted:

﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless it is a maneuver for battle or to join a company, he has indeed incurred wrath from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination. (16)﴾:

We note that in this noble verse, the Truth, glory be to Him, did not attach wrath to the one who turns his back in flight and running away from meeting the enemy. As for the one who turns his back as a stratagem, to give the enemy the impression that he is withdrawing while at that very moment he returns to the attack upon the enemy, encircling him, this is the true fighter, sincere in his faith, who outwits the enemy. Likewise, the one who turns his back in order to join a company of believers so as to renew the attack upon the enemies, so that his life is not lost without a price, this too is one who has employed his mind to inflict loss upon the enemy, because the believer always strives that his death should be in exchange for something. So if Allah promises him Paradise, should he not fight so as to strike the enemies with defeat?

The price of the believer in former times was ten unbelievers, meaning that Allah, the Exalted, granted every believer a strength that overcomes ten, in confirmation of His saying, Mighty and Majestic:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fighting. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand. (65)﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).

But Allah knew that there was weakness among the believers, so that one believer in the battle would face two unbelievers, in confirmation of His saying, the Most High:

﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast. (66)﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).

Therefore, we find that one who flees before three enemies is not called a fleer in the legal ruling. But whoever flees from facing two is considered a fleer, because the Most High said before weakness came upon us:

﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ (part of verse 65, Surat al-Anfal), meaning that the believing fighter was able to face ten unbelievers. If the opposing force is fewer than ten unbelievers, then the believer must preserve himself so that he does not die cheaply. Then the Truth, glory be to Him, made clear that weakness would afflict the believers, so He said: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred﴾ (part of verse 66, Surat al-Anfal).

Thus the ratio between believers and unbelievers moved from one to ten, to one believer against two unbelievers. This is from the mercy of Allah, the Exalted. Whoever sees himself facing more than two enemies, the Most High makes clear to him: you must join a company of believers, so that their [strength] protects you from being harmed without a price.

﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless it is a maneuver for battle or to join a company﴾ (part of verse 16, Surat al-Anfal).

We have known that the one who maneuvers for battle (mutaḥarrif li-qitāl) is the one of stratagem. We say in our expressions that run on our tongues in daily life: "So-and-so is ḥarīf," meaning that no matter overcomes him and he devises ruses against it. Thus is the maneuverer in battle, who plots against the unbelievers and devises things for them, so they think they have been defeated, while in reality they are preludes to victory. As for His saying, glory be to Him: "or joining a company" (muta­ḥayyiz), it is derived from ḥayyiz, which is the place occupied by a body. Each one of us has a ḥayyiz in a place he occupies; that is, each one of us is muta­ḥayyiz. The ḥayyiz is the spatial container that holds a person, and its name is "place of location." Each of those addressed has a place, and by nature he is muta­ḥayyiz. The word muta­ḥayyiz came in this verse to direct every believing fighter to take for himself a good position that enables him to hit the target. Likewise it indicates the necessity of the fighter joining a company with his brothers in order to strengthen the confrontation with the enemy. Whoever does not do this must receive punishment from Allah, which He has explained in His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿he has indeed incurred wrath from Allah﴾ (part of verse 16, Surat al-Anfal).

"Bā'a" means "returned," and the expression of the Qur'an is suitable to what they did, because whoever gives the enemy his back is the one who turns back from the advance and the fighting. But whoever returns with the aim of tricking the enemies and maneuvering in combat, or to strengthen another group of believers, his situation is completely different: he is a supporter of the religion of Allah, unlike the withdrawing fleer who is accompanied in his withdrawal by wrath from Allah. Wrath from Allah, as we know, is one of the causes for the sending down of punishment, and for this the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿he has indeed incurred wrath from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾ (part of verse 16, Surat al-Anfal). The refuge (ma'wā) is the place to which a person retreats, and we know that when one of us wishes for rest, he retreats to the place where he finds rest and security from every harm.

The one who flees from facing the enemy in the battles of Islam will find no refuge but the Fire; indeed the Fire welcomes him, and there is a dialogue between it and the Truth, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, which the noble verse makes clear:

﴿On the day We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Are there any more?" (30)﴾ (Surat Qaf).

The Truth affirms in His noble Qur'an that the Fire rages against the unbelievers, because it is one of the soldiers of Allah, the Exalted, and subjected to carry out the command of Allah. Whoever opposed the method in this world, the Fire receives him with rage and roaring, and the unbelievers hear its raging when it sees them from afar. The Most High says:

﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring﴾ (Surat al-Furqan). And when the Fire is their refuge, is that not "wretched is the destination"?

It is as if the one who retreats from the advance and the one who flees from facing the enemies, out of fear of being killed, will go to something worse than being killed.

Then the Truth (may He be exalted) educates the believers and asks them not to be deluded by apparent causes. He says, glorified is He:

﴿So it was not you who killed them, but Allah killed them; and you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw, that He might test the believers with a good trial from Him. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ (8:17)

The words of the Truth, blessed and exalted be He: ﴿So it was not you who killed them, but Allah killed them﴾ (part of 8:17), are like His words in another verse: ﴿And victory is only from Allah﴾ (part of 3:126).

In this there is an education from the Truth to the believers. Just as victory is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for one who takes the means, so too the killing of the disbelievers was by His will, for those who disbelieved, and that slaying came about at the hand of the believer. The believer strikes with the sword, and the enemy is wounded and bleeds. But have you not seen a wounded man who did not die, and have you not seen an unwounded man who died? So the killing is from Allah.

Glory be to my Lord; when He wills, there is no averting it, and nothing escapes Him.
How many a wounded man does not die, and how many an unwounded man dies.

Thus, when the believers fought the people of disbelief, they only wounded them, while death befell them from Allah, glorified and exalted be He. ﴿So it was not you who killed them, but Allah killed them﴾ (part of 8:17). One might say: the Truth, blessed and exalted, said in another place: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ (part of 9:14).

So for the believing fighter there is the appearance of fighting, and for the Truth there is the reality of killing. For this reason, after that, He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ (part of 8:17).

In this noble statement, something unknown to them is given with something known to them, and thus the unknown is measured against the known. We have known before that when you see an event or action both negated and affirmed of someone at one time, it may appear to you that there is a contradiction in the speech. Here, for example, the Truth negates the act in His words "and you did not throw" and affirms it in His words "when you threw." Throwing is well known, and the agent is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). How, then, does He negate the action from him first and affirm it for him second?

We know that the Speaker is a Wise Lord, and His style is of the highest order. To understand this matter: we know that every act has a form upon which it stands and an aim toward which it ends. Sometimes the act exists, but its aim is not achieved, just as a father says to his son: "The examination is near, so sit in your room and study." The son sits in his room with a book in front of him, but he does not turn its pages. After an hour the father enters his son's room and says: "Bring your book so I can ask you about what you studied." The father asks his son one question, then a second, and the son does not know the answers. The father says: "You studied, and yet you did not study." That is, it is as if he did not study, rather he performed the act formally, by sitting down to study, but he did not fulfil what was incumbent upon him, because the effect of the act, which is the studying, was not achieved.

At the Battle of Badr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sought help from his Lord, implored, called upon Allah, and raised his hands, saying:

("O Lord, if this group perishes, You will not be worshipped on earth ever again." Then Jibril said to him: "Take a handful of dust and throw it in their faces.") So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a handful of dust and threw it into their faces. There was not one of the polytheists but that dust from that handful reached his eyes, nostrils and mouth, and they turned their backs in flight.(1) It is known that when a speck of dust gets into a person's eye, he becomes preoccupied with his eyes and forgets everything else.

So the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted be He: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ (part of 8:17), mean: O Messenger of Allah, you did not send with that single throw, the handful of dust, into the eyes of all the enemies, because this is a matter no one is able to do. But "when you threw," that is, you carried out Jibril's advice to you. As for reaching the eyes of the enemy, that is from the act of Allah, the Strong, the Capable.

The Almighty continues: ﴿that He might test the believers with a good trial from Him. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ (part of 8:17).

The "good trial" here is entering the battle and performing well in fighting in it.

A person errs when he thinks that trial means the descent of calamities. No, trial is testing in whatever form it takes. For the student who has studied his lessons, the examination is a good trial for him, and for the one who has not studied, the examination is a bad trial for him. So trial is not blameworthy in every respect, nor praiseworthy in every respect; rather it depends on the outcome for the person in it: whether he succeeds or not.

So that we know the Qur'an explains itself, let us read the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted be He:

﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial﴾ (part of 21:35).

So good is a trial, and when you use good in the service of Allah's way and are not arrogant because of it, and when you are patient with evil and do not rebel against the decree of Allah, all of this is a test from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, says:

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by honouring him and bestowing favours, he says, "My Lord has honoured me"﴾ (89:15), and this is testing with good. As for testing with evil, the Truth, glorified be He, says about it:

﴿But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me"﴾ (89:16).

Testing with good or with evil is merely a trial, and a trial, as we have explained, is not blameworthy in every respect, nor praiseworthy in every respect, nor praiseworthy in every respect, but it is blamed or praised according to the aim that the one tested, or whoever goes through the test, reaches. If he succeeds, it is a good trial; if he fails, it is a bad trial.

We notice, for example, that the student who focused his thought and time, restrained himself, and exerted his energy in learning and studying throughout the school year, when he enters the examination, tries to avenge the fatigue he endured in acquiring and mastering the material. So he answers the questions precisely, and each time he finishes answering a question correctly, he feels some relief. If a classmate tries to distract him, he repels him and does not turn to him, and may even call the invigilator to his aid.

The believer who shares with the believers in the good trial is like the student who performs his duty with sincerity.

He who hears the whisper of every believer and sees his deed is the Truth, glorified be He. For this reason, after speaking of the good trial, He says: ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ (part of 8:17).

So Allah, glorified and exalted be He, hears what you speak aloud and knows what you conceal in your breasts. He, exalted and majestic, knows who fights by the strength of faith, and who is mixed with the desire that others see his skill in fighting so that they will praise this skill. No one is able to deceive Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

(1) Narrated by al-Tabari, al-Qurtubi and Ibn Kathir.

That is, the matter was as described. And Allah, glorified and exalted, here tells us that He weakens the schemes of the disbelievers.

(Quran 8:18) "That is so, and that Allah weakens the schemes of the disbelievers."

And "dhalikum" (that) is an indication that the matter was so. Here, glorified and exalted is He, informs us that He weakens the schemes of the disbelievers, meaning He diminishes this scheming. One may ask: Why does He not forbid them? And why does He weaken only disbelief? We say: weakening disbelief stirs up faith and makes the believers love faith when they see the effects of disbelief, which corrupt the earth, being diminished. Also, zeal for faith increases when Islam is attacked by its adversaries. Thus, the continuation of disbelief is a form of preserving faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 19:

Then He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has certainly come to you; and if you desist, it is better for you; and if you return, We will return; and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is; and indeed Allah is with the believers.﴾ (19)

"Tastaftihu" (تستفتحوا) derives from al-istiftah (الاستفتاح), which is the seeking of a fath (فتح, opening, victory, or decision). This is because the alif, sin and ta' (the prefix "ist-") come to mean seeking. Thus we say: istafhama (استفهم), meaning he sought understanding (طلب الفهم). So "in tastaftihu" means "if you seek an opening/decision."

We know that abstract meanings (المعنويات) are all derived from concrete sensory matters (الأمر الحسّي), because a person's first familiarity with knowledge came from sensory matters, and then rational knowledge (المعلومات العقلية) forms in him. An example is our saying: "Fire burns." We knew this statement from a sensory experience that passed through more than one person, and then it became a rational proposition that a person knows even if he has not seen a fire and has not seen burning.

When sensory perceptions (المحسات) accumulate, there form in a person moral leavens (خمائر معنوية) and universal propositions (قضايا كلية) by which he manages his general affairs. An example: we all know that the diligent person succeeds, and we took this truth from reality, just as we took the truth that both the negligent and the careless fail.

And the Exalted directs our attention to this, saying:

﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing﴾ (Qur'an 16:78). That is, each of us is created with a blank mind (خالي الذهن), and an empty mind seeks to be filled, and every piece of information that the young mind receives it can recall immediately. That is why we find the young pupil more able to memorize the Noble Qur'an than the grown young man, because that grown man's mind may be crowded with rational knowledge.

The psychologists have explained this matter when they said: every feeling has a focus (بؤرة), which is the center of consciousness. The matter you are thinking about, you find its specific information in your mind immediately. This information may be displaced from your memory if you think about another subject, just as the information of the previous subject shifts to the edge of consciousness (حافة الشعور) to be replaced by the information of the new subject at the focus of consciousness.

Space (الحيز) in abstract matters is like space in sensory matters. When you fill a bottle with water, the mouth of the bottle must be wide enough for the water to enter and the air inside the bottle to exit. But if the mouth of the bottle is narrow, like the mouth of a perfume bottle for example, it is difficult to fill it with water except by means of a tool with a thin tip, like a medical syringe, so that the water can enter and the air inside the narrow-mouthed bottle can be expelled.

Thus we see that space in sensible things does not hold two quantities of different qualities, and the volume of each of them equals the volume of the space. The matter in the brain comes close to this as well: you do not remember the information of a specific subject unless the subject is at the center of consciousness; if the subject moves away from your thinking, its information recedes to the distant periphery of consciousness. A small child has an empty mind, so he receives information quickly and has it readily available.

Therefore we must not accuse one person of stupidity and another of intelligence merely because one has the ability for quick recall and the other is unable to keep pace with his companion in that, for intelligence has multiple measures about which scholars still disagree until now. But on the subject of memory, a large part of scholars have agreed that the mind, like a camera, takes the information from the first snapshot, provided that the focus of consciousness is free for this information. As for when the focus of consciousness is occupied with another matter, it does not capture the information. And the Truth, the Exalted, is the One who says:

﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you may give thanks﴾ (Qur'an 16:78).

Hearing and sight are the principal senses; we take sensory perceptions through them and form from them rational information.

And the Blessed and Exalted here says:

﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has certainly come to you; and if you desist, it is better for you; and if you return, We will return; and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is; and indeed Allah is with the believers.﴾ (Qur'an 8:19)

The word fath (الفتح) has multiple applications, among them the concrete, such as opening a door or opening a bag, meaning removing the closure of something that protects something, like the opening of a door, and the door only protects what is inside the room. The concrete opening is represented in the Noble Qur'an by the words of the Truth, the Blessed and Exalted:

﴿And when they opened their goods, they found their merchandise returned to them﴾ (Qur'an 12:65). That is, when Joseph's brothers opened the sacks (وكانت هي بديلة الحقائب, the sacks being in place of suitcases), they found the merchandise they had taken with them in order to exchange it for other goods. This is the concrete opening.

The opening may also be in abstract matters, as in opening to good and to knowledge, such as the saying of the Truth, the Blessed and Exalted:

﴿Whatever Allah opens to people of mercy, none can withhold it﴾ (Qur'an 35:2). Thus the opening of mercy is an abstract opening.

The opening may also be in judgment, because judgment occurs between parties entangled in a matter, each party claiming against the other, and the judgment comes to remove the obscurity of the matter and open it.

An example of this is what happened between our master Noah, peace be upon him, and his people. His people said:

﴿If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned﴾ (Qur'an 26:116).

What did our master Noah, peace be upon him, say?

﴿He said: My Lord, my people have denied me. So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those who are with me of the believers﴾ (Qur'an 26:117-118). That is, our master Noah, peace be upon him, asked God to decide the matter between him and his people with truth, while knowing that God was with him. Therefore he asked for deliverance for himself and for those believers with him.

And here in the noble verse about which we are reflecting, we find that fath comes in the sense of the judgment that separates the disputants, and it is indeed a judgment that separates two groups: the group of guidance, and the one calling to it, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his followers among the believers, and the group of error, who are the disbelievers of Quraysh.

Both parties sought a decision. Abu Jahl said when the two sides met: "O Allah, sever the ties of kinship for us and bring us that which we do not know, so destroy him (أحنه) in the morning" (2).

Abu Jahl thought that our master Muhammad (ﷺ) was severing their kinship and making the son leave his father and mother. Likewise, when the polytheists went out from Mecca to Badr, they took hold of the curtains of the Ka'bah and sought Allah's help, saying: "O Allah, support the higher of the two hosts, the more honourable of the two groups, and the better of the two tribes." Such was the supplication of the unbelievers.

As for the supplication of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it was his saying: "O Lord, if this band perishes, You will not be worshipped on earth ever."

The seeking of decision from both sides indicates that each of them was preoccupied with the other's matter; for if one of them were at ease and the other troubled, only the troubled one would have sought the decision.

The judgment came from Allah, the Exalted, in this matter, as the Blessed and Exalted judged that the disbelievers should be plundered, killed, and become a source of mockery from themselves and from those who see them, and they deserved that because of their disbelief, their error, their obstinacy and their opposition to the truth. What makes it likely that the opening also came from the believers is that the Truth said: ﴿then the decision has certainly come to you﴾ (Qur'an 8:19). That is, if you sought the decision and asked for separation and judgment, then the decision has come to you. This opening was in the interest of the believers, and also in the interest of the supplication of the disbelievers; it came in both respects: an opening for the believers, and in the interest of the disbelievers' supplication. You, O disbelievers, have supplicated, so either you supplicated and Allah answered your supplication, which is evil for you, and this is evidence that you are foolish in supplication; and since the decision has come, it was necessary that each party stop at the limit that occurred, and the disbelievers should be convinced that they were defeated, and the believers should be convinced that they were victorious.

﴿And if you desist, it is better for you﴾ (Qur'an 8:19).

The word "tantahu" (تنتهوا) here applies first, by its apparent meaning, to the disbelievers: that is, if you desist from opposing and hostility toward the Messenger, and from the obstinacy by which you made him an enemy, and from plotting and conspiring against him, then desisting is better for you in your worldly life, because you have seen the result: some of your chieftains were killed, others were taken captive, and spoils and booty were taken from you. If you desist from the action that caused this, it is better for you in your worldly life, and better for you also in the hereafter, if desisting would lead you to desist from contending against the religion you contend against and to become among its adherents.

The Glorified and Exalted continues His saying:

﴿And if you return, We will return; and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is﴾ (Qur'an 8:19).

And if you do not desist and return to enmity and fighting this religion, then We will return to supporting the believers. Beware of saying that you are a large company, for your company will avail you nothing against Allah. The proof of that is that you were defeated at Badr while you were numerous, possessors of number and equipment. Your multitude did not avail you, nor did your equipment avail you anything.

﴿...and your company will avail you nothing, however numerous it is; and indeed Allah is with the believers﴾ (Qur'an 8:19).

The believers were few, yet despite that they were the victors.

What has preceded refers to the speech regarding the disbelievers. But what if the speech and the seeking of decision concern the believers? In what must they desist?

They must desist from the contention and disagreement over the spoils, concerning which the Truth, the Blessed and Exalted, said:

﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾ (Qur'an 8:1).

They were compelled to ask the Messenger (ﷺ) to ask his Lord. If they return to dispute and argument among themselves, as though they were two opposing factions not united upon faith, then no group will avail another anything. You, people of faith, must know that if one group among you is strong, let the other group be humbled before it, and do not think that because of victory you have become numerous, for victory came neither from the group nor from the angels, but victory came from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

1 Ahnahu: i.e., destroy him.
2 Narrated by Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim.

Almighty Allah says next:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear [him]﴾ (8:20).

This is a clear call from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the believers, and a specific command from Him to obey Allah and the Messenger. Faith (iman) is the firm conviction of the heart in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree (al-qadar), in its good and its evil. The believers must fulfil what faith requires. What faith requires, O believers, is that you carry out the obligations that the methodology (al-manhaj) brought from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and from His informant, our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in commands and prohibitions.

We have already explained the matter of obedience: obedience to Allah is in the general command, and obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ) is in following the detailed, practical ruling that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brings for the general command. Likewise, obedience to the Messenger is obligatory in any matter or ruling, because Allah has delegated (tafwid) that to His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ (from 4:80). The delegation from Allah, glorified and exalted, to the Messenger (ﷺ) is embodied in the saying of the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from﴾ (from 59:7).

Here, in the noble verse about which we are reflecting, we find the beautiful feature of Qur'anic expression:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear [him]﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).

Al-tawalli, as we know, means turning away (al-i'rad), and the command here is not to turn away. Since you have believed, there is no turning away from what you believe in. The beautiful feature is that He, glorified be He, did not say "and do not turn away from them both" as human style would have it, but He said "and do not turn away from him" (ʿanhu). That is, He, glorified and exalted, has unified the speech over the two matters, obedience to Allah and obedience to the Messenger, and because the Messenger is a conveyor from Allah, there is no division between the two obediences, since obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, exalted be He.

Or we may say: turning away never applies to Allah, for no one is able to turn away from Allah, because He overtakes and encompasses him at any time.

Therefore we find the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted say in another verse:

﴿They swear to you by Allah that they may please you, but Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾ (Surat al-Tawba, 9:62).

In this statement He, glorified and exalted, unifies the pleasure of Allah and the pleasure of the Messenger, making it one pleasure. One of these people swears that he did not commit the act contrary to faith in order to please the believers, and to clear himself before people. But there is a higher pleasure, the pleasure of observing the application of the methodology that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed and that the Messenger (ﷺ) brought, and there is a higher Guardian (Qayyum) who watches every conduct and knows what appears and what is hidden. If we were left to one another, then any person could confront another, each with his strength; but we, in faith, know that we are under the watch of the Almighty, the Self-Subsisting. So whoever wrongs his brother, and the wronged one forgives his wrongdoer, Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Lord of the wrongdoer and the Lord of the wronged; He does not forgive the wrongdoer but calls him to account.

He, glorified and exalted, also unified in this verse between the pleasure of Allah and the pleasure of the Messenger, and did not say "and Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please them both" in the apparent style of human speech; rather He willed to unify the pleasure, because it revolves around one matter with one obedience, and around one prohibition with one abstention.

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear [him]﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).

This command to obey Allah and the Messenger is a communication from Allah, and the first means of communication is hearing (al-adhan), because hearing is the gateway to perception (al-idrakat). Therefore the Messenger conveyed the commands to people by speech, and did not convey them by writing, because not all people read. The Messenger (ﷺ) conveyed to people orally, just as he was commanded to have the Qur'an written down so that it would remain preserved.

We know that hearing is the basis of reading, and you do not read what is written, nor write what is heard, unless you know the rules and know how letters are pronounced. The teacher teaches the seeker of knowledge reading and writing through hearing first. Thus hearing takes precedence in everything, and no one in the time of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, could say: "The call did not reach me," because the call was conveyed to people by hearing. His saying "while you hear" tells us that if the call has not reached a person, he is not a subject of obligation (manat al-taklif), because our Lord, glorified and exalted, is the One who said:

﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾ (from 17:15).

Societies that live in heedlessness, who have no messenger and to whom the methodology has not been conveyed, will not be punished by Allah. This is a matter that applies now in remote distant lands far from contact with Islam and the methodology of Islam, and far from hearing about Islam, because they have heard nothing about the religion and have not known its methodology. These people are saved from punishment according to the saying of Allah, Exalted:

﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾ (from 17:15).

So the fruit of sending the Messenger is that he conveys to people. For this reason we have derived an important ruling from the saying of the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿while you hear﴾ (from 8:20).

From this statement we derive that those to whom the methodology has not been conveyed are not held to account. But is hearing enough for us to know the methodology? No, hearing alone is not enough to know that there is a messenger who came to confirm a previous messenger; rather you must search for yourself. If there is anyone on earth to whom this has not reached, he is saved. But if news of a messenger has reached him without the complete methodology reaching him, then he must search on his own, as evidence that a person seeks the least important things as soon as he hears of them, and occupies himself with searching.

Suppose a man says in a village: "The government will change the ration card." Will not every individual in the village go to ask about this matter and be concerned with it in every way? Thus, for the message to arrive, it was sufficient that a person hear of a messenger among the Arabs who had come to all people with a general message, and that this message confirms the previous messages; and whoever heard this report was obliged to treat it as he treats fundamental worldly interests. For if the matter of this world is important, how much more so the matter of the well-being of this world and the Hereafter?

Part of the responsibility for this falls upon the Muslims who did not strive to convey the methodology of Allah and the religion of Allah to others.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 21:

Then the Blessed and Exalted Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear.﴾ (8:21)

In this noble verse, al-Haqq, glorified and exalted is He, forbids us from being like those who said, "We hear," and whom God judged as not hearing. These are the ones who took hearing according to the mechanism of events occurring on the surface of movement: they heard but paid no heed. This is because the intended meaning of hearing is not merely that you hear, but that you fulfil what you have heard. If you do not fulfil what you have heard, it is as though you did not hear at all. Indeed, you become worse than one who did not hear, because the one who did not hear was never reached by the call, whereas you heard and the call reached you, but you did not respond to it and did not carry out what it demanded.

So the words of God, the Exalted,

﴿"We hear," while they do not hear﴾ (part of verse 21 of surah al-Anfal),

explain to us that this hearing on their part was nothing more than the transmission of sound from the speaker to the listener's ear through the vibration that occurs, and they did not take what they heard seriously, such that it would have a deep effect on their lives. When they are not affected by the method, it is as though they did not hear. Would that they had not heard, for they became worse than one who did not hear.

﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ (surah al-Anfal), or hearing may be meant and intended to mean acceptance, just as we say, "O God, hear the supplication of so-and-so," and you know that God is All-Hearing of supplication even if you do not say that; yet you say, "O God, hear the supplication of so-and-so," meaning "O God, accept it." Thus the intended meaning of hearing is acceptance.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 22:

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason.﴾

The word "dābba" (creature that crawls, living being) means everything that moves on the earth, but by custom it has been restricted to the four-legged animals. The plural of dābba is dawābb.

The "dawāb" (living creatures), as we know, are the third category of existence, because existence ascends in links. The first of them is the inanimate (jamād), the second is the plant (nabāt), the third is the animal (hayawān), and the fourth is the human being. These four things are joined by a single bond: the highest rank of the lower is the first rank of the higher. The lowest is the inanimate, and above it is the plant, and the highest thing in the inanimate resembles the first thing in the plant, such as coral. It is as if the inanimate itself has ascents within its own nature that stop at a certain stage beyond which it does not pass. So it does not rise until it becomes a plant, nor does the plant become an animal. No, each category remains independent in itself, and within it there are ascents that stop at a defined limit. Since the highest thing in the inanimate almost resembles the first thing in the plant, it does not turn into a plant, like the phenomenon of the growth of coral reefs, which took on the appearance of a plant but does not transfer into a plant; rather it remains the highest peak of the inanimate. Likewise the plant: we find it ascending until it reaches its highest stage. The plant has stages, and its last stage is that there exists a plant that senses, because sensation is a branch of life. This is what we see in shade plants, which we observe turning by their natural formation toward the light of day, as though there were a kind of sensation in them. If the place of the light changes, they change their direction to the new place.

There is a type of plant that wilts as soon as you touch it. We hear of a plant called in the countryside "the shy lady" (al-Sitt al-Mustahiyya), which closes its leaves over its fruit upon touch. It has taken the highest rank of the plant, and it is the first rank of the animal, yet it does not ascend into an animal; rather it remains within its link as a plant.

We come to the animals and find them ascending. There are animals that can be domesticated, and animals that cannot be domesticated but remain wild, and our Lord created them for a certain wisdom. Man domesticates the camel but cannot domesticate the serpent or the flea. It is as if God wishes by this to teach us that we did not domesticate the animals we domesticate by our own power and intelligence; rather it is He who made you become tame with them. You became familiar with the camel, and you may see a small girl leading it and commanding it to stand and sit, while a small flea may keep a person awake all night, and he does not know how to catch it. So these matters give us a wisdom that the Truth, blessed and exalted, summarized in His saying:

﴿Have they not seen that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, so that they are their owners? And We subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ (Surah Yasin, 36:71-72)

Had the Truth, blessed and exalted, not subjected these creatures, man would not have been able to subject them. We see the small creature, before which man is helpless in subjugating it, so that he knows that the one who subjugates is not man, but the one who subjugates is Allah, glorified and exalted. Among the domesticated animals you find a kind that you train in some things, so it becomes accustomed to them and performs them, such as the monkey to whom its trainer says, "Knead the dough of the young woman or the old woman," and the monkey imitates the young woman or the "old woman," because it has the capacity for imitation. It possesses a degree of understanding, and it is the highest rank of the animal, and it stops there and does not evolve beyond it. The evidence is that if you teach a monkey everything, it does what you teach it of movements, and people laugh at it, but the monkey cannot teach them to its own kind. Likewise, we find someone training a lion and a tiger to perform entertaining routines in the circus, but the lion does not teach its cubs what the circus trainer has taught it.

So existence, with its four links, inanimate, plant, animal and human, has no link in it that ascends beyond the one above it; rather each stops at a defined limit. That is the confusion that afflicted some thinkers, who supposed that the origin of man is the monkey, because creatures are links that succeed one another, and the lowest rank of the higher link of each is the highest rank of the lower, and it stops within its limits. What refutes Darwin's theory from its foundation is this understanding of the nature of evolution:

﴿And of every thing We created two mates﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 51:49), meaning that all beings are created from the beginning by Allah, and no species has arisen from another species.

We present this rational proof to non-religious people, and we say: Why did the conditions that affected the first monkey so that it became a human not affect the rest of the monkeys so that they became humans?

Thus Darwin's theory collapses from its beginning to its end, and scholars of the species are now demolishing it. The Truth, blessed and exalted, has informed us that these creatures that lie beneath man in rank cannot arrange premises and draw conclusions from them, and do not know alternatives in choice. The animal, although it is the highest of the species, has no alternatives; it learns one task and the matter ends, because they are creatures that do not reason. But man has been given the capacity to choose between alternatives. Try to oppose a cat, and you will find it attacks you and wounds you with its claws, unless you have domesticated it and know that you are playing with it. As for the faithful, reasoning, accountable believer, he behaves in situations differently. If a person harms him, he may repay him with the like of what he suffered, he may pardon him, or he may restrain his anger.

﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon people﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:134).

So you, O believer, have many alternatives, but the animal does not possess such alternatives.

For this reason we gave the example earlier: if you feed an animal until it eats and is satisfied, then after it is satisfied you bring it some extra of its most delicious food, you will find it does not eat it. Whereas man, if he is satisfied, may not object to eating beyond his fill from a kind he loves.

Another example: we see in the countryside that when a donkey sees a stream of water whose width is beyond its ability to jump over to cross it, the donkey stops, refusing to leap or pass over this stream. Did the donkey measure the distance with its eye and weigh it against its ability? It leaps over streams that are within its capacity, but it refuses what is beyond that capacity, although we describe the donkey as dull.

This shows us that every kind proceeds according to the law of its creation to perform the task God intended for it. Someone may say: How does the Truth, blessed and exalted, say, "Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah," while all animals are subjugated? We say: if you, O man, take on the function of the lower, then you are choosing to be worse than the beast, because the lower is subjected by its law and does things by its instincts, not by its thought, so it is as though the faculty of choosing between alternatives does not exist in it. But you, O man, Allah has distinguished you with reason that chooses between alternatives. If you halt your reason from working, and you deprive yourself of the capacity to accept what you hear of revelation, are you not the worst of creatures?

When we reflect on the word "evil and good," we read the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ (Surah al-Zalzalah, 99:7-8). So good is opposed by evil, and when good is opposed by evil, a person distinguishes the good because it is beneficial and fine, and distinguishes the evil because it is harmful and ugly.

But the word "khayr" is sometimes used in another sense that is not opposed by evil; it is said: this matter is better (khayr) than the second, although the second is also good, as in the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, related from him:

("The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, but there is good in each.") (1)

Each of them, that is the strong believer and the weak believer, has good in him, but in good there are levels: there is a good that exceeds another good. The Lord informs us in His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, the worst of creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason."

That is, the disbelievers are the worst of what crawls upon the earth, because they have lost the means of guidance, which is hearing, and thereby they have become dumb, that is, they do not utter the word of guidance.

(1) Related by Muslim.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse.﴾ (8:23)

He, glorified and exalted is He, knew that there was no good in them, so He did not make them hear with the hearing of acceptance.

The Lord, glorified and exalted is He, is far above beginning with them by denying them hearing, since there was no good found in them. The good here is intended to mean the first faith in the Messenger, and they did not believe. Thus they did not listen to the call to guidance from him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as one who conveys from Allah, exalted is He. Therefore the absence of good originated from their side, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who said:

﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ (part of 2:264)

and they, therefore, were preceded by disbelief, so Allah did not guide them.

And He, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ (part of 2:258)

and they were preceded by wrongdoing, so Allah did not guide them.

And He, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ (part of 5:108)

and they were preceded by defiant disobedience, so Allah did not guide them.

Allah is far above being unjust toward some of His servants, so He did not make them hear with the hearing of acceptance to the call of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

(And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse.)

The knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, is eternal, but He does not judge His servants by what He knew of them from eternity. Rather, He grants them the choice of free will in the practical experience of life. Let me give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: you find a father suffering the tragedy of his son's failure in his studies or in relying on himself in life, and the boy lives heedlessly, not considering the consequences of life. The father's friends say to him: "Why do you not set up a project for your son to occupy him instead of frivolity?" The father replies: "I know this boy. He will take the project in order to sell it and spend its price on frivolity." The father says this from his experience with the son. But is it not possible that this son has grown weary of deviance and frivolity and wanted to repent, or at least to prove to people that his father's opinion of him is not correct? Therefore we find the father opening a project for his son, but the boy is overcome by his bad nature, so he sells the project to spend its money on corruption.

Did that happen because of a deficiency in the father's experience? No. Rather, the father knew his son's lack of seriousness and how easily he yields to his desires. So what of the Supreme Truth, who knows from eternity all that is hidden and manifest of His servants?

However, glorified and exalted is He, willed not to hold His servants accountable for what He knew of them from eternity, but rather to hold them accountable, glorified and exalted is He, for what actually happens from them. He is the One who said:

﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabut, 29:11).

So He, glorified and exalted is He, knows from eternity, but He willed also to know by the acknowledgment of the servant himself, because if Allah judged the servants by what He knew from eternity, the servant would say: "I would have done what Your method requires, O Lord." Therefore the Truth leaves the choice to human beings so that they may be known in light of their choices, and the action becomes an acknowledgment of what has occurred from them.

﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse.﴾ (Surah al-Anfal, 8:23)

Even if Allah, mighty and majestic, made them hear, they would have turned away from hearing and been averse to it, because He, glorified and exalted is He, knows that they chose to be worse than beasts in His sight: they are the deaf who do not hear the call to guidance, and the mute who do not utter the word of monotheism, and who do not understand the benefit of the method that Allah, exalted is He, set down for the goodness of their worldly life and their hereafter.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿O you who believe! Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart, and that to Him you will be gathered.﴾ (8:24)

Here the matter shifts from hearing to responding, for the task of hearing is to respond.

﴿O you who believe! Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life.﴾ That is, respond to Allah, the Exalted, in legislation, and to the Messenger (ﷺ) in conveying. The purpose of legislation and of conveying is one. There is no conveying from the Messenger except by legislation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the Messenger (ﷺ) was given the authority to legislate. The Messenger of Allah did not legislate of his own accord; rather he legislated by means of a ruling from Allah, the Exalted, where He says:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it.﴾ (59:7)

Let me give an example, and to Allah belongs the highest example. We hear that a certain man was dismissed because he had been absent from his work in his post for fifteen days. The lawyer returns to the constitution that the country follows and does not find this provision in its articles, and he hears from the more experienced lawyer that this law is derived from the constitution's delegation to the body that organizes work and workers.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is delegated by his Lord with conveying and legislating.

﴿Respond to Allah and to the Messenger﴾ (8:24). You will also find that the Exalted and Almighty said: "when he calls you" and did not say "when they call you" (dā‘awākum). In this there is unification of the purpose; He did not separate Allah's legislative ruling from the Messenger's conveying to us. We know that in matters where the Messenger (ﷺ) issued a ruling and then Allah amended that ruling for him, this amendment originated from Allah, and he (ﷺ) never originated a ruling that Allah amended except in matters on which Allah had not sent down a ruling.

When Allah sends down a ruling that contradicts a ruling the Messenger had set, then, out of the greatness of the Messenger (ﷺ), he conveyed this amendment to us. Thus, his (ﷺ) rulings, when they agree with the truth, are not amended, and if the matter is not so, he (ﷺ) amends them for us. By this, all rulings ultimately trace back to Allah, the Exalted. If someone asks: how can you say that the Messenger's speech is from Allah's speech? We answer: it is He, glorified be He, who said:

﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is nothing but revelation revealed.﴾ (53:3–4)

And "desire" (hawā), as we know, means that you know a ruling and then turn away from it to its opposite in order to serve a desire within yourself. The Messenger (ﷺ), whenever he set down any ruling for which he had no ruling from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then if an amendment came, he conveyed it to us. Thus he does not speak from desire; that is, in everything Allah did not send down, and on which he (ﷺ) ruled by his humanness, he had no desire serving any ruling.

In the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿O you who believe! Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you﴾ (8:24), we find that the word "calls you" (da‘ākum) is singular, like the word "they should please Him" (yurḍūh) in His saying:

﴿Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾ (9:62),

and like the pronoun in "from him" (ʿanhu) in His saying:

﴿Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him﴾ (8:20).

In these noble verses there is unification of the pronoun after the dual, and this unification has been a source of doubt for the orientalists, who said: how does He address two and then make them singular? We say to whoever says this: you approached the Qur'an without the faculty of the Arabic language. You did not understand. Had the disbelievers found in the Qur'anic style anything contrary to the language, they would not have remained silent; they are obstinate, and had they found in the Qur'an a single word contrary to it, they would have announced that contradiction. The disbelievers' not announcing these doubts that the enemies raise indicates that they understood the aim and meaning of everything that came in the Qur'an.
