For example, they understood the verse that the orientalists repeatedly talk about in order to cast doubt upon the Noble Qur'an, namely the saying of the Truthful, the Exalted:

﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight against the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.﴾ (49:9)

The orientalists wondered, in disapproval: how does the Qur'an speak of two groups and then the action performed by them comes in the plural form? We say: "two groups" (ṭāʾifatān) is the dual of ṭāʾifah, and ṭāʾifah is not applied to an individual but to a body, just as we say: "the two schools gathered," though "school" (madrasah) is singular. Yet each school has many students, and likewise "two groups" means each group is composed of individuals, and when fighting occurs it is fighting between a multitude and a multitude. Therefore the Noble Qur'an was precise when it said: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾, and it did not say: "and if two groups of the believers fight (dual verb)," because that wording would not precisely express the situation of fighting, since they, as two groups, if they come to fighting among themselves. At the moment of fighting, each individual does not single out one individual to fight; rather each one fights against all the individuals of the other group, and thus the fighting occurs between a large multitude from both groups.

After that, the Truthful, the Exalted, continues to depict the situation of fighting precisely, saying, glorified be He:

﴿Then fight against the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them﴾ (49:9).

Here He, glorified be He, says: "make peace between them" and did not say "make peace between them" in the plural. Thus He shifted from the plural used in fighting to the dual, because in reconciliation we reconcile between two opposing factions, and we do not bring every individual of the group to reconcile him with individuals of the other group. Each group is represented by its leaders or a delegation from it. Thus the Truth used the dual in its place and used the plural in its place, and glorified be He, He is free of error.

Now, in the verse we are still reflecting upon, the Lord, glorified be He, says:

﴿O you who believe! Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ (8:24). At its beginning is a call from Allah to the believers, and a call requires first that the one called be living, for He, glorified be He, said:

﴿And the living and the dead are not alike. Indeed Allah makes hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those in the graves﴾ (35:22).

So how can He say to those He addresses, who are alive: "calls you to that which gives you life"?

We say: what is life first? We know that life takes two aspects: the aspect of sensation and the aspect of movement. This is not achieved except after the spirit exists in matter, so life comes into being. This is a matter in which believer and disbeliever are equal. The fruit of life is that a person be happy in it, not that he live in war, hatred, and the troubling of others and his troubling of others. Real life is that sensation and movement exist, on condition that each person's movement makes him happy and makes those around him happy; thus energies cooperate in increasing reform in beneficial and useful matters. But if the energies produced by sensation and movement are dissipated and life is lost in opposing one another, this is a life of fatigue and hardship, a life in which there is neither good nor ease. This contradicts what Allah, the Exalted, willed for creation. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made man His khalifah (vicegerent) on earth so that he would reform, not corrupt, and so that the righteous would increase in righteousness, and the movement of one individual should not oppose that of another, for every person is a khalifah of Allah, and since we are all khulafa' of Allah on earth, why do we not make our movements in life mutually supportive rather than opposing?

For example: if a person wishes to serve himself and those around him by digging a well, all those who will benefit from the well must cooperate with him: one group digs, and another group carries the dirt away, so that water comes out and everyone benefits from it. But if a person sneaks in to fill the well, this makes the movement of life opposing rather than supportive.

The method was sent down from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so that the movement of waters would be supportive; therefore the Truth, the Exalted, says:

﴿O you who believe! Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ (8:24).

The call here from Allah is to believers only. If Allah says: "O you who believe! Respond to what you have believed in," He did not require you to respond to one you have not believed in; rather He asks you to respond when you have entered the fold of faith in Allah, and have been guided to that by your reason, by the cosmic signs, and are convinced of it, and believe that if He asks something of you, He does not ask it in vain, but asks it of you because you have believed in Him, the Exalted, as God, Lord, Creator, Provider, Wise, and Just.

When one who has these attributes commands you, it is obligatory upon you to respond to what He calls you to. And to Allah belongs the highest example: in our lives we find a father and a mother who take into account the near interests of the child; the father commands him, saying: "listen to the speech, for I am your father who labors so that you may enjoy ease." And the mother adds, saying to him: "listen to your father's speech; he is not a stranger to you, rather you have a bond with him, and he is not your enemy, and his experience with you is that he benefits you and wishes you good." Here the son responds. And we are all dependents of Allah; so when Allah says: "O you who believe! Respond to Allah and to the Messenger who conveys from Allah, for he will call you to that which gives you life," then it is incumbent upon us to respond to the call.

The caller, then, is Allah, the Exalted, and His blessing preceded you before He imposed obligations upon you, and He, glorified be He, has sent a Messenger supported by a miracle no one can produce, calling every person to what is good, and nothing prevents a person from responding to this call except being foolish.

We notice in our daily lives that a sick person, afflicted in his dearest and most precious possession, his health and well-being, seeks recovery from this illness and asks about the specialist doctor for what he complains of. For every part of the body there is a specialist physician. If he knows the doctors, he goes to the appropriate doctor; if he does not know, he keeps asking until he finds the suitable doctor. In this way he has fulfilled the task of reason in reaching the one he trusts with his health. When he goes to the doctor and the doctor diagnoses the disease and the remedy for him, at that moment the patient will not say: "I will not take the medicine unless you convince me of its wisdom and benefit and what it will do to my body," because the doctor might say to him: "If you want to know the wisdom of this medicine, go to the faculty of medicine and study as I studied." Naturally no patient will do that, because the matter concerns his health; he goes to the pharmacy, buys the medicine, and asks how to take it, and the patient, in doing so, does it for his own benefit, not for the benefit of the doctor or the pharmacist.

And the Messenger (ﷺ), when he calls us to that which gives us life, does so only because Allah, the Exalted, entrusted him with conveying the method that sets our affairs right. If life is sensation and movement, after the spirit comes into matter, man faces the circumstances of life from then until death. This is a life for both believer and disbeliever, and life may contain troubles and be filled with opposing movements; a single household may be filled with quarrels between children and between neighbors, and a person says: "this is"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 25:

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict exclusively those among you who have done wrong; and know that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Almighty and Majestic Allah commands us to guard against trials (fitan) from their beginning, before their matter grows severe. A person should avoid sin, and society should strike at the hand of every deviation. Whoever today steals treasuries began first by stealing something small: he stole from his brother, or from the house, then from the neighbours, then from the bank. If every deviation had been checked by striking the hand of the one who committed it while it was still small, the deviant and the deviation would not have grown large. You would have buried major crimes in their cradle, because whoever commits a small offence and is not punished has already been given licence. Beware lest any of you say: "As long as such deviation does not touch me, it is none of my concern," for the one who dared against someone like you will find it easy to dare against you. We all know the story of the three bulls: the red, the white and the black. The lion attacked the white bull and ate it, and neither the red bull nor the black bull defended it. Then the lion attacked the red bull, and the black bull said to himself: "As long as the lion has not eaten me, this matter is no concern of mine." Then the lion came to the black bull, and as it approached him it said: "You were eaten on the day the white bull was eaten."

So the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict exclusively those among you who have done wrong﴾ (part of verse 25, Surah al-Anfal)

This saying indicates to us that guarding against trial begins with striking the hand of the one who creates the trial while it is still at its beginning. I shall give this example so that it remains in memory always: a mother divided the food, with its meat, vegetables and fruit, among the children. One of the children ate his share, and then the mother kept the remaining shares of his siblings in the refrigerator. Afterwards the mother noticed that this son, who had eaten his share, was eating the share of one of his brothers behind her back and without her permission. Here she must rebuke him and punish him for such an act, so that he does not go on doing so.

Likewise, if a son brings a toy or an item whose price exceeds his pocket money's ability to purchase, the father must strike the son's hand so that the boy does not continue to ruin himself. Thus we find that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, placed the blood-money (diyya) for accidental killing upon the 'aqila, who are the 'asaba, that is, the paternal kinsmen of the killer, and they are called the family, that is, the killer's family, because when the members of a family see that each of them will bear a share of the penalty, they strike the hand of whoever goes to extremes in terrorising others and threatening them, if he is of their family.

Therefore you see that when people see the wrongdoer and do not strike his hand, Allah encompasses them with a punishment from Him, because the wrongdoer goes to extremes in his injustice and tyranny and runs riot against others.

Thus injustice spreads through society, and the punishment of Allah becomes due upon everyone. For this reason we find our master Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, saying, explaining this to us in what Imam Ahmad narrated from him. Imam Ahmad narrated, saying: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "O people, you recite this verse: ﴿O you who believe, you are not harmed by those who have gone astray if you are guided﴾, and you place it other than its proper place. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'If people see the evil and do not change it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is about to encompass them with His punishment.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explains the decisive path in matters of creed and legal rulings and brings a clear example upon which all agree. He (ﷺ) said, as narrated from him by al-Nu'man ibn Bashir: "The likeness of one who upholds the limits of Allah and one who falls into them is that of a people who drew lots over a ship, so some of them obtained the upper part and some the lower part. Those in the lower part, whenever they needed water, would pass by those above them, and they said: 'If only we made a hole in our portion and did not harm those above us.' If they are left to what they want, they will all perish; but if they seize their hands, they will be saved and they will all be saved."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives us the example of people who boarded a ship and cast lots among themselves so that they would divide into two groups: a group sitting in the upper half of the ship, that is, on its deck, and a group dwelling in the belly of the ship, according to what the division by lot brought, which is what is called al-istihām.

This indicates to us that they were good people, and there was no strong group among them imposing something upon a weak group. Those who lived at the bottom of the ship, when they wanted water, would climb up to lower their vessels from the deck of the ship to the river.

Had those in the bottom of the ship been left to carry out their desire to bore a hole in the ship in order to take water from the river, the ship would have sunk; but if those living above the ship seize the hands of those who wish to bore it, they will all be saved.

Thus is our understanding of the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict exclusively those among you who have done wrong; and know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾ (Surah al-Anfal).

Someone may ask and say: The punishment falls here upon the wrongdoer and the wronged, and the wrongdoer is the one who deserves punishment for the injustice that issued from him, but what is the fault of the wronged?

The answer: The wronged person had the ability to repel the injustice but he kept silent about it, so he deserved to be included in the punishment.

And if societies do not pay attention to resisting trials, Allah sends punishment upon them, and the punishment of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is more severe than the punishment of creatures.

1 istahamu: cast lots.
2 Narrated by al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 26:

The Exalted Lord says:

﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might snatch you away; so He sheltered you, strengthened you with His help, and provided you with good things, that perhaps you would be grateful.﴾ (8:26)

After all the events that had taken place, the Lord, glorified and exalted, here reminds the one in the highest state of his lowest past, so that it is established for him that the One who moved you from a lowest life to a highest life exists and still exists. Since His power willed to move you from the lowest to the highest, then His power, glorified and exalted, if He willed, could move you from the highest to the lowest.

So if you are in a higher state, beware of forgetting that you were once in a lower state. You must acknowledge the favour of the Creator, the Bestower, the Benefactor, and say: My mighty, great Lord is the One who gave me and raised my station, and I did not do that by my own skill. Even if you have risen by your skill, skill is a gift from Him, glorified and exalted. Therefore the Lord, mighty and majestic, says:

﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land﴾, meaning: keep this matter in your minds always, and beware of fearing any force, however great it becomes; rather, prepare against every force the appropriate method of confrontation in abundance, because you are bearers of a call (da'wa), and whoever bears the call may suffer calamities, hardships and difficulties; but this must not weaken your resolve.

The early Muslims were a few people suffering from the humiliation and persecution of the powerful disbelievers. Sometimes an early Muslim would find no one to protect him from the persecution of the tyrants, so he would turn to a disbeliever in whom he hoped to find mercy and say to him: "Grant me protection from your disbelieving brothers." When the weakness of the early Muslims reached its peak, and they found no protector from the oppression and torture of the disbelievers, the Prophet (ﷺ) proposed that they emigrate to Abyssinia (al-Habasha), because there was a king there under whom no one is wronged. The emigration to Abyssinia was a flight from the strength of the adversaries. The condition of the Muslims did not remain thus; rather, God helped them, not by their strength, but He, glorified and exalted, willed for them to take up the causes of His method, so they prevailed and the word of Allah, mighty and majestic, was exalted.

We take this matter as proof and as an example with which to confront those who doubt the ability of Muslims to administer life and advance it, because the whole world witnessed a thousand years in which the Muslims were the leaders of knowledge, thought and innovation, and most nations were subject to the rule of the state of Islam.

I have already said that Harun al-Rashid, the Muslim caliph, sent to Charlemagne, king of France, a gift: a water-driven clock (sa'a daqqaqa), designed with such high precision that it exceeded the imagination of the people of France. When they saw it in France, they thought that devils were what moved it, because scientific and applied progress in Baghdad at that time surpassed all European conception, while they were living in severe scientific backwardness.

But the matter has been reversed in our time, and we suffer from backwardness in taking up the causes of God in order to benefit from knowledge. When the "radio" and the "television" came to some Islamic countries, we found someone saying about the radio that inside it there is a devil who speaks, changes colour and alters his voice. Those holding this opinion did not give up their astonishment and rejection of the existence of the broadcasting station and receiving sets in their countries until we said to them:

Turn the dial of the radio and you will find it broadcasting the Noble Qur'an. When they did so, they listened to the voice of Sheikh Muhammad Rif'at, who was reciting in Surat Maryam. We said to the holders of this opinion: the devil does not recite the Qur'an; rather, the radio and receiving sets are scientific inventions reached by those who took up the causes of God in applied science.

When the invention of the "microphone" came, and many demanded that it be placed in the mosques at the time of Friday prayer, we found some refusing the entry of the microphone into the mosque, ignoring that in large mosques, making the people hear the Friday sermon requires more than one "microphone". I said to one of these people: May God set right your condition and your affairs. Why do you wear medical glasses and place them over your eyes? He answered me: Because my sight is weak and the glasses enlarge the writing. I said: Likewise the "microphone" enlarges the voice so that the one sitting far from the pulpit and the imam may hear it during congregational prayer and the Friday prayer.

If some Islamic countries have reached this degree of incapacity in accepting knowledge, this is a warning to us to return to taking up the causes of God in the universe, to develop the sciences, and to serve with them the method of God, instead of remaining backward, although the method of God urges us to take up the causes present in the universe. All of us know that the universe is in God's hand and its laws are in His hand; He, glorified and exalted, subjects them to whoever takes up the causes.

The Blessed and Exalted Lord reminds us with His saying: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might snatch you away﴾ (part of 8:26).

Khatf (snatching) is taking quickly, meaning that a person or a group takes what is not rightfully theirs. We have known before that taking what is not right has several forms. For example, a merchant displays, that is spreads out, his goods of dates or apples, and a passer-by comes to look at the goods laid out, having no money to buy with, and snatches an apple or some dates and runs quickly away; the owner of the goods tries to run after him but cannot catch up. This is khatf. But if the owner of the goods is able to catch up with him and the thief tries to get free and escape from him, this is called ghasb (usurpation). As for theft (sariqa), it is taking property secretly from a safe place when its owner is absent. All of this differs from embezzlement (ikhtilas), because embezzlement is taking from what is in your custody while you are entrusted with it. So the forms of taking what is not right are: snatching (khatf), usurpation (ghasb), theft (sariqa), or embezzlement (ikhtilas). The Blessed and Exalted Lord says:

﴿fearing that people might snatch you away, so He sheltered you and strengthened you with His help﴾ (part of 8:26), meaning: they would seize you without anyone defending you. And here you are, having become strong through the settling of faith in your hearts and by the aid of Allah, mighty and majestic; therefore you must remember Him always in gratitude, appreciation, worship, thankfulness and humility. He, glorified and exalted, has given you stability in the new refuge, the city of Madinah, and the community of faith in Madinah welcomed you.

When you entered Madinah, you established the mosque, which is a sign of the continuing of light from heaven as guidance for the earth. This was your first work, and you had not been occupied with any other work before it. The Ansar regarded you as brothers, and you became strong through the brotherhood of faith, and they too became strong through this brotherhood, after the Jews had been seeking victory over them through the coming Prophet. The Messenger came, and his mission was the support of the oppressed, and his method became a strength for you and for the Ansar. Whoever among you emigrated would find an invitation from an Ansari to his house, not only for food and drink, but for residence as well.

Then the remarkable point occurred. A person, when God bestows on him various blessings, may love to share these blessings with his companion, except for a woman, since a husband is jealous over his wives. But an Ansari among them, if he was married to two women, would say to the emigrant: "You have come from Makkah to Madinah without your family. Look at my two wives; whichever of them pleases you, I will divorce her, and you may marry her after her waiting period ('idda) ends." This is the remarkable point, and it is a matter that could never pass through the imagination of an Arab.

The Blessed Lord concludes the noble verse with His saying:

﴿and provided you with good things, that perhaps you would be grateful﴾ (part of 8:26).

God, glorified and exalted, provided for them, supplied them with bounties, weapons and precious things, and they defeated the chiefs of Quraysh. The spoils had not been lawful to any prophet before, but they were made lawful for our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). So He who did all that for you deserves to be remembered and never forgotten, and to be thanked always.

The commentary continues, and the passage above is part of a longer exposition. Here is the translation of the text provided.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says after that:

﴿O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know [better].﴾ (8:27)

Betrayal (khiyanah) is opposed by trust (amanah). A trust is a thing that one person deposits with another without any document upon it and without witnesses. Rather, the matter is left to the one who holds the trust: if he wishes, he acknowledges it, and if he wishes, he denies it, because a trust has no certificate upon it, no witnesses, and no bill of exchange. It is governed by nothing except the good faith of the one who was entrusted. The Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was ever wrongdoing and ignorant.﴾ (33:72)

All the kinds that exist in the universe below the human being—animals, plants and inanimate things—are all subjugated, and they do not possess the choice to act or not to act. The sun has no choice to say, "I will rise today upon these people," or "I will not rise today." The air does not possess the will of choice. All the creatures that Allah brought into being in this existence, other than the human being, are subjugated to the believer and the disbeliever alike. These creatures refused to bear the trust of choice, but the human being said: "I have an intellect that chooses between alternatives, and I accept to bear the trust, and I will fulfill all the requirements of the trust because I am capable of choosing."

But the human being claimed for himself the capacity to fulfill the trust, as though he were certain of himself that he would discharge it, while he does not know what judgment he has passed on a matter that is unseen and future.

It is true that at the moment of undertaking, he intended to discharge the trust, but what about the moment of discharging it? You do not know what events and changing circumstances will bring upon you; a situation may come upon you in which you are compelled to squander the trust. Therefore you find the wise person is one who says: "Keep far from me the trust of choice, for I do not know what changing circumstances will do to me at the moment of discharge." Everything other than the human being declared its inability to bear the trust and accepted subjugation, whereas the human being declared his acceptance of the trust and that he would discharge it. The Noble Qur'an described him, saying:

﴿Indeed, he was ever wrongdoing and ignorant﴾ (from 33:72): "wrongdoing" toward himself, because he burdened himself with something that was not in his power; and "ignorant," because he measured the moment of undertaking and did not consider the moment of discharge. He did not take into account what the changing circumstances would do to him.

The Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿Do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know [better].﴾

Many of a person's behavioral conduct is concealed from the eyes of people, because when people's eyes see a crime, they summon men of law to take the rights of society from the criminal. But what about hidden crimes?

We know that every crime that surfaces and appears clearly is in fact underlain by concealed crimes, because the one who kills is hiding other crimes, such as buying a weapon without a license; and if he has no money, he may steal in order to buy the weapon, then he recruits others to help him in the killing. All of that is hidden crime. Certainly there are inner behaviors, after which comes the behavior that disturbs society, which is the apparent crime. The utmost of human law is to guard society from apparent crimes only, but the eye of the law does not perceive inner and hidden crimes. As for the eye of religion, it is different: it guides the depths toward what is right, because religion is a trust that the Truth—who created creation—placed in the conscience of the human being. So beware of betraying the trust in secret matters that no one knows except Allah, because matters that people know can be defended before those people, unlike inner matters, which are the important ones, because they are what controls the production of behavior.

So beware of betraying Allah and the Messenger, and betraying the trust that has been placed upon you. You have no argument in that except your choice: if you wish, you act, and if you wish, you abstain. A person must not betray the trust between himself and his Lord; if faith's guardianship from his conscience over inner deeds is not present, he may deviate, because every apparent crime is carried out only after an inner matter has been plotted.

Since you have believed in Allah, the Exalted, as Lord by your own free choice, then adhere to the things that the one in whom you believed has brought you. You know that faith is the cause of every obligation. For example: you pray five obligatory prayers because the Lawgiver commanded you to, you pray two rak'ahs at dawn, four at noon, four at afternoon, three at maghrib, and four at night, because the Lawgiver, who is the Master, glorified and exalted, commanded you. And you fast because Allah commanded you to fast. If you later come to realize that there are benefits for you in fasting, that is another subject; nevertheless, the reason for fasting remains that Allah commanded it. Thus the cause of every ruling is faith in the one who issued that ruling.

﴿O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger﴾ (from 8:27).

And what is betrayal? The root of betrayal is all deficiency; its opposite is completeness, perfection and fidelity. Corresponding to all of this are treachery (ikhtiyan) and deceit (ghadr). So if Allah says to us: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger," then we must comply, because the legislation has reached us from Allah through the Messenger, and whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah, because Allah did not address us directly, but addressed a messenger whom He chose from among His creation and supported with a miracle. Every communication was made through the Messenger.

﴿Do not betray Allah and the Messenger﴾: so do not betray Allah in what came in the Qur'an, and what came from the Messenger who was authorized by Allah to legislate. The legislation of the Messenger and his followers is in the words of the Exalted:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ (from 59:7).

So Allah has a trust in what He has stated explicitly in the Qur'an, and the Messenger has a trust in what the Qur'an did not state explicitly, through the delegation by the Speaker of the Qur'an to the Messenger to legislate. So if you obey this Messenger, you have obeyed Allah.

We have understood that betrayal is deficiency, and the meaning of deficiency is standing far from the perfection and completion required. When a person believes, faith becomes a trust in the soul. You have believed that there is no god but Allah, and the trust of this faith requires that you do not grant any created being authority over you or loyalty to him, unless that loyalty springs from following the method of Allah, the Exalted. This is the trust of the testimony; as for the trust of the message, it is keenness to apply everything that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, conveyed from his Lord, to the extent of one's ability.

Therefore, the trust with Allah, the Exalted, is that you adhere to the word of faith that there is no god but Allah. Beware of believing that anyone can dispose of you, or possess for you harm or benefit, or that your affairs can be settled apart from Allah. Everything is in the hand of Allah, the Glorified, possessor of might and power, and there is no god but Allah. Beware of understanding that a ruling comes to you by a route other than the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, because if you step outside this framework you become a person who has not discharged the trust of Allah nor the trust of the Messenger.

The pinnacle of trust is faith in Allah and faith in the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah has commanded rulings, and when you accept them, they become a trust; their trust is to discharge them without deficiency in anything, whether it is general or specific, even if it is a hadith that passes before you. The trust of faith extends to everything, such as the trust of any gathering you attend: it is not permissible for you to transmit the secrets of others to that gathering, or the secrets of the gathering to others.

We know a man among the leaders of the Arabs, Ziyad ibn Abih, who was extremely firm. A tale-bearer informed on Hammam ibn Abdullah al-Sulami to Ziyad, and the people expected a severe punishment for Hammam, because Ziyad used to act on suspicion. But Allah inspired Hammam with a word that remained a constitution followed. When Ziyad summoned Hammam, Ziyad said: "It has reached me that you satirized me." Hammam said: "Not so, may Allah set you right. I did not do it, nor are you deserving of it." Ziyad said: "This man—and he brought the man out of the tent—informed me." Hammam looked at him and found him a companion, a friend and an intimate. When he saw him thus, he turned to him and said: "You are a man: if I entrusted you when we were alone and you betrayed me, or if you spoke a word without knowledge and then retracted from the matter that was between us, then it is in the position of betrayal and sin. That is, either you are a traitor or a sinner. If I entrusted you with a word by which I relieved myself, then you are a traitor; and if you fabricated it against me, then you are a liar." Ziyad was impressed by this argument, distanced the tale-bearer, and did not accept from him. It is said that he bestowed gifts and rewards upon Hammam. Whenever Hammam saw the tale-bearer, he would say: "Do you have another tale-bearing that would enrich me?!"

In the biography of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, there are incidents that occurred in his history, even from some of the Companions. For example: we know that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Madinah, he made a covenant between himself and the Jews. The Messenger of Allah kept faith with them as long as they kept the covenant. When they broke the covenant, the Messenger of Allah wished to discipline them, and he disciplined them. The first of that was with Banu al-Nadir, and he made clear to them that he would not kill them, but would suffice with expelling them from their homes and banishing them to Syria. Then treachery came from Banu Qurayzah, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, besieged them for a period of time. They sent to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, someone who said: "O Messenger of Allah, Banu Qurayzah want you to do to them what you did with Banu al-Nadir," meaning that Banu Qurayzah offered to leave the land for Syria. The Messenger refused this except after they accepted that Sa'd ibn Mu'adh should judge them. Sa'd loved Banu Qurayzah and had ties with them. Banu Qurayzah knew that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would be reassured by Mu'adh's judgment, so they said: "No, but send Abu Lubabah to us first." This was his kunyah; his name was Marwan ibn Abd al-Mundhir, and his wealth was in the hands of the Jews, who traded with it for him, meaning he had a financial tie with them.

Abu Lubabah went to the Jews, and they consulted him on the matter, asking: "Shall we accept the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh?" What did Abu Lubabah say? He said: "It is slaughter," and he pointed to his throat. After that, Abu Lubabah blamed himself and said: "By Allah, my feet had not moved before I realized that I had betrayed the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace." But look at faith, the certainty of faith, and the preference of the matter of the Hereafter over the matter of this world; the exposure of a person in this world is a light matter compared with his exposure in the Hereafter.

He went to the pillar of the mosque—that is, a column in the middle of the mosque—in full view of people, and he passed sentence upon himself to bind himself to the pillar with his own hand, and he remained without eating or drinking for seven days, until his strength gave out, he fainted and fell. Allah turned toward him with mercy, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Allah had accepted his repentance. They said to him: "Release yourself, for you are the one who bound yourself." He said: "By Allah, I will not release myself until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, releases me." So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went and untied him from the pillar.

Why did Abu Lubabah do that to himself? Because he felt that he had betrayed the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he told the Jews that it was slaughter.

There is another Companion, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had resolved to prepare for the conquest of Makkah and wished to conceal his advance so that Quraysh would be surprised, so that the surprise would prevent the emergence of obstinacy and the peace would be completed. Therefore he kept the matter secret. Afterward, the Messenger sat among his Companions, and Allah informed him that Hatib had sent to Quraysh informing them. Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 8, verse 28:

The Blessed and Exalted Truth says:

﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward.﴾

When we investigate the connection between this verse and the one before it, we find the link is clear. Betraying Allah, betraying the Messenger, and betraying trusts happen only to achieve a desire or a benefit for the self. You must judge this for yourself, since you may not be able to judge for others. For example: you may not be able to meet your children's demands, and your income may not be enough for their needs. Does that mean you should take a trust deposited with you by someone? No.

Does that mean you should cheat in buying and selling to achieve some interest? No.

Should you betray people's trusts for the sake of your children's interests, or so that you become rich? No.

Here the Truth has mentioned both wealth and children together and told us that they are a trial (fitnah). As we have learned before, a trial is not blamed or praised except by its outcome. It may be praiseworthy if you pass the test, and blameworthy if you fail the test described in this noble verse.

Those who follow the secrets of Qur'anic expression know that every letter has wisdom, every word has wisdom, and every sentence has wisdom. Therefore, some ask: why did the Blessed and Exalted Truth put wealth before children? We say: because every person has wealth, even if it is only his clothing. Naturally, not everyone has children. Moreover, children come from marriage, and marriage requires wealth. Therefore it was logical for the Truth to mention wealth first and then mention children.

The noble Qur'an treats this subject in various ways. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women and sons, and heaped-up piles of gold and silver﴾ (part of verse 14, Surah Ali 'Imran).

In this statement we find that "heaped-up piles of gold and silver" are mentioned after women and sons. It does not mention wealth first and then children as a trial. We must notice that He, glory be to Him, mentions here the heaped-up piles, which come after achieving the first desire, namely women, and the second adornment, namely children. We know that whoever has wealth sufficient for marriage and having children may still crave more wealth. If the unit of the "qintar" (heaped measure) is the qintar, then the person who owns a qintar craves more, just as one who owns a thousand pounds desires to increase what he owns until he reaches a million pounds, and so on. Thus "heaped-up piles" means the desire to exceed in wealth.

Here the Blessed and Exalted Truth says:

﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ (part of verse 28, Surah al-Anfal).

And He says in another verse:

﴿O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ (part of verse 14, Surah al-Taghabun).

In this statement we find that enmity comes from spouses before children. We know that sometimes the wife is the one who dislikes first, and then the children are affected by her dislike and imitate her. This is logical speech, because the One who speaks is a Wise Lord.

"And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial." In this statement there is a clear warning: beware lest you fail this test. Whoever gathers wealth from the unlawful for the luxury of his children is a betrayer of the trust, and this is his punishment. For this reason, the Blessed and Exalted Truth reminds us at the end of this verse of what makes success in the test dear to us, saying: "And that with Allah is a great reward."

We know that human nature, by its innate creation from Allah, is inclined to love benefit for itself. But what is disputed is the value of this benefit and the duration of this benefit. The one who steals wants to benefit himself through another's effort, and the one who does not steal also wants to benefit himself, so that Allah blesses him in his wealth and gives him lawful provision. Thus utilitarianism lies behind every action, whether positive or negative. The example I always give for this is the student who neglects his lessons, whose family wakes him each morning with difficulty, and then he leaves the house to wander the streets; and the second student who wakes early, goes to his school, and devotes himself to his lessons. Each of the two students wanted to benefit himself: the failure wanted a foolish benefit, and the successful one wanted benefit in the future. We know that benefit is a sought-after goal for every soul. What matters is the value of the benefit and its duration. So if betrayal would bring you benefit in your children and your wealth, then recall the reward with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that corresponds to the trust. Place this on one pan and that on the other pan, and see which pan tips. The pan of the reward with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will certainly outweigh.

For this reason al-Mutanabbi said:

I see that we all seek life for ourselves,
eager for it, enamoured of it, passionately devoted.
So the love of the coward for his soul brings him to piety,
and the love of the brave for his soul brings him to war.

We all love life: the coward who fears war loves life, and the brave one who loves himself and knows his worth in the sight of his Creator plunges into war desiring the life of martyrdom, which is a life with Allah until the Hour comes, followed by the life of Paradise, where he abides forever.

Thus the measure by which we weigh benefit is the very point of disagreement.

In the custom of people, the wage equals the value of the work, but the reward with Allah does not equal the work only; rather it is great by the boundless power of the Blessed and Exalted Truth:

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 29:

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan) and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, begins this noble verse with the call of faith, then sets a condition: "if you fear Allah," and the answer to the condition is that He will grant us a criterion (furqan), will remove our misdeeds, and will forgive us. He, glorified is He, is the Generous and the possessor of great bounty.

What is meant here by taqwa (God-consciousness) is commitment to the rulings (al-ahkam). The peak of commitment to the rulings is faith in Allah, mighty and majestic is He. When the two are found together, faith in Allah and commitment to the rulings, the promise of Allah must be realized, as represented in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿He will grant you a criterion, and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾ (part of verse 29, surah al-Anfal)

The word furqan comes from the root "f-r-q" (fa, ra, qaf), and it always comes to mean separation between two things, just as Musa struck the sea with his staff, so that each divided part was like a great mountain.

And He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And when We divided the sea for you﴾ (part of verse 50, surah al-Baqarah), meaning that Allah, glorified is He, removed the connection between two connected things, so that a great division came between them.

Suppose, for example, that you brought a cloth of fabric even in weave and color, then you cut a part of the cloth. Here it is not said that you separated the two pieces (faraqta); rather you parted them (fasalta). But the word firq is not used unless the separation results in two groups: one group here, with its things and attachments, and another group there, with its things and attachments.

Therefore furqan is not merely separation between things that are joined together; rather it is a separation that results in each group having its own method, doctrine and opinion.

And "He will grant you a criterion" means He separates between two things that had no agreement between them, for if there were agreement between them they would become one group. But because they are different, there must be contradiction between them. And here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: He will grant you a criterion. For example, there are those who are guided, and there are those who go astray. Naturally there is a difference between guidance and misguidance. Allah expanded the chest of the one guided to Islam, and made the chest of the disbeliever narrow and constricted, containing spite, envy, hatred, deceit and treachery. Therefore our Lord separates between the one in whose heart is the tranquility of faith and the one whose chest is filled with rancor. The believer belongs to a group that differs from the group of people with hateful hearts.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿He will grant you a criterion﴾ (part of verse 29, surah al-Anfal): that is, He, glorified and exalted is He, separates you, or separates the generality of truth from the generality of falsehood, because He wants the movement of life to be an integrated, harmonious unity, not dominated by the desire of one group against another group with a different desire, for they are all vicegerents of Allah on earth, all created by Allah, and all enjoying the provisions of Allah. Therefore their movements must be mutually supportive and coordinated, not antagonistic.

Division, as we know, arises only from a clash between two parties: one of them represents the party of guidance, and the second is the one upon whom the punishment of Allah is due.

﴿If you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion﴾ (part of verse 29, surah al-Anfal). The furqan is represented in the guidance of the heart, insight, knowledge, and whatever separates truth from falsehood. Man's conditions, as we know, are of two kinds: conditions of this world and conditions of the Hereafter. The conditions of this world include hidden matters of the heart and apparent matters. If we look at the states of this world, we find apparent ones, which is outward movement perceived by the senses, and heart-related ones, which only the owner of the heart knows. The furqan in the heart-related matters of this world you sense when you find who has been guided and who has gone astray; we find that the guided one has had his chest expanded by our Lord to Islam, and we find that the one who has gone astray is the one whom Allah has not expanded his chest to Islam. The guided one lives within the group in which there is no rancor and no hatred, and the one who has gone astray is the one who lives in a group characterized by rancor and hatred. This is regarding heart matters. As for outward deeds, the Truth grants the furqan between the people of faith and the people of disbelief, through victory, dominance and honor.

And what of the furqan in the Hereafter?

The Truth grants the furqan in the Hereafter, such that for the people of faith there is lasting bliss and great reward, and for the people of disbelief there is severe punishment and great abhorrence.

﴿If you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion and will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ (part of verse 29, surah al-Anfal). If we are to fear Allah, will we have misdeeds?

I say: if by His saying "if you fear Allah" you mean faith in Him, then He, glorified is He, removes your misdeeds, both minor and major. Disobedience does not harm together with faith; rather it falls under the pardon and forgiveness of Allah.

And if by taqwa you mean "commitment to a command," then the removal of misdeeds means that we fear Allah by abandoning major sins, so He removes from us the misdeeds, which are the minor sins. Removal (takfir) is of two kinds: first, that He covers them for you in this world, or second, that He removes from you the punishment of the Hereafter. For this reason He, glorified is He, concludes the verse with a beautiful ending: ﴿And He will forgive you, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ (part of verse 29, surah al-Anfal).

When bounty is described as great, this means that there is bounty less than great, just as there is bounty that surpasses it in distinction. Yes, and we know that differences in favor exist among human beings: this one favors that one with food, or favors him with clothing, or favors him with drink, or favors him with housing. That is, there are many kinds of bounty, but they are not described as great, because great bounty comes from Allah, the Exalted alone, since every bounty other than Him ultimately returns to Him. Whoever gives another the last loaf of bread, let us know that behind it is one who brought the bread from the bakery, and behind that one who brought the flour from the mill, and behind that one who planted and harvested.

Therefore every bounty is from Allah, and its ultimate return is to Allah, mighty and majestic is He; this is the great bounty. We also find that the one who bestows a favor on another must seek something through this favor, such as completeness of self, and that he wishes praise and commendation, and seeks the comfort of a human soul. We see people who give favors to others in order to lessen their own pains, not because they apply the method of Allah, but desiring only the comfort of the soul, like the disbelievers who make things that benefit people; they do them while Allah is not in their minds, but only the comfort and harmony of their own souls.

So the one who bestows a favor is seeking something: either completeness of wealth, or praise and flattery, or relief of the soul from the painful scenes it sees. This is evidence that he suffers from some deficiency and wants to complete it. If Allah, mighty and majestic is He, is the possessor of bounty, is there any deficiency in His perfection?! No.

So this is the great bounty, which He bestows upon His servants as an act of grace, without desire for perfection or praise. Also, every bounty other than Allah contains reproach, but the bounty of Allah, exalted is He, contains no reproach and no humiliation for anyone. A person may disdain to take something from another person, but who disdains the bounty of Allah? No one, because all life is a gift from Him. For this reason the example is given of the young woman who said to Ma'n ibn Za'ida:

"Return, for the generous return,
and do not think of the son of Arwa that he would return."

The young woman was asking Ibn Za'ida to return to bestowing favors upon them, so her father rebuked her, and she said to him: "O my father, kings are not ashamed to be asked."

﴿And Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ (part of verse 29, surah al-Anfal). The Truth, glorified is He, wants us to pay attention to the fact that every manifestation of your existence in life, every means by which your life is sustained, and all your comforts, if you trace them back, will reach Allah. If you are buying, for example, furniture for your house, and you choose rosewood to be the wood from which the carpenter makes this furniture, you bring this wood from Indonesia or Pakistan, for example, because the forests there produce this type of wood. Everything in your life, if you trace its chain, you will find that the hands of created beings end at a creation of Allah that He gave to man, and this is the great bounty from Allah, blessed and exalted is He.

After the Truth, glorified is He, made clear with this guidance: "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts (amanat), for the sake of your children or your spouses. And know that the return of all bounty is to Allah, exalted is He," and mention the reality of the world with you: have these matters come true, or will you not believe them? All of them have come true, as the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people would snatch you away﴾ (part of verse 26, surah al-Anfal).

This statement applied to the Muslims. What of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? Here the Lord, glorified is He, says:

﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters.﴾ (verse 30)

We note that God, glorified and exalted, does not use the word *dhikr* (remembrance) with regard to the Prophet (ﷺ). He does not say to him, "Remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you." Yet in addressing the Companions He uses the word *dhikr*, saying: ﴿And remember when you were few﴾. What is the reason?

The reason is that it does not occur to the mind that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would neglect the remembrance of God, the Exalted, because *dhikr* is his mission, peace and blessings be upon him. God, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder﴾ (Surah al-Ghashiyah).

This remembrance and reminding are the function of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). This differs from the role of faith in the lives of believers, because for them faith is meant to correct and reform their lives. Therefore, here, He used only the adverbial phrase (*idh*, "when").

﴿And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters﴾ (Surah al-Anfal, 30). All of this is a condition and a justification for His saying: ﴿And God is the possessor of great bounty﴾.

Makr (plotting) is to devise in secret something that harms the opponent. One who plots and secretly schemes against his enemy does not have the capacity to confront him, so he schemes from behind. Had he the power to confront him, he would not plot. Therefore, only the weak practise plotting. Our Lord, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ (part of verse 76, Surah an-Nisa'). Then He says, glorified and exalted: ﴿Indeed, your plot is great﴾ (part of verse 28, Surah Yusuf). Since their plotting is great, their weakness is greater. For this reason, the Arab poet says:

*A weak woman, when she gets an opportunity,*
*Says: "Thus is the power of the weak."*

Because the weak, if he obtains an opportunity, seizes it, thinking that he may not be given another opportunity; therefore he rushes to kill his opponent. As for the strong, he trusts himself and his abilities, and therefore gives his opponent a second and a third chance, then punishes him in proportion to the harm he has done.

﴿And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you﴾ (part of verse 30, Surah al-Anfal): that is, they devised scheming and plotting against you, but they do not know that He who sent you, O Messenger of God, nothing is hidden from Him. They may be able to plot against those who are like them in power, but you, O Messenger of God, are enveloped by the care and power of God, the Exalted, and bearer of His message; you are under His protection and watchfulness.

So you are not alone, for you take refuge in God, and God reveals to you all their plotting. This scheming and plotting is exposed and disclosed by God. Therefore, the Lord, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿They plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters﴾ (part of verse 30, Surah al-Anfal).

Their plotting has means and ends: they plot to confine you, they plot to kill you, and they plot to expel you. Each of these three has its cause. When the disbelievers of Quraysh learned that the people of Medina, from the Aws and the Khazraj, had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to support him, the disbelievers of Quraysh became alarmed and wished to put an end to this matter. They gathered in Dar al-Nadwa, seeking a solution that would halt the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). A Bedouin entered upon them and found them consulting. They said: "Let us confine him." Confinement (*tathbit*) is the opposite of movement, and His saying "to confine you" means to restrict your movement in the call, because this call was shaking them. Had it not been for the message, they would have continued to welcome you, O Messenger of God, for in their view you had been truthful and trustworthy. Only your final movement to spread the way of God on earth disturbed them, so they wished to restrict his movement (peace and blessings be upon him).

Restriction may be either by preventing the one who moves from moving, or by restricting the mover himself so that his range of movement is defined. Thus confinement comes through shackles or imprisonment. It was said to them: "This is an unsound opinion, for if you shackle him or imprison him, his people will rise and attack you, or they will devise means to free him from the shackles or prison, and you have already besieged him before and did not succeed." Another said: "Let us expel him from our land." They discussed this matter and did not find it correct, and said: "If he leaves, he will influence those to whom he goes, so that he will gain followers from among them who will come to us afterwards to fight us." The Bedouin suggested killing the Messenger of God (ﷺ), but the leaders of Quraysh said: "We fear that his people will take up his vengeance." Then Abu Jahl proposed, saying: "We will take from each tribe among us a strong and sturdy youth, and then they will go to Muhammad while he is in his bed and strike him as one man. When he dies, his blood will be spread among the tribes, and no single tribe will be able to confront all the tribes, so they will accept the blood-money, and we will pay it to them, and end this matter."

Thus did the people debate the confinement of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), the restriction of his movement, his expulsion from his land, or his killing, and all of this with plotting and scheming. God revealed all of that to His Messenger and brought him out of Mecca as an emigrant to Medina, to make clear to them that He, the Exalted, is truly and certainly the best of plotters.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 31:

The Truthful, Glorified and Exalted One says after that:

﴿When Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the legends of the ancients."﴾ :

The Almighty's words, "Our verses," mean the verses of the Qur'an, because we have already established that "verses" (ayat) are either the cosmic signs that draw attention to the existence of the Supreme Creator, such as the night and the day, the sun and the moon, or they are verses in the sense of miracles:

﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why have you not invented one?"﴾ (part of verse 203, surah al-A'raf), and these miraculous verses are a sign of his truthfulness. Or they are verses that form a portion of the Qur'an, which is the methodology.

Here the Blessed and Exalted One says:

﴿When Our verses are recited to them﴾ (part of verse 31, surah al-Anfal). From the word "recited" we understand that the intended meaning is the verses of the Noble Qur'an. So what did they say?

﴿They say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is"﴾ (part of verse 31, surah al-Anfal).

Their saying "if we wished" indicates that they did not say it, because "law" (lau) is a particle of impossibility for the impossibility of something else, just as you say: "If you had come to me, I would have honoured you," so the honouring was impossible from me because the coming was impossible from you. This means impossibility for impossibility. Likewise, a speaker says: "If I had money, I would have bought a palace," and he does not own money, so he did not buy the palace. Therefore, they did not wish and did not say; their speech was merely "bluster" (tahwish) and a threat with no basis. Neither this nor that occurred from them.

So the miraculous nature is established. It was established because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) first asked them to bring the like of this Qur'an. When they said that the Qur'an was extensive and they could not produce its like, he challenged them to bring ten surahs, and when they failed, he challenged them to bring one surah, and they did not come. This was a gradual progression in the demonstration of the miracle.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) challenged them, and the meaning of a challenge is that it stirs the one challenged to mobilise everything within his power to answer the challenge. If the talents that guarantee acceptance of the challenge do not gather for them, they withdraw. But one of them, named "al-Nadr ibn al-Harith," went to Persia, saw a book containing legends and tales, and came to say in the midst of Quraysh: "Here I am saying the like of Muhammad." But his speech had no aim, did not carry a methodology, and there was no capacity for each word to draw a meaning; there was no meaning in his speech attracting the word, so the people turned away from him.

﴿When Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the legends of the ancients."﴾ (surah al-Anfal).

This is their saying, and they had previously acknowledged that it is the Qur'an, and they had earlier said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it in abundance, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (surah al-Isra', 90-93).

When you read these noble verses and enumerate what they asked of him, you find that they asked for the earth to be made to gush forth with a spring of water; they asked that he have a garden of palms and grapes with rivers gushing forth within it in abundance; they asked that the sky fall upon them in fragments as he claimed; they asked that he bring Allah and the angels before them as a guarantee; they asked that he have a house of gold; and they asked that he ascend into the sky. All of this is a long speech that the Noble Qur'an recorded. So is what they said considered Qur'an? No. Let us notice the precision of the Qur'an's expression. No single person made all these demands; rather each of them made a demand, in a different style. But the eloquence of the Noble Qur'an gathered all the styles and rendered them with precise clarity and extraordinary inimitability. For this reason, we should notice that when we hear a quotation of another's speech in the Qur'an, we must not take this speech as the words that were said; rather, these are meanings that were spoken, and the Qur'an brought them in the style of Allah.

Let me give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: if you come to your son and say, "My son, go to your uncle so-and-so and tell him: My father invites you tomorrow evening to dine with him, because he has guests and wants you to see them and them to see you, and to strengthen his standing." When the boy goes to his uncle, does he say the same words? Of course not, because the father may be educated, and the son cannot say the very same words. Or the father may be unlettered, while the son is cultured and mature, so the son conveys the message in more eloquent form.

Therefore, if you hear or read speech from someone other than Allah on the tongue of another, know that this is Allah's rendering of what the speaker required.

﴿When Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the legends of the ancients."﴾ (surah al-Anfal).

"Asatir" is the plural of "usturah," meaning fabricated events and fanciful tales, such as The Thousand and One Nights, Kalila wa Dimna, the Iliad, and other books of legends.

Almighty Allah says next:

﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ (8:32)

The word "idh" (إذ, "when") also comes as an adverb of time. He, glory be to Him, did not say "wa-udhkur an qalu" (remember that they said), but rather said "idh qalu" (when they said). Their incapacity reached the point that they said: if this Qur'an is the truth coming from You, then rain down stones upon us, or bring us a painful punishment.

Is this statement not evidence of the foolishness of those who uttered it? By Allah, if they had intellect, logic and reflection, would they have said that?

Would it not have been more fitting for them to say: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then guide us to it, or make us accept it"? And since they said "O Allah," the one being addressed is Allah.

﴿If this is the truth from You﴾ (part of 8:32).

So they know that Allah, mighty and majestic, has a "from-ness" (indiyyah), and in it there is truth. Thus we see that they acknowledged the existence of Allah, and that with God there is truth. How then if a man came to you and said: "I am a messenger from Allah, and this is the method, and it is both a method and a miracle at the same time" – would it not be obligatory for us to lend an ear to the one who conveys this truth from Allah, and for you to respond to him? But since they had invited upon themselves curse and punishment, this is evidence of their hatred for Muhammad, and out of this hatred they called upon Allah to send down punishment upon them, as He had done to the earlier nations. Their request for this punishment shows that they knew that whoever denies the messengers and rejects the method is indeed receiving punishment from Allah. Thus it becomes clear to us that what prevents them from declaring faith is their refusal to accept the Messenger of Allah personally, and this is expressed in the words of the Almighty in another verse:

﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a man of importance from the two cities?"﴾ (43:31)

So if the Qur'an had been sent down to someone else, they would have believed in it. In this is an acknowledgement that the Qur'an is a miracle and a method. His saying, exalted is He: "And when they said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment'" was spoken by Abu Jahl, and this indicates the abundance of his ignorance, the severity of his denial, his obstinacy and his arrogance, he and those polytheists with him who denied. On the authority of Anas ibn Malik: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham said:

"O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment." Then the verse was revealed: "But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness" (1).

These obstinate people also said: ﴿Or cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim﴾ (17:92).

This is evidence of confusion in speech and loss of rational awareness.

﴿or bring us a painful punishment﴾ (part of 8:32).

Allah, the Almighty, is able to afflict specific people with punishment and able to save the believers. Allah chose not to send down the punishment, because seeing one in pain, even if he is an enemy, involves causing pain. Therefore the Almighty said:

﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ (8:33).

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 33:

Because God's way (sunnah) with His creatures who deny the messengers is that, before sending down punishment, He, glory be to Him and exalted, brings out the Messenger and the believers who follow him. An example of this is His command to Noah, peace be upon him, to build the ark so that he would be saved from the flood. Every messenger whose nation did not respond was struck by something of this kind. Thus the Messenger goes out first, and then the Truth sends down His punishment. Just as He, glory be to Him and exalted, says, explaining the virtue of turning to God through seeking forgiveness:

﴿And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ (part of verse 33, surah al-Anfal).

If they seek God's forgiveness, that means they have believed in Him. But the Truth brought this statement to guide them to the Saviour who delivers a person from them from the crime of disbelief. In this there is mercy from Him, glory be to Him and exalted, as if He urges them to seek forgiveness so that punishment does not descend upon them, and He lays out for them the means of salvation.

﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them﴾ (part of verse 33, surah al-Anfal). The lam in "liyu'adhdhibahum" is called "lam al-juhud" (the lam of negation), and we find that God would not punish them while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was among them. So the presence of the Messenger among them is a matter with a special decree. As for them, the Truth, blessed and exalted, says concerning them:

﴿And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ (part of verse 33, surah al-Anfal).

Thus we see the realities of faith. The pure believing soul, when it has an enemy and a disaster befalls that enemy, the word of gloating never comes to the mind of the believer. This is the believing moral character, which may pain him to see the enemy's display of weakness and humiliation, so God is generous in not punishing a people among whom there are those who seek forgiveness. It is as if He clarifies for us: forgive our wrongdoer for the sake of our good-doer, that is, let the good-doer be lenient toward the wrongdoer. Therefore we find that the Messenger (ﷺ), at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, was prevented from the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram), and this prevention led to their concluding with him a covenant, which is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Among the believers there were those who opposed this covenant, and among them one who said: "Why do we give up the lowly position in our religion?" The one who said this was Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. In the negotiation, Ali ibn Abi Talib came to write the covenant, and at its beginning he wrote "This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed to." The spokesman of the camp of polytheism objected, saying: "If we believed that you are the Messenger of God we would not have fought you. Rather, write: 'This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah has agreed to.'" Ali refused to write it and said: "I will not write it except that the Messenger of God..." So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered him to write it, as they say, to end the situation and to give a miracle; he looked at Ali while he was pleased with him, and said to him:

"Write it, for you will be given the like of it while you are oppressed." This was fulfilled after the Prophet's life, and the caliphate of Abu Bakr, the caliphate of Umar, the caliphate of Uthman, then the caliphate came to Ali and what happened in it happened. The saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was fulfilled:

"Write it, for you will be given the like of it while you are oppressed" (1).

That is, they will take a stand against you like this one, and you will accept it. When the dispute arose between Mu'awiyah and his troops and between Ali and his troops, they wanted to make an agreement between them to prevent conflict among the Muslims. Ali, may God honour his face, said: "This is what the Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib, has agreed and contracted." The spokesman on behalf of Mu'awiyah said: "If you were the Commander of the Believers, would we fight you?" Ali, may God honour his face, recalled what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had said on the day of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah: "Write it, for you will be given the like of it... etc."

This means that politics requires that one not be rigid like one who speaks from an iron mould; rather, politics presumes in those who practise it some flexibility and far-sightedness so that difficult positions may be resolved, because if each party insisted on its position, the covenant would not have been concluded. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was necessary and appropriate so that the Muslims, after being secure from Quraysh, could devote themselves to calling to the way of God on earth. This is what happened during the ten years that followed this covenant, and Islam spread across the regions of the Arabian Peninsula, and after that to all the horizons of the earth.

Therefore the ruler must possess the insight that does not make him rigid, for if he became rigid he would end the good that exists in him and in his people. Thus the Messenger of God wished to teach us the avoidance of rigidity through the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, despite the fact that some Muslims, among them Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "No! Why do we give up the lowly position in our religion?" Others said, questioning and even reproaching: "Did you not promise us, O Messenger of God, that we would enter the Sacred House?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Did I tell you this year?"

When the Muslims heard that, they did not pay attention to the importance of allowing political decisions to mature before they are put into effect. The division nearly occurred among the Muslims, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered upon his wife Umm Salamah distressed, and said to her: "O Umm Salamah, the Muslims are ruined. I commanded them and they did not comply."

We see the stance of Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, the trustworthy wife, the counsellor and adviser. She said: "O Messenger of God, they are distressed. They came with the intention of going to the Sacred House after long separation and longing, then they were prevented from that while they were in sight of the House. But go out, O Messenger of God, and do what God has commanded you, and say nothing to them; slaughter your offering, and when they see you do it, they will do it."

Indeed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out, slaughtered the offering, and the Muslims did likewise. We find our master Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, saying of Hudaybiyyah: "It was the victory in Islam." There was no victory greater than the victory of Hudaybiyyah, but people's assumptions did not extend to the secret from God. The servants are always hasty, while God is not hasty with the haste of His servants until matters reach what is intended for them.

The opponents of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were zealous for their religion, according to the measure of their knowledge and not the knowledge of God. The Truth, blessed and exalted, willed to explain to them the reason He did not make Hudaybiyyah a place of fighting or engagement; so He said:

﴿They are those who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque, and the offering detained from reaching its place. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and thereby incur blame on your account without knowledge, [God would have permitted you to fight. But He admitted to His mercy whom He willed. Had they been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment]﴾ (surah al-Fath, 48:25).

Yes, there were believing men and believing women hiding among the disbelievers. Before the conquest, Mecca had no separate quarter for Muslims who concealed their faith and a separate one for the disbelievers; rather, people lived together. So if war broke out between the people of Mecca and the army that came to Hudaybiyyah, one might kill his Muslim brother who had not declared his Islam. Had it been possible to separate the Muslims who had not declared their Islam from the disbelievers, God would have punished the disbelievers at the hands of the believers with a painful punishment.

And here, in this noble verse which is the subject of our reflections, the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ (part of verse 33, surah al-Anfal). This means that some of them are the ones who seek forgiveness, so God, mighty and majestic, withholds punishment from all, just as He withheld it from the disbelievers at Hudaybiyyah, because there were believers hidden among them.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Reconciliation (Kitab al-Sulh).

Al-Sha'rawi, the commentary on surah 8, verse 34:

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿Why should Allah not punish them, when they keep others from the Sacred Mosque, though they are not its guardians? Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know.﴾

Here we ask: what prevents them from being punished by Allah? Their punishment is justice, because they did what deserves punishment. They barred the Messenger and the Muslims from visiting the Sacred Mosque, because they thought they had guardianship over it, despite the fact that some of them had heard the story of Abraha al-Ashram (Abraha the Ashram) when he came with the elephants to demolish the Ka'bah. Abraha al-Ashram seized one hundred camels belonging to the chief of Quraysh, 'Abd al-Muttalib, the grandfather of the Prophet (ﷺ). 'Abd al-Muttalib went to him and said: "You have taken one hundred camels from me, so I hope you will return them to me." Abraha al-Ashram said: "I came to demolish your House and the House of your forefathers, and you do not speak to me about it, but you speak to me about one hundred camels that I seized from you?" 'Abd al-Muttalib said: "I am the lord of these camels; as for the House, it has a Lord who will protect it."

This is a statement that no one would make who was certain that the Sacred House has a Lord who protects it.
