Then came birds in flocks (ṭayr abābīl) pelting Abraha with stones of hell, and made him and his army like chewed-up husks (ka-ʿaṣf ma'kūl).

So how can Quraysh bar Muhammad and the believers with him from the Sacred House, when by the admission of their own chief they know that the House has a Lord who protects it? How can you have guardianship over the House? It was incumbent upon them to know that guardianship over the House of Allah is by Allah's choosing, and it belongs only to the God-fearing, and Quraysh were not among the God-fearing.

So the grounds for punishment are, then, their barring of others from the Sacred Mosque and that they were not its guardians. Why?

﴿Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know.﴾ (part of verse 34, surah al-Anfal)

If most of them do not know, then the few among them know with certainty the reality of the Sacred House. The sanctity of this House, which the minority knows and the majority of the disbelievers of Quraysh forgot, is the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer; so make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits﴾ (part of verse 37, surah Ibrahim).

Allah, mighty and majestic, placed them in this place so that they would establish prayer, because He, glory be to Him and exalted, loves to be worshipped on earth, even by one person in this place, and so that His worship would remain continuous. However much a group of people rises up, like Quraysh, by barring others from the Sacred House they have followed their desires, and He, glory be to Him, accomplishes what He wills: He defeated Quraysh, gave victory to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Ka'bah regained its sanctity and became a place of worship to Allah on a continuous basis.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 35:

We find that the legislation of the True One, glory be to Him, concerning the times of prayer varies: Subh (dawn prayer) for one people is Zuhr (noon prayer) for another people, and Zuhr for one people is Subh for other peoples, and 'Asr for one people is Subh, Zuhr, Maghrib or 'Isha' for other peoples. Thus we find every part of the day occupied with the times of turning toward God, and at every moment there is someone turning toward the Sacred House of God with a prayer at its appointed time. No corner of the earth is free of the words "Allahu Akbar" (God is greatest), and the Sacred House was built for this very prayer.

But the Quraysh transformed prayer from submission, humility and worship of God, and the recollection of His greatness and majesty, into what the Exalted and Glorified says:

﴿And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.﴾

Their prayer was a manifestation of frivolity and play, which they performed with whistling (muka') and clapping (tasdiyah). Muka' is the whistling they would blow, and tasdiyah is the clapping. Their prayers were a whistling that produced an echo in the ears, along with clapping in a particular rhythm. How, then, could such a thing be a prayer? And how could they bar access to the Sacred House when they had no guardianship over it? For whoever is in charge of the affairs of the Sacred House must be one who fears God, but these people were not fit for piety, because they did not stand for the prayer required of the Sacred House, in which God must be mentioned and worshipped. Therefore punishment was due to whoever persisted in this after the final method of God had been revealed to our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert (people) from the way of Allah. They will spend it, but it will become a regret for them; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered into Hell.﴾ (8:36)

In this verse the Lord makes clear that these polytheists disbelieved in Allah and expended their wealth in order to bar (people) from the way of Allah, yet nothing of what they intended was achieved, and the affair yielded no result at all. It is as if the Truth is exposing the disbeliever: he persists in spending against faith, so he loses his wealth and tastes the pain of regret, because Allah will overcome him afterwards.

When they heard the words of Allah, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿They will spend it, but it will become a regret for them; then they will be overcome, and those who disbelieve will be gathered into Hell﴾ (part of 8:36).

They did not notice that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, is speaking of the future, and that however much the disbelievers spend against the religion of Allah, they will reach no result. The course of events confirms that everything the noble Qur'an brings is true.

And why did they not take note of this? Why did they not save their wealth, when Allah has given victory to His religion?

This, then, is the act of one who has lost insight and intelligence. When the Noble Qur'an says, "fa-sayunfiqunaha" (they will spend it), meaning that the spending will take place in the future, the future has two stages: a near future and a distant future. If the future is near, it says "fa-sayunfiqunaha"; but if it is distant, it says "fa-sawfa yunfiqunaha," just as the Qur'an also says:

﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them away from their qiblah which they used to face?"﴾ (2:142).

The Qur'an informed us in advance of the matter from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Companions proclaimed the report openly, and the Noble Qur'an also informed them; yet they did not heed the warning, which afterwards became a report narrating the proof of their loss of the purity of natural disposition. Therefore regret comes to them after they have spent their wealth and lost it, so they gained nothing and did not achieve their aim or their hopes. Glorified and exalted be He continues to append to this verse, saying:

﴿And those who disbelieve will be gathered into Hell﴾ (part of 8:36).

When the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, speaks of the great torment that befalls the disbelievers in Hell, He does not intend by this discourse to make the Fire their abode; rather, He warns and frightens them away from disbelief, calls them to faith, and urges them not to be disbelievers, lest they be gathered into Hell.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 8, verse 37:

Allah, blessed and exalted, says after that:

﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, and place the wicked some upon others, pile them all together, and then put them into Hell. Those are the losers.﴾ (37)

This noble verse reveals to us that the battles which arise between Islam and its followers on one side, and the enemies of Islam and their followers on the other, are a matter willed by Allah, exalted is He. For the upheaval that occurs, even among those who have believed, is a purification (tasfiyah) of the element of faith. An example of this is what happened at the Isra' (the Night Journey), when we find the one whose faith was weak asking: "Is it reasonable that Muhammad went to Bayt al-Maqdis in one night?!" While we find one whose faith was firm, such as al-Siddiq Abu Bakr, saying: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." The one whose faith is firm and strong believes, while the one whose faith is not firm denies. Thus were the events of Islam: they all came to distinguish the wicked from the good, and to gather the wicked together, one with another, so that they become a heap, and then Allah places them in the Fire.

The events of Islam came for testing (tamhis), just as you put iron into the fire to extract its impurity so that it becomes pure. In the same way Islam came so that the hearts of the believers would be purified and their faith strengthened, because they carry the message of Allah, exalted is He, to the whole earth, after they have passed through many such purifications.

Such purifications also occur in the field of sport. Weightlifters, for example, enter preliminary competitions, and whoever is able to lift the heaviest weight is the one qualified to enter the international competitions, so that the strongest remains.

﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, and place the wicked some upon others, pile them all together, and then put them into Hell. Those are the losers.﴾ (part of verse 37 of Surah al-Anfal)

Allah, glorified and exalted, has given us examples of events that distinguish the wicked from the good. In ordinary, routine circumstances, people's inner natures do not show. When people are believers and do not face danger, they claim courage, generosity and nobility, and they claim a strong faith ready for any sacrifice in the way of Allah. But when events come, they are the true test of what is in the hearts. A person may say to his friend: "I and my wealth are yours." Then if a calamity befalls this friend, he flees from him. So what, then, determines the truthfulness of what one says about oneself? It is events. Thus Allah, exalted is He, willed to distinguish the wicked from the good: calamities rubbed the believers, and the veneer fell away from those of fragile belief, so that people would be witnesses against themselves, and the believers who have purity of heart and creed would remain. When Allah distinguishes the wicked from the good, He, glorified and exalted, intends to single out the good so that it is not mixed with the wicked. The wicked takes various colours and many kinds: this one is wicked in one respect, that one is wicked in another respect, a third is wicked in a third respect, others in a fourth respect, and a fifth, and so on as Allah wills; and Allah gathers all the wicked together and piles them up in the Fire, all of them together.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease, what has passed will be forgiven them; but if they return, the way of the ancients has already passed.﴾ (38)

"Say" is a command from Allah Almighty to His Messenger ﷺ. Since a command exists, there must be one who conveys the command; that is, there is an addresser and an addressee. The addresser here is Allah, glorified is He, and the addressee is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for Allah said to him, "Say." The message he is required to convey to the people is what is contained in the words of the Lord, glorified is He:

﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ (part of verse 38 of Surat al-Anfal). That is: if they cease from disbelief, their sins which they committed during their disbelief will be forgiven. We notice here a difference in the style of speech, because when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addresses the disbelievers, the context would require him to say to them: "If you cease, you will be forgiven." For address must agree with the addressee, and ordinarily when you direct speech to a person there is the "lam of direction"; you say: "I directed my speech to so-and-so," and you address him directly. But here Allah says to His Messenger ﷺ:

﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease, they will be forgiven﴾ (part of verse 38 of Surat al-Anfal), and the context would have required: "If you cease, you will be forgiven." But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, turned away from "in tanhū" (if you cease) to "in yantahū" (if they cease), while the speech is addressed to the disbelievers, and the disbelievers are present, so how can He address them in the third-person form?

Allah, exalted is He, intended that the address be general, to encompass every speaker to whom this statement is said, from any believer; so it is as if He generalized the address in order to cut off excuses. Similar to this is the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed: "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾ (part of verse 11 of Surat al-Ahqaf).

If we apply the same measure, the speech would require saying: "Had it been good, you would not have preceded us to it." But since this phrase was said by more than one disbeliever, to the believers, in multiple places, Allah, glorified is He, wished to draw our attention to this, so He generalized the address to include all cases, not applying to one case only, but to every similar case. Therefore He, glorified is He, said:

﴿If they cease, they will be forgiven what has passed﴾ (part of verse 38 of Surat al-Anfal). This shows us that if they cease from resisting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from their obstinacy against him, then He, glorified and exalted is He, forgives them, because obstinacy and resistance arise from disbelief; if they cease from both, they become believers. And Islam wipes out what came before it.

That is why, when a combatant declared his faith, embraced Islam, testified that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and then entered the battle and was martyred, he became a martyr; for he had been forgiven, by the testimony of Islam, all the sins he committed during disbelief, which are the sins that concern the rights of Allah, Exalted is He. As for what concerns the rights of people, his heirs must discharge it on his behalf.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿But if they return, the way of the ancients has already passed﴾ (part of verse 38 of Surat al-Anfal).

His saying here, "but if they return," Allah intended to teach us that this word should run on the tongue: if they return once more to disbelief and obstinacy, they are cast out from the mercy of Allah and His forgiveness. So the condition for their being forgiven is that they persist in their faith and not return to disbelief again. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the way of the ancients has already passed﴾.

"Sunnah" is the path, or the manner, or the state in which they are; that is why the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And you will not find any change in the sunnah of Allah﴾ (part of verse 62 of Surat al-Ahzab): that is, the method which Allah has chosen for dealing with matters with truth and justice. The meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿the way of the ancients has already passed﴾ is: the method you have known, by which Allah, mighty and majestic is He, dealt with the case of those who opposed the messengers and took toward them the stance of dispute and contradiction. A similar thing happened to the disbelievers at Badr. It is as if whoever stands before the call of Allah and His methodology must face destruction, as happened with everyone who resisted the prophets. You know what Allah did to the people of Hud, the people of ʿAd, the people of Thamud, and the people of Pharaoh, and all of that has passed before you, as a general sunnah encompassing everyone who resisted the prophets and stood in the way of their call to Allah.

The address is either directed to them in their state in their homeland, and to what befell the opponents at Badr, who saw their destruction; or the address is explaining the sunnah of Allah, glorified is He, Whose sunnah willed the annihilation of every opponent of His sunnah.

Then the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, says after that:

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and [until] religion is entirely for Allah. But if they cease, then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ (8:39)

This is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to fight. Qital (fighting) is a mufa'alah, which takes place between two or more parties, that is, a clash between one fighter and another. Therefore, when you hear the word "qital," there immediately comes to your mind the existence of two sides, not one side, or between one group and another group.

When the Almighty, Glorified and Exalted, says: "And fight them," we understand that this is a command to the believers to fight the disbelievers. It must be that the disbelievers have done something that deserves that they be fought over, or that they are plotting to fight the believers, and the believers must confront them and fight them. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, did not say "kill them" but said "fight them," meaning a confrontation that involves the mutual action of fighting. Tafa'ul (reciprocity) means that the action does not come from one party alone; there must be a counterpart with it. You say "qabaltu" (I met/faced), meaning you faced a person, and he also faced you, and this is mufa'alah. Or you say "sharaktu" (I shared), meaning you and another person participated together in some work. Here the Almighty, Glorified and Exalted, said:

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ (part of 8:39): The meaning of that is that there is a fighting that leads to a fighting. The fighting came to settle the matter, because leaving these disbelievers to transgress against the Muslims, and to take their wealth unjustly, would cause people to see the believers as humiliated and oppressed, and the disbelievers as dominant and powerful, so fitnah would arise in the religion, meaning people would be tested in their religion while they see humiliation without any attempt or movement to repel it.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted, wants the fitnah to end. Fitnah is testing. As we said, testing is not blameworthy in itself, but it is blamed by its result. If the student fails the test, its result is blameworthy; if he passes, it is praiseworthy. The disbelievers of Quraysh used to inflict fitnah on people in their religion by torturing them severely until their strength gave way and they submitted to their rule. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, wanted to put an end to this injustice, so He permitted fighting them, because they were the ones who did what necessitates fighting them.

We find His saying, Glorified and Exalted: ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ (part of 8:39).

Whereas we find that it was mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah without "kulluhu" (entirely), where the Almighty says in it: ﴿and religion is for Allah﴾, without the word "kullu" being mentioned. Each verse has its own nuance and meaning, because every word in the Qur'an has a meaning. So His saying, Exalted be He: ﴿and religion is for Allah﴾ means that two religions must not coexist in the Arabian Peninsula, and this has happened. As for His saying, Exalted be He: "religion is for Allah" [entirely], it gives us another nuance. The first pertains to the Arabs and the Arabian Peninsula, while the second means that Islam is for the entire world. The Almighty, Glorified and Exalted, says in the verse we are discussing: ﴿But if they cease, then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ (part of 8:39).

As for His saying, Exalted be He: "But if they cease," meaning they comply and obey. And His saying, Exalted be He: "then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do," meaning they should beware of making this a deception, because Allah is Seeing of them and Aware of them. And since they have moved from the enclosure of disbelief to the enclosure of faith, Allah erases their evil deeds and replaces them with good deeds, because a people who lived upon disbelief and became accustomed to its traits, then abandoned that for faith, this is a difficult matter that requires intense struggle against the self, so Allah, Exalted be He, rewards them according to the measure of their striving against themselves, and the Master, Glorified and Exalted, rewards them generously. There is a second meaning in His saying, Exalted be He:

﴿then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ (part of 8:39), meaning: O you who have taken a hostile stand against faith, and confronted the disbelievers with the confrontation that restored to them refinement and good conduct toward the believers, know that He, Glorified and Exalted, is Seeing of what you have done, so that religion may be entirely for Allah.

Thus we see that each of the two meanings completes the other.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 40:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector (mawlakum); an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper.﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted, desires that people should believe, but at the same time He makes clear to them that the large number of believers is not what raises the banner of Islam or produces victory for faith. So He says: ﴿And if they turn away﴾.

Here is a doubt: that God, exalted is He, is eager for these people to believe, to submit, and to return to the enclosure of truth. Perhaps someone might think that Islam wants to grow strong through them. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿And if they turn away﴾, meaning: beware lest that weaken your arms, or lest this matter diminish your resolve and courage, for you are only victorious by a reinforcement from Allah, the Exalted, the Mighty. So if they do not believe, know that Islam is not victorious through them, and its spread is not by the multitude or the fewness of Muslims, for victory is from Allah, and He is not in need of His creation. The multitude of Islam's soldiers does not produce victory; for Allah's victory for the Muslims, if they follow His method, is realized whether they are few or many. Therefore He draws their attention and alerts them that He has turned away from them because they did not believe, so beware lest that affect your courage, for you are not victorious by reinforcement from these who rejected faith, but by reinforcement from Allah, glorified and exalted; Allah is your Protector. And since Allah is your Protector, that is, your Helper and Supporter, He, glorified and exalted, is:

﴿an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper﴾ (part of verse 40 of Surah al-Anfal). Why?

Because if the protector (mawla) is other than Allah, he is among the things that change (aghyar); today he may be strong and capable of taking us by the hand and helping us, but tomorrow he may die. Therefore he is not fit to be a protector. His authority and strength may fall away from him, and he may become weak, in need of someone to help him, so he benefits no friend and aids no one. The true Protector in whom we must hold fast is the one whom changing things do not touch, because He is everlasting in existence, not ended by death, and He is ever-strong and capable, never weakening. This is the Protector in whom you place your trust and upon whom you rely. Therefore we find that the Truth, glorified and exalted, makes clear to us that we must not place our trust and hope except in Him, nor rely except upon Him, glorified and exalted, when He says:

﴿And put your trust in the Living One who does not die﴾ (part of verse 58 of Surah al-Furqan). That is: if you truly want to rely upon someone, then rely upon the One who always exists and is always strong; so rely upon Allah. His saying, ﴿an excellent Protector﴾, affirms that Allah is strong, capable, and everlasting in existence; and His saying, ﴿and an excellent Helper﴾,

affirms, glorified and exalted, that He encompasses everything that your enemies plot against you, so nothing escapes Him. You fight them with the tricks and arts of war that you know, and they do likewise; but Allah, glorified and exalted, knows their stratagems and nullifies them, and He grants you victory by inspiring you with stratagems they cannot withstand. He gives you reinforcement from heaven, and this reinforcement is what achieves victory for you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 41:

Next, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, speaks about the spoils of war, saying:

﴿And know that whatever you acquire of booty, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (8:41)

What is the reason for mentioning the spoils here? And what is the connection (munasabah)? We say: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is speaking about fighting, and at the end of every battle in which the Muslims are victorious there are spoils.

This is the connection for speaking about the spoils. Since Allah, glorified and exalted is He, speaks of His support for the believers, that He is their helper, and that He is the best of helpers, yet spoils only come as a result of victory, it is as if Allah wants the believers to be assured that victory will be their portion; the evidence is that the discussion moved on to the spoils. Ghanima (spoils) is every movable property that the fighting Muslim takes from the disbeliever, and it is established that spoils were not lawful for any of the prophets before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The Truth says:

﴿And know that whatever you acquire of booty, a fifth of it belongs to Allah﴾ (part of 8:41)

So, a fifth belongs to Allah, and four-fifths remain to be distributed among the fighters. How is the fifth that belongs to Allah to be divided?

The Qur'an has mentioned the method of distributing this fifth in a manner on which the scholars differ. The verse says:

﴿a fifth of it belongs to Allah, and to the Messenger﴾ (part of 8:41)

Then it adds:

﴿and to the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer﴾ (part of 8:41)

Some scholars, holding to the apparent wording of the noble verse, said: the fifth of the spoils is distributed among those whom Allah, exalted is He, named in His Mighty Book, and they are six: (Allah, the Messenger, the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, the wayfarer). So the shares would be six. But the majority of scholars hold that the fifth of the spoils is divided into five shares, so that Allah and His Messenger have one share, because there is no separation between Allah and His Messenger; and the remaining four shares of this fifth are distributed among the four categories (the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, the wayfarer), each category receiving one share.

They also differed concerning the meaning of ﴿and to the near relatives﴾: are they the relatives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or others?

After that, the share of the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer came, and there was no disagreement concerning it. The summary: the spoils in their entirety are divided into five parts, a fifth for these five, and the remaining four-fifths for the fighting army, because Allah, exalted is He, explained the ruling on the fifth and was silent about the rest, which indicates that it belongs to those who took the spoils. Then the Truth says:

﴿if you have believed in Allah﴾ (part of 8:41)

They are, by their very nature, believers in Allah. It is as if this statement came so that they would review their faith if they objected to this distribution. If any of them coveted the fifth that belongs to Allah and His Messenger, and was not content with the four-fifths distributed (as Allah, exalted is He, said), he has damaged his faith in the One who issued this command, and it is He, glorified is He, who sent down this distribution. Whoever deviates and whose eye longs for something should turn back from this deviation, because the One who divided is Allah, who gave victory to the fighters. And if victory is what brought the spoils, then the One who gave victory is Allah, glorified and exalted is He; victory is from Allah, and what is bestowed upon a person of right, the servant must accept Allah's division in it.

An example of this is what Allah wills for the Muslim person of good conduct in his wealth. He is free in his life and holds the right to dispose of this property. Out of respect for your social, human, and emotional sentiments in the environment in which you live, Allah has given you the right to bequeath by will a third of your property to whatever and whomever you wish. You may see that there is a person who is not among your relatives, who will certainly not inherit from you, but who served you in your life, or in your illness, or in your old age, and you want to leave some of your wealth to him in recognition of his kindness; or perhaps there are people among your acquaintances whom you know to be more in need than your children, so you allot them some of the wealth, on condition that it does not exceed a third. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, willed to set a place for the faithful human emotions among people, so He left you free to dispose of a third of the estate, and then Allah, glorified is He, divided the two-thirds among the heirs.

So the statement of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿if you have believed in Allah﴾ (part of 8:41): that is, He, glorified is He, has made it part of faith that the spoils be distributed in the form that Allah, mighty and majestic is He, has specified. Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿and what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾ (part of 8:41)

Al-Furqan (the Criterion) is that which distinguishes truth from falsehood, a distinction so clear and forceful that it is evident to all. Allah has applied the name al-Furqan to the noble Qur'an in Surat Al 'Imran, where He, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel, Before, as guidance for mankind, and He sent down the Criterion﴾ (parts of 3:3-4)

When Allah, exalted is He, sent down the Torah and the Gospel, the Torah came to distinguish between truth and falsehood, and the Gospel also came to distinguish between truth and falsehood. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, willed that the word "al-Furqan" be applied only to the noble Qur'an, because the Qur'an is the final criterion after which no other criterion will come, for no other heavenly book will be sent down.

﴿and what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Criterion﴾ (part of 8:41)

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, here means by the Day of Criterion the day of Badr, which was a distinction between truth and falsehood, a conspicuous distinction that caught the attention. The word al-Furqan took on the general meaning, that of distinguishing between truth and falsehood. The Muslims were few and the disbelievers were many; the Muslims were going out to seize the caravan and the merchandise, and they had no equipment or arms for war, while the disbelievers prepared for war and fighting with numbers, equipment, and horsemen. The Muslims were wishing that the caravan of Quraysh would be theirs, a caravan guarded by only a small number of men with no strength. But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, willed that the Muslims, being few, should face an army possessing strength, that is, possessing equipment and arms; because the Muslims thought that seizing the caravan would not take them long or great effort, since its guards were limited in number and had no strong weapons. But Allah, mighty and majestic is He, willed that the believers should enter the battle while few, and that they should be victorious, so that everyone would know that this small believing group had triumphed without numbers or equipment over those who possessed the numbers and equipment. Thereby the difference between faith and disbelief appears, and between Allah's victory and the deception of Satan. Had the Muslims seized the caravan of Quraysh, it would have been said: any group of armed men could have plundered this caravan. For this reason Allah did not give them the caravan, but tested them with the nafir (the force), the army that came out of Makkah intending war and prepared for it, so as to draw attention to those believers who had gone out without intent to fight and who had triumphed over the disbelievers who had gone out for war and prepared for it. The believers numbered three hundred, and the disbelievers' army was a thousand. So when victory came, everyone was certain that the balance had tipped in favor of the believers; and if anyone wonders how this small, unarmed number could triumph over this large, armed number, they may repeat the saying of Allah, exalted is He:

﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾ (part of 8:41). This divine will is what turned the scales.

At the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, recounts for us the story of Talut (Saul) and Jalut (Goliath). It relates how the children of Israel asked a prophet of theirs that Heaven designate a person to be king over them, to lead them in a battle against a tyrant named Jalut, who had expelled them from their homes and scattered them. When the command came that Talut should be king, the children of Israel argued about his leadership over them.

﴿They said: "How can he have kingship over us when we have more right to kingship than he, and he has not been given abundance of wealth?"﴾ (part of 2:247)

It was they who asked that there be a king for them; then when Talut came, by the choice of Allah, they objected to him. Then Talut set out with those who followed him, and Allah tested them with a river while they were thirsty. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿So when Talut set out with the troops, he said: "Indeed, Allah will test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except one who scoops with his hand." But they drank from it, except a few of them﴾ (part of 2:249)

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, tested them by having them pass a river while they were thirsty, and He asked them not to drink except that each take a little water in the palm of his hand to moisten his mouth. When they reached the river, most of them rushed to gulp and drink as much as they wished, and only a minority complied with Allah's command and did not drink. These were the ones who remained with Talut and crossed the river. But when they saw the enemy's army, the majority of them said what the noble Qur'an recounts and relates to us:

﴿So when he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said: "We have no power today against Jalut and his troops."﴾ (part of 2:249)

That is, they feared to face the army of Jalut and refused to fight, except for a minority among them. Thus a purging took place twice: by choice and by trial; the first by patience against thirst, and the second by facing the enemy's army. These were the pure minority whose faith was firm, and they said what the Qur'an mentions:

﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said: "How many a small company has overcome a large company by Allah's permission! And Allah is with the steadfast."﴾ (part of 2:249). That is, this believing group that remained, which feared the reckoning of Allah in the Hereafter, was not frightened by its small number nor by the multitude of Jalut's troops; rather they said: how many a small company has overcome a large company by Allah's permission. They indeed triumphed, and this was a manifest criterion from Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

Here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾ (part of 8:41): that is, the day the host of the believers and the host of the disbelievers met, and the victory of the believers was realized despite their small number and lack of equipment. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, concludes the verse with the noble saying:

﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾ (part of 8:41): that is, Allah, mighty and majestic is He, is able to grant victory to the believers when they are few and not prepared for fighting.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 42:

The Blessed and Exalted Lord then says:

﴿When you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side, and the caravan was below you. Had you made an appointment together, you would surely have differed about the appointment. But (it was so) that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done, so that whoever perished might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lived might live upon clear evidence. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

As soon as you hear "idh" (when), you know it is an adverb of time, and its meaning is: remember this time, remember when you were on the near side (al-'Udwa al-Dunya). The 'udwa is the bank or side of a valley. It is a raised mountain, because when there is open space between mountains we call that open space a valley (wadi). Thus the valley is the space between two mountains, and the high ground on its right and left is each an 'udwa.

His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿on the near side, and they were on the far side﴾ (part of verse 42 of Surat al-Anfal)

is a clarification and explanation of the geography of the battle. The people of Islam were on the side of Madinah. His saying "dunya" is the feminine of "adna", meaning nearer, so the Muslims were close to Madinah. The disbelievers had come from Makkah and camped in the farther place.

So His saying:

﴿you were on the near side﴾ (part of verse 42 of Surat al-Anfal): that is, in a nearby place. The site of the Battle of Badr, as we know, is close to Madinah, whereas the disbelievers of Quraysh had come from Makkah. Thus they came from a place far from Madinah, and for this the Blessed and Exalted Lord named it here: ﴿the far side﴾, that is, in the place far from Makkah. The Lord, glory be to Him, continues His saying: ﴿and the caravan was below you﴾.

The "rakb" is the caravan (al-'Ir), that is, the camels carrying the merchandise, which the Muslims had gone out to seize. When Abu Sufyan learned of this, he changed the route of the caravan and turned toward the sea coast. The Blessed and Exalted Lord speaks of Abu Sufyan's conduct when he ordered the caravans to travel alongside the sea coast. The sea coast, as is well known, is always lower than any dry land. Even now the surface of the sea is taken as a measure of heights and depths relative to human measurements: it is said that a place is one hundred metres or two hundred metres or more or less above sea level. The sea coast is level relative to the sea surface, whereas land, mountains and valleys differ in height and depth, so they cannot serve as a measure of heights and depths, while the sea surface is soundly levelled, such that there is no high spot and low spot on the surface of the water.

Thus the Blessed and Exalted Lord draws our attention to the fact that the lowest part of the earth is the sea coast, and people have taken the surface of the sea as the measure of heights.

The Blessed and Exalted Lord says:

﴿Had you made an appointment together, you would surely have differed about the appointment. But (it was so) that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾ (part of verse 42 of Surat al-Anfal): that is, had the believers agreed with the disbelievers upon a time and a place, some of them would have arrived late for the appointment or deviated from the place. But Allah, may He be exalted, is the One who determined the time and place of the battle with complete precision, so the meeting took place at the appointed time and place, in order that the matter might be accomplished as Allah, may He be exalted, had decreed. The matter is the Battle of Badr, and so that the believers would meet the disbelievers and triumph over them.

﴿so that whoever perished might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lived might live upon clear evidence﴾ (part of verse 42 of Surat al-Anfal).

Does the Lord's saying ﴿whoever perished might perish﴾ mean that perishing here is dying? Some believers also died and were martyred. And the Lord's saying ﴿whoever lived might live﴾: does living here mean merely remaining alive in this world? Many of the disbelievers also lived, although they fought in the Battle of Badr. So perishing here does not mean death, and living does not mean mere survival. Rather, the Lord's saying ﴿whoever perished might perish upon clear evidence﴾ applies to the disbelievers, whether those who died or those who escaped, because the perishing here is a spiritual perishing. Whoever of the disbelievers was killed perished, and whoever escaped also perished, because by fighting the believers he cast himself into destruction, with the punishment awaiting him in the Hereafter, unless the mercy of Allah overtakes him and he believes before his term comes. Those who lived are the believers, and the meaning, then, is: that whoever disbelieved might be lost, and whoever believed might believe with certainty.

We have said before that the Blessed and Exalted Lord applies the word "life" to several meanings. There is the life in which there is movement and sensation, and this is realised the moment the soul enters the body so that the human has life. This life belongs to both believer and disbeliever. But life in this form is life that ends in a death which is not fixed in time, which we await at any moment. The life required by Allah, however, is the life in which death does not come, in which there is no weariness or misery; that is the life to come. For this reason the Blessed and Exalted Lord says:

﴿And indeed the Abode of the Hereafter, that is the true life, if they only knew﴾ (verse 64 of Surat al-'Ankabut): that is, it is the reality. So whoever believes with true faith, Allah, may He be exalted, will grant him the life of eternity in Paradise. For this reason let us all listen to the saying of the Blessed and Exalted Lord:

﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ (part of verse 24 of Surat al-Anfal).

Some of us ask: how does Allah address people as living and say to them, "when He calls you to that which gives you life"? We say: the Blessed and Exalted Lord wants for us, through faith, an everlasting life in Paradise. Then the Blessed and Exalted Lord concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾. The meaning of "Hearing" and "Knowing" is that He, may He be exalted, perceives all things and thoughts: whatever is heard by the ear He hears, whatever is seen by the eye He sees, whatever is in the breast He knows, and whatever is in any sensation of the human being He knows, because He has encompassed all things in knowledge.

The means of human cognitive perception are hearing, sight, taste, touch and smell; these are the five senses that give knowledge to the human being who knew nothing.

And He, may He be exalted, is the One who said:

﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that perhaps you would be grateful﴾ (verse 78, Surat al-Nahl): that is, these senses are what give the human being what he did not know. Whenever he knows something, let him say: Praise be to Allah.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 8, verse 43:

The Real (al-Haqq), glory be to Him and exalted is He, teaches us how His decree is carried out, so He says:

﴿When Allah shows them to you in your dream as few. And if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed over the matter, but Allah saved [you]. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ (43)

When the Real, glory be to Him and exalted is He, wills a decisive battle, He makes the impulses in each people stir them toward war, because He, glory be to Him, wants the two groups to engage, and the Real, glory be to Him, will settle the matter. And if this engagement occurred by ordinary measures, the small group might well have shrunk from facing the large group. For the battle to take place, each of the two warring sides must be certain of victory, because if either one were certain that it would be defeated, it would not have entered the battle.

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, teaches His Messenger and the believers how Allah prepared the psychological preparation for the battle: He showed the Prophet in a vision that the number of the disbelievers was small, so that the believers would be confident that they would defeat them easily. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw in his dream a vision clarifying that the number of the disbelievers was small in the eyes of the believers, and he informed his people of that. Allah made the number of the disbelievers seem small in the eyes of the believers, and made the number of the believers seem small in the eyes of the disbelievers, so that the encounter would take place and the battle would occur.

And to this the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And [recall] when He showed them to you as few in your eyes when you met, and made you few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah are [all] matters returned.﴾ [8:44]

So the believers saw the disbelievers as few, and the disbelievers saw the believers as few. Had Allah made the disbelievers numerous in the eyes of the believers, or made the believers numerous in the eyes of the disbelievers, the battle would not have taken place. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, willed to make each side appear few in the sight of the other, so that the fighting would begin. Our master ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud relates:

"I said to a neighbour of mine, 'I think they are seventy,' and he said, 'No, rather a hundred.'"

Thus the number of the disbelievers appeared few in the eyes of the believers, and the number of the believers was indeed few in the eyes of the disbelievers.

Furthermore, the Truth, glorified is He, willed that this contain a clear sign of the signs of prophethood concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for the Prophet saw the number of the disbelievers in a dream as few, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed his people of that. The battle that Allah, exalted is He, willed then took place:

﴿that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah are [all] matters returned.﴾ [part of 8:44]

The decisive matter was the meeting of the combatants in the Battle of Badr, so that Allah might distinguish between truth and falsehood, and between faith and disbelief, so that matters would be returned to Allah. Each one of the soldiers of the battle has a recompense from Allah, glorified and exalted is He: the believers have a recompense according to the measure of their intentions and sincerity in jihad, while the disbelievers incur the wrath of Allah, exalted is He. Wrath has stations, and each station of wrath is according to the conditions of its bearer. In the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, ﴿And to Allah are [all] matters returned﴾, we find the word "al-umur" (matters), which is the plural of amr (matter/command). In battles there are various kinds of commands: every soldier has a command, and there is a general command at which battles end, namely the victory of one party and the defeat of the other. In order for victory to be achieved for the believers, Allah asks them to stand firm in the battle, so He, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may succeed. [8:45]﴾

The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 8, verse 45:

Whenever you hear the word "fi'ah" (a group), know that its meaning is a body of people specially engaged in fighting in the field of battle. It is not any group at all; rather it is a cohesive body of fighters, because each fighter rallies to (yafi'u ila) his companions. Another group that is not cohesive can be dispersed by a shout or a stick, whereas fighters will not be turned away except by a force greater than theirs, and each of them tries to protect his comrade. So each of them rallies to the others.

The Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, says:

﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by God's leave.﴾ (part of verse 249, Surat al-Baqarah).

And He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿There has already been a sign for you in the two companies that met: one fighting in the way of God, and another disbelieving.﴾ (part of verse 13, Surat Al 'Imran).

So al-fi'ah is a group in war.

And His saying, exalted be He:

﴿When you meet a company, then stand firm.﴾ (part of verse 45, Surat al-Anfal).

It is meant at the time the battle occurs and fighting breaks out, because war requires first preparation, then planning which is carried out before close engagement, then going out to the place of battle. His saying, exalted be He, ﴿when you meet﴾ means that the matter has reached confrontation with the disbelievers. The Truth, Blessed and Exalted, says ﴿stand firm﴾, and steadfastness here means confrontation and courage, because when a person is steadfast in fighting, the enemy fears him and stands in awe of him; if he is not so, he will be forced to retreat, and this is what emboldens the disbelievers against you.

Since you have come to fight, your enemies must witness your courage, for if you flee, that is a testimony of weakness against you.

Therefore there must be training in steadfastness and fighting, and this is the advance preparation for war: with strong training and precise planning, and that none of you turns his back and flees at the moment of the advance, for this act is among the greatest of the major sins. The Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless swerving for battle or joining a company, has indeed earned anger from God.﴾ (part of verse 16, Surat al-Anfal). "Yuwallihim" means "gives them", and "dubura" means "his back", and this is a condemnation of the act of fleeing, because the back is the place of protection and safeguarding. We know that someone said to Imam 'Ali, may God honour his face: "Your coat of mail has a front but no back," meaning that the coat of mail protects your chest, but behind you there is no part of the mail to protect your back. He said: ﴿No, I would not be if I let my opponent reach my back.﴾ That is, he, may God honour his face, preferred martyrdom to letting his opponent reach his back. Had his coat of mail been both in front and behind, he would have had in his intention to let his opponent reach his back; therefore he made the coat protect only the chest, and he was certain he would never turn his back to his enemy. They call this other situation "the phenomenon of self-restraint", meaning it is a way of preventing the thing from happening even if it happens in a time of hardship, because the fighter who enters the battle while protecting only his chest does not turn to flee, since he knows that if he turned, he would expose his back to them, they would be able to reach him, and he would be killed.

When the Truth, glorified be He, says ﴿stand firm﴾, He does not demand this steadfastness in an absolute sense, but He wants the believers to be steadfast and strong in fighting. However, if the company the believers face is large in number or abundant in equipment, that requires study and preparation, and here the Truth demanded steadfastness so that the believers would know with certainty that they do not face their enemy with their own strength, but with the strength of God for whose sake they strive. Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿And remember God much﴾, meaning: remember, while you fight, that God is with you with His help and victory. If your means cannot bring victory, the Creator of means can, by His power, bring victory.

We all know that the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, has placed means in His creation. When we exhaust our means, we turn to the Creator of means. That is why we find that whoever does not believe in God, when his means fail him, kills himself, collapses completely, or goes mad; but the believer says: when my means fail me, the Lord of means and its Creator is with me, and he takes refuge in a firm support.

If a small child is attacked by someone, he says: I have a father or a brother who will repel the harm from me, because means do not give him the power to respond. How then should one whose Lord's power is above the power of the whole universe, and whose strength is always present, not do so? That is why we find the people of Moses, when they reached the shore of the sea and found the water before them, and looked behind them and saw Pharaoh's soldiers approaching from afar, said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken.﴾

They were logical in what they said: the sea was before them and the enemy behind them, and they had no way of escape by using the ordinary means in this universe. But Moses, peace be upon him, by the strength of his faith in God, Exalted, said what came on his tongue in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿He said, "No!"﴾ That is, Pharaoh and his soldiers will not overtake us; the people of Moses did not understand, because the sea was before them and Pharaoh's soldiers behind them. Our master Moses, peace be upon him, added with full voice the words:

﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ (part of verse 62, Surat al-Shu'ara'). That is, he raised the matter from the means to the Causer, and behold, God commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, and it split, and dry land appeared. The Children of Israel crossed the sea, and when Moses and his people reached the shore of the sea after they had crossed, Moses wanted to strike the sea again so that the water would return to its former course, and Pharaoh's soldiers could not catch up with them. But God, glorified and exalted, said to Moses:

﴿And leave the sea as it is, at rest; indeed, they are an army to be drowned.﴾ (verse 24, Surat al-Dukhan). That is, do not hasten to strike the sea so that it returns to its course; leave it as it is, still, for what God saved the Children of Israel by will drown the family of Pharaoh. Thus with one thing He both saved and destroyed, and none can do this but Him, glorified and exalted.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿O you who have believed, when you meet a company, then stand firm and remember God much that you may succeed.﴾ (verse 45, Surat al-Anfal).

He, glorified and exalted, is the Creator of the human soul and is the One who knows it when it faces a power it did not reckon with, and how the soul suffers great distress, especially in the field of battle. Therefore He asked the believers to remember always that they are not alone in the battle and that He, glorified and exalted, is with them. Let them remember this often, so that their victory over their enemy continues; for when they persist in remembering God, Exalted, this remembrance strengthens their faith and places in their hearts the courage necessary to achieve victory.

The word "much" (kathiran) in the Truth's remembrance here means that a person may remember God only in despair, and if ease comes afterwards, he may forget the remembrance of God. Therefore, glorified and exalted, He emphasises here that the remembrance of God should be much, so that God's victory for the believer over his enemy continues. An example of this: we find that when He, glorified and exalted, summons the believers to prayer on Friday, He says:

﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew. And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God; and remember God much that you may succeed.﴾ (verses 9–10, Surat al-Jumu'ah).

The Truth, glorified and exalted, asks this of the believers, while He knows that they devote themselves to Him, glorified be He, five times every day.

Then after the Friday prayer He commands them to disperse in the land and seek the bounty of God, and He alerts us to persist in His remembrance, as if He is saying: beware lest your works and worldly interests distract you from the remembrance of God, or that you think the remembrance of God is only in the mosque or at the time of prayer. Rather, persist in the remembrance of God in all the events of life. If you do this and remember God much, you will be among the successful. To remember God much means that you feel at every moment that God, glorified and exalted, is with you, so you fear Him, praise Him, and seek His help. In this way the connection between you and God, Mighty and Majestic, is constant at all times.

An example of this is what happened in 1973 in the Battle of the Tenth of Ramadan. The remembrance of God filled the hearts, and the soldiers drew from their saying "God is greatest" an immense energy with which they confronted the enemy, and they stormed the "Bar-Lev Line." God aided them with a reinforcement of faith from Him, and placed in the soul of each of them an immense energy by which victory was achieved; this was through excellent training and constant remembrance of God, Exalted.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says after that:

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾ (8:46)

We have already known that obedience to Allah, the Exalted, is embodied in carrying out what He commanded in the manhaj (the methodology), and that obedience to the Messenger is practical obedience in conduct, and it is also obedience to Allah, because the Messenger conveys from his Lord. The one who obeys must keep away from disputing with his fellow believers, because dispute is the opposition of forces: there exists one force opposing another force, and opposing forces waste each other's energy. Thus the opposition between two forces wastes the energy of each of them, so that each force becomes weak and ineffective. So be one hand, for if you dispute, your strength will be lost and you will meet with failure, meaning you will achieve nothing of what you want, because you have squandered your strength in disputing, and you will no longer have a strength with which to achieve what you want, and your "wind" (ريح, rih) will depart in this case. Failure (فشل, fashal) is a person's falling short of the task he had hoped of himself.

And observe the expression of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ﴾ (part of 8:46)

We know that "rih" (wind) is applied to the air whose space is the expanse over the surface of the earth. So the place of air is any empty place on the surface of the earth. That is why we find that a column made of cement and iron, for example, contains no air, because there is no empty space in it; but the gaps between the columns contain air, because there is empty space in them. We know that the requisites of life are food, drink and air, but air is the first requisite of life, for you cannot endure being without air for the length of an inhalation and exhalation.

So air is the first requisite of your life and the life of everyone in this universe. As long as air surrounds a thing in such a way that pressure is equal from all its sides, the thing remains stable; but if you remove the air from one side, the air pressure will act to shatter that thing. In school experiments we witnessed the effect of air pressure: they would bring us a tin in which water was placed, and they would leave it to boil on the fire, so the water vapour expels the air present in the empty part of the tin, and the vapour fills this empty space. Then they seal the tin tightly and pour cold water over it from the outside; the vapour condenses, its volume decreases, and a part of the tin becomes empty of air, so the walls of the tin collapse inward because of the pressure of the air outside the walls and the evacuation of air inside the tin. That is why we find that when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wishes to punish a people or bring punishment upon them, He sends a wind upon them. He says, exalted is He:

﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind; He subjected it against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people in it fallen as if they were trunks of hollow palm trees.﴾ (69:6-7)

And likewise we find Him, glorified and exalted, saying:

﴿This is a cloud approaching us [bringing rain]; rather, it is that for which you were impatient: a wind containing painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord.﴾ (46:24-25)

And also the Truth, glorified is He, speaks of the wind that drowns with its high waves:

﴿Until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, there comes upon them a stormy wind and the waves come at them from everywhere, and they assume that they have been encompassed.﴾ (10:22)

So the word "rih" expresses the destructive force of the air, for when the wind's force and direction unite, it becomes destructive. But if another wind meets it, balance occurs between the two forces. That is why, when the Truth uses the word "rih," He speaks of it only for ruin and destruction. But when He speaks of it for good, He says "riyah" (winds) in the plural, because the multiplicity of the directions of the winds is what establishes balance in life. So when Allah, glorified is He, wishes to destroy with wind, He brings it from one direction, so that the force of the wind on one side has no other wind-force from the opposite direction to counterbalance it.

﴿And it is He who sends the winds as heralds before His mercy﴾ (25:48)

And He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And We send the winds fertilizing﴾ (15:22):

That is, the winds carry pollen between plants, so pollination occurs, fruits grow, and good comes. But there is one verse in which the word "rih" came and carried good, in His saying:

﴿Until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it﴾ (10:22).

And when He, glorified and exalted, used the word "rih" in this verse, He described it as ﴿good﴾ (طيبة, tayyibah). And here in the verse He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your "rih" depart﴾ (8:46).

And "rihakum" means your strength, because the "rih" here means the force that destroys your enemy. We know that in the past ships were sailed by the power of the wind, and when science advanced and steam and electricity came, the sail of vessels was abolished and engines that propel the ship's motion were used instead.

The word "rih" is also applied to a smell, so one says: ﴿a fragrant scent﴾ (rih 'atirah). This scent remains in a place even after the one who used it has left it, and every one of us has a distinctive scent, just as every person has a distinctive fingerprint, though we cannot distinguish it; but trained dogs can distinguish a person's particular scent, so the dog comes, smells the person's scent, and follows him to the place he went. Or it can pick him out from among dozens of people. The scent of one person does not mix with that of another despite their being in one place; otherwise a trained dog could not distinguish the scent of a particular person among the dozens of people present.

As for the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted: ﴿and your rih departs﴾, it means that you will come to an end and no trace of you will remain; for as long as you have a trace on the earth, you have a "rih" that distinguishes you. That is the one which, as we said, trained dogs can distinguish. But when a person dies and is buried, he has no scent. The noble Qur'an guides us to this when it speaks of the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him, when his brothers threw him into the well. A caravan found him, then the king of Egypt bought him, then he entered prison and came out and became the 'Aziz of Egypt. His brothers came to him, and Yusuf, peace be upon him, gave them his shirt to cast upon the face of his father Ya'qub, so that he would regain his sight, after grief had taken away his sight. The Truth says about the departure of the caravan from Egypt toward Syria, where our master Ya'qub lived:

﴿And when the caravan departed, their father said: Indeed, I perceive the scent of Yusuf, if you did not think me senile﴾ (12:94). That is, when the caravan came out of the buildings, which can block the scent by the strength of their mass, for buildings have emanations that may block and conceal the scent; and after the caravan was in the open, Ya'qub, peace be upon him, perceived the scent of his son Yusuf from the shirt they were carrying: ﴿He said: Indeed, I perceive the scent of Yusuf, if you did not think me senile.﴾

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted, concludes the verse about which we are reflecting:

﴿And be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ (8:46).

This is the completion of the picture which Allah wants us to notice: He commanded them to stand firm in fighting, and fighting requires strength, non-dispute, and patience in hardships; especially if your enemy is patient and fierce in might.

So in battle, Allah, mighty and majestic, wants the believers to stand firm in fighting and not flee, to remember Allah much, and not to dispute, lest the strength of the believers be lost; and He, glorified is He, enjoins them to patience, for their enemy may have patience and endurance, so the believer must possess a reserve of endurance and patience that enables him to defeat his enemy. The quality of patience indicates competition. It is taken from when they would dive under water: the one who stays under water longer than the other has greater endurance. That is why our master 'Abbas and our master 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, entered into a competition in diving. He said to him: "Compete with me," that is, let us see who will remain under water longer. And "sabir" (patient) means one who bears more in difficult situations and endures with patience beyond the endurance of his opponents. The Truth, mighty and majestic, says here:

﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ (8:46), by which He, glorified and exalted, establishes that every believer must feel that Allah, blessed and exalted, is the One who has appointed him to carry out this fighting mission, and He is with him; so his soul does not weaken, for the weak, when he takes refuge in the strong, is given courage and the capacity to endure, just like a small child: if he walks in the street alone, other children may attack him, but if he walks with his father, no one approaches him. So what of the person who is with his Lord? Therefore the Truth enjoins every fighter to remember that he is in the company of his Lord, and that no harmful event in the universe can reach him, however weak he may be, because the power of Allah is with him.

It is therefore related that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Allah, mighty and majestic, will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me." He will say: "O Lord, how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He will say: "Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him? O son of Adam, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me." He will say: "O Lord, how could I feed You, when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He will say: "Did not My servant so-and-so ask you for food and you did not feed him? Did you not know that if you had fed him, you would have found that with Me? O son of Adam, I asked you for drink and you did not give Me drink." He will say: "O Lord, how could I give You drink, when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He will say: "My servant so-and-so asked you for drink and you did not give him drink. Had you given him drink, you would have found that with Me."¹ So when a person falls ill, his well-being is taken from him, and he cannot walk or move, but lies on his bed in pain; and the Truth, glorified and exalted, makes clear to us that the one from whom well-being is taken, which is a blessing, is with Me. Therefore beware of panicking when a blessing leaves you, as long as the Bestower is with you. The believing patient senses that Allah is with him.

When a Muslim is in the company of Allah, the measures of matter and of human calculation do not apply at all. The example is the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and Abu Bakr in the cave. The disbelievers came to the entrance of the cave, and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, saw them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looked beneath his feet, he would see us." This is a logical statement from a material perspective, for if one of those disbelievers bent down and looked into the mouth of the cave, he would see the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and Abu Bakr. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, wished to reassure Abu Bakr and remove from him what had come to his mind, that the disbelievers might see them. It would have been expected that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "O Abu Bakr, be at ease; they will not look inside the cave." But the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "What do you think of two whose third is Allah?" Concerning this, Imam Ahmad narrated from Anas that Abu Bakr told him: "I said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, while we were in the cave: 'If one of them looked at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet.' He said: 'O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is Allah?'"²

Since Allah is their third, the company is present; and if you are in the company of One whom eyes cannot perceive, can eyes perceive you? Certainly not: the eyes of enemies and opponents cannot perceive you. O Allah, make us always in Your company.

¹ Narrated by Imam Muslim (al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib, vol. 4, p. 317).
² Related by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Exalted Lord completes what He wills to prevent the believers from being in the hours of hardship, so He says, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people, and who averted [others] from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾ (8:47):

"Those who went forth from their homes insolently" are the disbelievers, when they learned that Abu Sufyan had escaped with the caravan and the Muslims had not been able to seize it. They had set out from Makkah to rescue the caravan from the hands of the Muslims. So when it was said to them that the caravan had been saved under the leadership of Abu Sufyan, "Turn back," they said: "This is not enough for us. Rather, we must go out and fight Muhammad and those with him, and defeat them, and beat the drums and slaughter the sacrificial animals, so that the people of the Peninsula will know the news of Muhammad's defeat and his companions, and none of them will dare to attack one of our caravans."

Thus, they were not content that their wealth had been returned to them; rather, they wanted more than the situation required. They wanted to go out in a misguided demonstration, for boasting and arrogance, to establish that they had strength.

The rescue of the caravan should have sufficed them and the matter would have ended. They should have turned back, but they wanted to stage a demonstration for which there was no necessity.

So the matter is one of gloating, and this is a form of *batar* (insolence, ungratefulness toward blessings): that you have a blessing but do not appreciate it its due worth, and you want to rise above it. It is said, "So-and-so is *bataran*" when they bring him breakfast of, for example, fava beans, and he says: "He wants jam, butter and honey." Likewise the disbelievers of Quraysh did: they were not content with the rescue of the caravan, but belittled this blessing, were not satisfied with it, and sought more.

As for His words, exalted is He, *"wa ri'a' al-nas"* (and to be seen by people): that is, they intended by the war with the Messenger of Allah and those who believed the reputation among people, and that the Arabs would know that they went out to Madinah and fought Muhammad and his companions, so that they would have a reputation and awe among people in the Arabian Peninsula.

As for His words, exalted is He:

﴿and who averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾ (part of 8:47): because when people see the disbelievers, who are opposed to the method of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), and power has come to them, dancing and singing over their victory, while they see the Muslims hidden and fearful of facing the disbelievers, this will entice people to follow the method of disbelief. Thus the disbelievers, by their desire to fight the Messenger of Allah and his companions, are in effect averting [people] from the way of Allah. Then the Exalted Lord comes to clarify: do not suppose that they are far from My knowledge.

﴿And Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾ (part of 8:47): that is, Allah, exalted is He, encompasses all their deeds; not a single action of what they do escapes Him. He completely encompasses them, and they cannot escape from Him.

And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them and said, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector." But when the two hosts came in sight of each other, he turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment." (8:48)

The Almighty wishes to draw our attention to the role of Satan and his helpers and what he does to the disbelievers. So the Blessed and Exalted says:

[Quran 8:48 repeated]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the disbelievers in his dream as few, and this was from the making of Allah the Exalted, so that the battle might be accomplished. Satan began to make the disbelievers' deeds seem fair to them and to praise them, and to delude them, saying: "You are many, and there is no one like you in the arts of war, and you will obtain victory in the twinkling of an eye." But the Almighty wanted to firm up the believers and strengthen them, and therefore Allah the Exalted willed to show the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the disbelievers as few. In reality they were few, because victory does not lie in numbers but in the support of Allah the Exalted, and however many the disbelievers are, before the support of Allah they are few. Satan tries to make the fighting against the believers seem fair to the disbelievers, that is, to make it beloved to their souls, and that they will achieve victory and become the talk of all the Arabian Peninsula, and people will fear and dread them, and they will become the great ones and the men of authority. Thus Satan portrayed to them the act of fighting the Muslims in forms beloved to their hearts. Here we clearly see the stupidity of Satan and his inability to know the decree of Allah. Had he known what the battle of Badr would end in, he would not have made the disbelievers' entry into battle seem fair, because the battle ended in victory for the Muslims and the killing of the chieftains of Quraysh, and the image of the believers rose throughout the whole Arabian Peninsula. Victory was not what Satan wanted; rather, out of his ignorance, he made the battle seem fair to the disbelievers.

On this the Almighty says:

[Quran 8:48 fragment: "And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them and said, 'No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector'"] (part of verse 48, Surat al-Anfal): That is, Satan's whispering to the disbelievers was in the form of magnifying their strength, that none would overcome them in their fighting at Badr, and that he—that is, Satan—would support them in the battle and protect them if any harm befell them. But does Satan have authority to help the disbelievers? We know that Satan has no authority except to adorn (evil) only. How, then, could he have authority over the outcome of the confrontation between truth and falsehood? On the Day of Judgment Satan will come, and the disbelievers will ask him to protect them from the punishment of Allah the Exalted, because he is the one who misled them, made their evil deeds seem fair to them, and dragged them to the path of the Fire. He will then disown them and say to them:

[Quran 14:22 fragment: "I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me."] (part of verse 22, Surat Ibrahim): That is, he says to the disbelievers: "I did not compel you to sins, so I had no authority of compulsion over you to force you to do anything, nor authority of argument to convince you to commit sins. Rather, as soon as I called you, you responded to me, because you desired disobedience and the pursuit of your desires." As for His words, "I cannot help you (musrikhikum)," one who cries out for help (asrakha fulanan) means he heard his cry and went to him to rescue him. When a person faces a power greater than himself, he cries out, hoping someone will hear his cry and come to his aid. The one who hears the cry either is weak and does not respond, since he cannot rescue the one facing danger, or is strong and goes to his aid; thus it is said "asrakhahu," meaning he rescued him and removed the cause of his cry. As for the Exalted's words, relating what Satan says, "I cannot help you," meaning Satan cannot save them from the punishment or rescue them from it, removing the cause of their cry: "nor can you help me."

That is, you are unable to repel the punishment from me.

Satan kept adorning their deeds for them and falsely promising them that he would protect them and back them in their victory, until the believers and the disbelievers drew close to one another and came within sight of each other.

[Quran 8:48 fragment: "But when the two hosts came in sight of each other, he turned back on his heels and said, 'Indeed, I am free of you'"] (part of verse 48, Surat al-Anfal): That is, the moment the two groups came into view of each other, before they joined battle and fighting began, Satan fled, disowned the disbelievers, and ran far away. This is what Allah the Exalted explains in His words:

[Quran 59:16: "Like the example of Satan when he says to man, 'Disbelieve.' But when he has disbelieved, he says, 'Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'"] (Surat al-Hashr).

This is consistent with Satan's situation when Allah expelled and cursed him, because he refused to carry out the command to prostrate to Adam. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to him:

[Quran 38:78: "And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense."] (Surat Sad).

Then Satan humbly implored Allah to let him remain until the Day of Resurrection:

[Quran 7:14: "He said, 'Reprieve me until the day they are resurrected.'"] (Surat al-A'raf).

Thus Satan acknowledged the absolute power of Allah the Exalted and that he was helpless, unable to do anything before the might of Allah. The Truth, Blessed and Exalted, said:

[Quran 15:37-38: "He said, 'Indeed, you are among those reprieved, until the day of the time well known.'"] (Surat al-Hijr).

So Satan has no power and no ability to do anything; all he can do is deceive, adorn, and lie. That is why he kept deceiving the disbelievers and lying to them. And as soon as the believers and the disbelievers came within sight of one another, Satan fled in terror, turned back on his heels, and declared his fear of Allah, because he knew that Allah is severe in punishment.

Therefore, the source of Satan's fear here is fear of the punishment and the torment that will certainly befall him, and Satan did not flee out of love for Allah the Exalted.
