Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, presents us with another image:

﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "Their religion has deluded these," and whoever puts his trust in Allah, indeed Allah is Almighty, Wise (49)﴾:

"Al-munafiq" (the hypocrite) is a word derived from nafaqa'the yarbu' (the escape-hole of the jerboa). The yarbu' is an animal resembling a mouse that lives in the mountains in burrows. When another animal pursues it to devour it, it hurries to its burrow, which resembles a tunnel, and it opens more than one opening for this burrow so that it has exits. Such openings are like back doors, and by them it escapes being devoured. It is as if it has opened for itself a tunnel from which it slips away, so that others cannot catch up with it. For this reason, we find the hypocrite in conflict with himself: his tongue utters what he does not believe, whereas the believer is harmonious within himself, his tongue uttering what is in his heart. The disbeliever too is likewise harmonious, his tongue uttering what is in his heart of disbelief. But the hypocrite is torn within himself: his tongue says the words of faith while his heart harbours disbelief. Thus the faculties of the hypocrite are at odds, and when the heart and the tongue are at odds there is no peace of mind. Enough of the hypocrite is that his faculties are in conflict.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, describes the hypocrites with His saying:

﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "We are truly with you; we were only mocking."﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah) (2:14).

So the self is lost, for a person does not lose his self when his faculties are harmonious and no faculty opposes another, and his action is balanced. But the one whose faculties are at odds lives always in psychological anxiety and bewilderment. Therefore he tries to flee from his reality, resorting to drugs or other things. The solution is not for a person to numb himself in the face of events; rather, a person must confront events and seek a solution for them. The hypocrite cannot do that, so he collapses. Allah the Exalted says:

﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "Their religion has deluded these"﴾ (part of verse 49, Surat al-Anfal).

After the believers are victorious, you find them increasing in faith and in confidence in themselves, and filled with the might of faith, so the hypocrites look at them with envy and malice, because they hate the believers and do not wish them any good. In their hypocrisy they are disbelievers; there is rancour in their hearts toward the believers. They address one another, saying: "These people have been afflicted by delusion through their religion." But what befell the believers is not delusion, because the meaning of delusion (ghurur) is that you are dazzled by a quality in yourself that makes you superior to others. The believer, at the moment of victory, is not conceited with himself; rather he takes pride in God, the Strong, the Mighty, and grows more humble before Him, occupied with thanking God for the victory He has granted him. The conceited person, by contrast, is one who detaches the blessing from the Giver and attributes it to himself. The believers attribute everything to God, blessed and exalted is He, because they know that blessings are a gift from the outstretched hand of God, with blessings that cannot be counted or enumerated. As long as the blessing has not distanced a person from God, God increases him in it, because He entrusts him with the blessing and attributes it to its Owner. The conceited person boasts of any quality by which he is distinguished, unlike the believer, who never boasts of it, because he knows that he has no self-sufficiency of his own and that the favour belongs to God Most High. On this, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says, describing the believers:

﴿Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ (part of verse 29, Surat al-Fath). Severity here is not conceit; it is a disposition and a faculty. Had it been conceit, it would have remained as it is. But the believer is severe toward the disbelievers and humble toward the believers, never arrogant toward them. His faith does not place him in a rigid mould, because faith gives believers flexibility in the face of events. Thus we find that the believer is neither severe absolutely, for there are situations that call for mercy in dealing with believers, nor merciful absolutely, for there are situations that call for severity in confronting disbelievers.

Our master Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was known for weeping much out of his fear and awe of Allah, and his heart was full of mercy toward the believers. But when the wars of apostasy broke out against those who withheld zakat, what happened? He and Umar ibn al-Khattab sat together consulting one another, and Umar was known to be stern. Umar's opinion was that they should not fight those who had apostatised by denying and withholding zakat, because they said: "There is no god but Allah." Abu Bakr said to him: "By Allah, I will surely fight whoever separates prayer from zakat, for zakat is the right of wealth. By Allah, if they withhold from me a cord which they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would fight them over withholding it."

This is Abu Bakr, who was known for weeping much out of fear of Allah, and whose heart was filled with mercy for the believers. He declares with strength and severity in the truth that he will fight those who transgress the bounds of Allah and who withhold and deny zakat. Had this been said by Umar, people would have said: "We are accustomed to that severity." But that this should come from this gentle, merciful man, naturally disposed to tenderness and softness, shows us the severity of the believer in confronting disbelief.

The believer, then, is neither naturally disposed to absolute severity nor to absolute mercy; rather, he is severe when severity is required for the religion, merciful when mercy is required for the religion, mighty when might is required for the religion, and humble when humility is required for the religion. Thus the statement of the hypocrites, ﴿Their religion has deluded these﴾, is not based on sound judgement; rather it is dictated to them by their hypocrisy. Why?

Because the believers always put their trust in Allah and attribute all favour to Allah Most High:

﴿Indeed Allah is Almighty, Wise﴾ (part of verse 49, Surat al-Anfal).

Since Allah is Almighty, the one who believes in Him is mighty, and He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ (part of verse 8, Surat al-Munafiqun).

And since Allah is Wise, He gives wisdom to the believers. Trust in Allah (tawakkul) means that you entrust all your affairs to Him, glorified and exalted is He. The first of these affairs is that He has commanded you to take the means (al-asbab), so never abandon the means; rather take them always along with trust in Him. If they do not avail you, there is the Causer of causes (al-musabbib). The Truth, blessed and exalted, has said to His believing servants:

﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them at your hands﴾ (part of verse 14, Surat al-Tawbah).

And Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded us to strive, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿So walk in its broad paths and eat of His provision﴾ (part of verse 15, Surat al-Mulk).

Thus He, glorified and exalted, just as He commanded the believers to fight and take the means, because He wills to punish the disbelievers by the hands of the believers, has also commanded them to strive in pursuit of provision.

When you rely passively, you transfer a quality into another quality, for trust (tawakkul) is an act of the hearts, and action is performed by the limbs (al-jawarih), so do not make passivity (tawakul in the sense of inaction) the act of the limbs, since the limbs act through means. The hearts trust in Allah. Thus we understand that true trust for the limbs is that you act; therefore action and taking the means are necessary along with trust. We must also take note of the hypocrites at Badr, of whom Allah, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "Their religion has deluded these"﴾ (part of verse 49, Surat al-Anfal).

The hypocrites, as we have said, are the people whose faculties are in conflict, and what is on their tongues contradicts what is in their breasts. As for those in whose hearts is a disease, they are people of weak faith: Muslims in times of ease, deserters from religion in times of hardship. So there are two groups that the Truth, glorified and exalted, has mentioned: the hypocrites, and these, who were from the Aws and the Khazraj, whose faculties were in conflict because they wanted lordship over Madinah. One of them had been expecting to wear the crown of kingship, but with the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah this opportunity ended for him, and the chance of kingship and leadership was lost, which produced in him resentment and rage. But the phenomenon of the people of Madinah entirely turning to faith and entering Islam made these hypocrites unable to resist; so they uttered the two testimonies with their tongues, while rancour and enmity toward Islam remained in their hearts. Thus each of them was pulled between two opposing directions.

Those in whose hearts is a disease are not hypocrites, but they are weak in Islam. They entered the religion to take but not to give: when Islam gave them some of the blessings of this world they rejoiced in them, and when hardship befell them they fled. Among them were some who had embraced Islam in Makkah. But their Islam did not bring them to the point of migrating to Madinah, out of fear that they would leave behind their wealth and children, so they remained in Makkah. These sick-hearted people did not lose life, for disease does not destroy life, but they suffered from the unsoundness of their faith. When the matter of fighting came at the battle of Badr, they consulted: Should they go with the disbelievers or not? And with which of the two sides should they fight? They said: "We will go out with the disbelievers; if we find that they are stronger we will be with them, and if we find the Muslims are the stronger we will join them."

Among these were Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Ali ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-As ibn Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj, al-Harith ibn Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and Abu al-Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughirah. These gathered together and went out to the battle, to join whichever side would prevail, whether believer or disbeliever. They took this stance because soundness of faith was absent from their hearts; they were people of sick hearts, attached to the love of this world. What the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said indicates a desire to avoid harm, even though these were in Madinah and those were in Makkah; yet they said one and the same thing, and this is evidence that the seduction of Satan over the two groups was one and the same. For this reason the expression was unified, and both said: ﴿Their religion has deluded these﴾.

The two groups (the group of hypocrites and the group of those in whose hearts is a disease) said it despite the difference of place, for some of them, as we have learned, were from Makkah and some from Madinah. So there must have been a common factor that made them speak with one voice, namely that Satan whispered this expression to them. Therefore it was incumbent upon them to notice that agreement of speech is evidence of Satan's seduction of them.

As for the meaning of ﴿Their religion has deluded these﴾: "gharrartu fulanan" means I adorned the matter for him in such a way that he embraces it with an eagerness his strength does not warrant, and I strengthened his readiness to carry it out. For example, if you come to a man of limited income and want to tempt him to buy a car, you say, to make the matter attractive to him: "Borrow from so-and-so and so-and-so, and pay the rest in installments," as if you are tempting him to adopt a position other than the one he had intended.

But what is the sense of delusion regarding religion?

The believers who were deluded by their religion sensed their numerousness, though their number was small. They advanced to war on the strength of the vision Allah, glorified and exalted, showed to His Messenger (ﷺ) that the number of the disbelievers was small, and on the strength of Allah's promise of victory to them; or they were deluded by being told that whoever is killed in this battle becomes a martyr and is granted an everlasting life. This made the strong among them and the weak fight with vigour, because the martyr will go to Paradise. Thus, in the opinion of the hypocrites, the believers were deluded by their religion.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, answers them with His saying:

﴿And whoever puts his trust in Allah, indeed Allah is Almighty, Wise﴾ (part of verse 49, Surat al-Anfal).

This is the answer to them: the believers will not be deluded by their religion; rather they are reliant upon Allah, and whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him and suffices him. He, glorified is He, is Mighty and cannot be overcome, and Wise, placing defeat in its place and victory in its place.

So the matter is that these believers chose Allah, and He honoured and granted them victory.

But was this phrase spoken openly by the hypocrites? No, they did not dare to declare it openly...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 8, verse 50:

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿And if you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs, [saying]: "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾

The one addressed by this discourse is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The meaning is: if We were to unveil the unseen for you, you would see. And you notice that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, left out the response, so He did not say what happens to this disbeliever while the angels are striking him. When the response is omitted, you leave it to the imagination of each person to picture what happened in its most horrific form. Had Allah, glorified and exalted, given its response, He would have specified for us what happens; but leaving out the response makes each of us imagine a strange matter that does not occur to the mind, and this is an expression of the horror of what will happen.

The image here moves us from the punishment of the disbelievers in this world to the hour of death.

"Yatawaffa" means: at the moment the angels seize the souls of the disbelievers. The tawaffi (taking/seizing of souls) is sometimes attributed to Allah, glorified and exalted, in accordance with His saying: ﴿And He is the One who takes you back (yatawaffakum)﴾; sometimes it is attributed to the messengers from Allah: ﴿Our messengers take him back (tawaffathu rusulunā)﴾; and sometimes it is attributed to the Angel of Death, who is 'Izra'il: ﴿Say: The Angel of Death will take you back (yatawaffakum malak al-mawt)﴾. Thus the taking has been attributed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sometimes to 'Izra'il, and sometimes to the angels of death. We say: there is no contradiction among these statements, because the matter in every case proceeds from Allah, glorified and exalted; either 'Izra'il carries it out, or his soldiers, who are many, do.

The original command, therefore, is from Allah; it is attributed to the direct recipient from Allah, who is 'Izra'il; and it is attributed to those whom the Angel of Death asks to carry out these operations. This punishment occurs at the moment of death agony (al-ihtidar), the moment in which a person does not deceive himself, because a person may deceive himself in this world. He may be sick with an incurable illness and say: "I will recover tomorrow," giving himself hope of life; or he may be poor, possessing nothing of worldly means, and say: "I will become rich." For a person is always overcome by hope, except at the hour of death agony. This is a moment in which every dying person is certain that he is truly dying and that there is no escape from meeting Allah. That is why you find that one who wronged a person, at the moment of dying, says to his children: "Bring me so-and-so; I wronged him, so return to him his rights from me and what I wronged him in." A person at the moment of death agony sees the whole reel of his deeds. If he was a believer, he sees a luminous reel, so he smiles and welcomes death with tranquility. But if his deeds were evil, he sees darkness, and terror and fear take hold of him, because he has recognized his destiny.

When Satan made the disbelievers' deeds appear fair to them, promising them victory and saying: "I will protect you when the tide turns against you," and when the two groups came within sight of each other, Satan fled, because he saw what the disbelievers did not see of the might of Allah. This is always Satan's position: when he sees the might of Allah, he hastens to flee, and he acknowledges that all his speech to the son of Adam is only a false promise, its cause being the spite in his heart; because he received the punishment from Allah, glorified and exalted, after he refused to carry out Allah's command to prostrate to Adam, and that is what made the punishment he will face obligatory. We see Satan, for example, as the Truth informs us in His saying:

﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾ (Surah Sad, 38:82). That is, he swore by His majesty and might. The meaning of Allah's might is that He is free of need from all His creatures; He needs none of them. He is Allah, with the majesty and beauty of His attributes, before He brought any of His creation into existence; He created this universe and brought it into being without seeking help from anyone. Even if all people believed in Him, that would add nothing to His dominion; even if all people disbelieved in Him, that would subtract nothing from His dominion. Iblis swore by Allah's might, acknowledging it. He swore by the might of Allah that he would seek to lead man astray, because Allah, glorified and exalted, since His dominion neither increases nor decreases by the faith of His creatures, gave them freedom of choice. Had Allah willed people to be believers, Iblis would not have been able to approach any of them. Iblis, out of his spite toward man and his hatred of him, tries to turn him away from the path of faith. But does Iblis possess power to mislead a believer? No. Therefore there is an exception:

﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ (Surah Sad, 38:83). That is, Iblis cannot approach a sincere believing servant in his faith. Therefore we must attend to the words of Satan that came on his tongue in the noble verse:

﴿Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment﴾ (part of verse 48, Surah al-Anfal, 8).

So then, since Iblis fears Allah, and since he knows that Allah is severe in punishment, what removed this fear from him when Allah commanded him to prostrate to Adam, and he disobeyed? Especially since he knows that Allah is severe in punishment. And if he had known that Allah does not punish, or punishes with a light punishment, we would say that the simplicity of the punishment tempted him to disobey. But his knowledge of the severity of the punishment should have pushed him to obedience all the more.

We say: at the moment of arrogance, Iblis forgot everything!

For when arrogance seizes you, you become haughty even in situations of hardship, even if you know that a severe punishment may befall you; yet all of this disappears from your soul when arrogance enters it. That is why you may find a person being beaten severely, yet his arrogance makes him neither cry out nor scream. And we find a person who, in a moment of arrogance, makes a decision with grave consequences, yet bears it. When Iblis refused to carry out the command to prostrate, he was filled with arrogance and pride, and his conceit made him disdain Allah's command, so he said:

﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 17:61).

So, at the moment of arrogance Iblis forgot everything, and he rushed into his disobedience, filled with self-conceit, and insisted on disobedience despite his knowledge that Allah is severe in punishment.

And in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And if you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs, [saying]: "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ (Surah al-Anfal, 8:50).

We find that the response of "law" (lo) has been omitted. The meaning is: if the veil were lifted and you saw the angels taking the souls of those who disbelieve, you would see a great and dreadful matter. Does this happen at the time of battle, when the disbelievers are killed in the fighting and the angels greet them with blows, or does this happen at the moment of natural death? Both are true, and this punishment takes the form of their facing the blows and attempting to flee. That is why Allah, the Truth, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿striking their faces and their backs...﴾ (8:50). The one of them who advances, they strike on his face; when he turns his face to avoid the blow, they strike his back. The disbelievers used to torture the believers in this manner: the believer who approached them they struck on the face, and if he tried to flee they struck him on the back and on the head.

Allah makes the disbelievers taste what they used to do to the believers. But the difference is that the striker among the disbelievers struck with limited human strength, whereas the striker among the angels strikes with angelic strength. It is said that the angels have maqami' of iron, that is, large iron pieces with which they strike the faces and backs of the disbelievers. From the violence of the blow and the friction of the iron against the body, a spark of fire comes out of it to burn the bodies of the disbelievers.

Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾ (part of verse 50, Surah al-Anfal, 8).

So they strike the disbelievers at the moment of death agony with a very painful blow; but this striking, despite its severity, and the sparks that come out of it, do not save them in the Hereafter from the punishment of the burning.

For this reason a companion came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw on the back of Abu Jahl something like the strap of a sandal," that is, a mark of severe, evident striking on his body. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is the striking of the angels." Another companion came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended to kill so-and-so, and I headed toward him with my sword; before my sword reached his neck, I saw his head fly from above his body." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "The angel has preceded you to him." This is in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted:

﴿When your Lord inspired the angels: "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike above the necks and strike from them every fingertip"﴾ (Surah al-Anfal, 8:12).

And here, in the noble verse about which we are reflecting, the blessed and exalted Truth says:

﴿And if you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs﴾ (part of verse 50, Surah al-Anfal, 8). That is: the striking involves more humiliation than punishment, although the punishment may be more painful. A criminal may commit a crime, and if he is seized and punished, he may bear the punishment by flogging; but if he is struck in front of people, that is a greater humiliation for him; and if the striking comes from the one against whom the crime was committed, the humiliation is greater still.

But this striking and punishment do not save them from the punishment of the Fire; rather, they will be consigned to the most severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This is the logical result of what the disbelievers do: their disbelief in Allah, their harming of the believers in Him, and their spreading corruption on the earth.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 51:

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿That is because of what your hands have sent forward, and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾

We know that most of a person's deeds are carried out by his hand, though he may do some things with his feet or his tongue; but most actions are accomplished by the hand, because the hand carries the capacity to act. Glorified is He; He did not wrong them.

"That" points to the beating and punishment they suffer being the result of what their hands sent forward. He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ (part of verse 51, Surat al-Anfal). That is: the punishment that befalls the disbelievers occurs as the result of two things: what their hands sent forward, that is, what they earned of sins and disobedience, and the justice of Allah, glorified and exalted.

And we find the Truth, glorified and exalted, saying:

﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich." We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning. That is for what your hands have put forward, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants."﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran)

And He, glorified and exalted, says in Surat al-Hajj:

﴿That is for what your hands have put forward, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ (Surat al-Hajj)

Thus we find that the Truth, glorified and exalted, said that He is not ever unjust to the servants three times in the Noble Qur'an. Those who wish to find fault with the Book of Allah say: it has come in the Qur'an more than once that He, glorified and exalted, is not ever unjust to the servants. So does this mean that Allah, God forbid, is unjust? We say: No. He, glorified is He, negates injustice from Himself absolutely. A person who wrongs is "unjust" (zalim); if his wrongdoing becomes severe and repeated, he is called "very unjust" (zallam). This is thus an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) of injustice, just as you say: so-and-so is "akil" (eats) and so-and-so is "akkal" (a great eater), meaning one who eats excessively. And you say: so-and-so is "najir," meaning he took a piece of wood without expertise and made something from it; but when you say "najjar" (carpenter), this is an intensive form showing his mastery of his craft. Likewise "khaʾit" (sewer) and "khayyat" (tailor). And you say: so-and-so is "jazir," meaning he is able to slaughter; but when you say "jazzar" (butcher), his occupation is to slaughter with skill. So "fa''al" is an intensive form of the action.

Intensive forms have two states: an affirmative state and a negative state. When you say, "so-and-so is an akkal," you affirm for him the quality of intensity in eating, that is, excessive eating, and by greater implication the quality of eating in general; and since you have affirmed the higher quality, the lower quality is established. When you say that so-and-so is a khayyat, you affirm that he knows tailoring and does it well; and if you say he is a najjar, you affirm that he is a carpenter who has mastered carpentry. As for negation: if you say that so-and-so is not an akkal, you negate the intensity, but you do not negate that he eats; if you say that so-and-so is not a najjar, you negate his mastery of carpentry, but you do not negate that he may be a carpenter (najir); and if you say that so-and-so is not an 'allama (very learned), he may still be a scholar ('alim). When you affirm the higher, you affirm the lower; when you negate the higher, you do not negate the lower. When you say, "so-and-so is not a zallam," you have negated the intensive form, but it does not follow that the lower is negated: he may be a zalim (unjust) without being a zallam. Thus the phrase "not a zallam" negates only the intensity, not injustice itself.

This is what the orientalists said: that the verses of the Qur'an contradict one another. In one verse, for example, He says: ﴿not a zallam﴾, negating the higher, and negating the higher does not necessarily negate the lower. And He, glorified and exalted, says in another verse:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (even) the weight of an atom﴾ (part of verse 40, Surat al-Nisa')

Here both the lower and the higher are negated. They consider this a contradiction. We say: when the higher is negated, must the lower be affirmed? Certainly not. Negating the higher does not prevent the lower from existing, but it does not require its existence.

So the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted, ﴿and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ (part of verse 51, Surat al-Anfal) negates the principle of injustice, while His saying, ﴿He is not a zallam to the servants﴾ negates the principle of intensity. The Qur'an completes itself: if it is said that God negated the higher, which means the lower is affirmed, we say: negating the higher does not necessarily entail affirming the lower, nor does it prevent the lower from existing. If another verse then negates the lower, then He is neither a zallam nor a zalim.

We must also attend to the miraculous character of the Qur'an in its style. The speaker is Allah. Did Allah say, "He is not a zallam to the servant" or "He is not a zallam to the servants"? The Truth said: ﴿not a zallam to the servants﴾, and here it is an intensive form. The intensive form may denote the intensity of an event even if it is not repeated, and it may denote intensity through repetition of the event. A person who wrongs in a clear and exaggerated manner is called a zallam, because he has gone to excess in wrongdoing; but if he does not exaggerate in wrongdoing, and his wrong is slight yet touches a large number of people, he is a zallam in view of the multiplicity of the wronged.

Since the Truth, glorified and exalted, said ﴿not a zallam to the servants﴾, and did not say "to the servant," and since injustice is proportional to capacity: we find, for example, that the capacity of a ruler to do injustice is greater than that of a person of limited influence, and this is greater than that of an ordinary individual. Had Allah, glorified and exalted, been unjust to each of His servants, even to the weight of an atom, He would be called zallam. Allah, glorified and exalted, intended by this noble verse to inform us that He does not wrong anyone, even to the weight of an atom; so He is not a zallam to the servants, for if He wronged every one of His servants even an atom's weight, the quantity of injustice would be immense because of the multitude of servants. But even this atom's weight of injustice does not occur from Allah, glorified and exalted, because Allah is not a zallam to the servants.

Then the Truthful Lord (Allah, glory be to Him) gives us examples of the peak of disbelief in this worldly life, so He says, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿As was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed Allah is Strong, Severe in punishment.﴾ (8:52)

The word "da'b" (usual practice, habit) is the habit that recurs with a person; it is said: "da'ub 'ala kadhā," meaning he does it continuously. Allah, glory be to Him, here makes clear to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: the practice of these disbelievers toward you, O Muhammad, is their habit with you, just as the practice of the people of Pharaoh toward their messenger; that is, they treat you as the people of Pharaoh treated Moses, peace be upon him.

As for His saying, "and those before them": these are the people of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot and others. What happened to them? Destruction, annihilation, punishment, drowning, or being swallowed up by the earth. So the disbelievers who oppose the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, fight him, and stand in the position of harming him, this practice and attitude toward him is like the practice and attitude of the people of Pharaoh toward Moses, peace be upon him, and the people of Lot toward Lot, peace be upon him, and likewise those before them. The Truthful Lord, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿they denied the signs of Allah﴾ (part of 8:52). So has Allah left them? No. ﴿So Allah seized them for their sins.﴾

Some of them were drowned, some were struck by the thunderbolt, and some had the earth swallow them up. And since Allah, glory be to Him, has done this with the earlier disbelievers, as is established, He, glory be to Him, will surely send His punishment upon the disbelievers who deny the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and they will not step outside the rule of dealing with those who deny the messengers. Similar precedents have occurred in the universe and in real events. The people of Pharaoh, for example, reached the peak of progress and civilization in their era, and Allah, glory be to Him, speaks of the civilization of the Pharaohs:

﴿And Pharaoh, the lord of the stakes﴾ (89:10).

As for Thamud, if we go to the cities of Salih in Saudi Arabia, we find the remains of Thamud, who carved their houses into the mountain rocks, and the Truthful Lord speaks of the civilization of Thamud:

﴿And Thamud, who hewed the rocks in the valley﴾ (89:9).

Most ancient civilizations have vanished and left no trace, and if any trace remains, it is small and simple and does not bear all the marks of civilization, except the remains of the Pharaohs, where there are huge obelisks, tall columns and great pyramids, and they still endure. As for the civilization of the people of 'Ad, Allah, the Glorified, has obliterated its traces, so we have not found anything of it until now. Most traces of civilizations have been effaced except the remains of the civilization of the people of Pharaoh, to which people come from all over the world, to marvel at the beauty of the building, the splendour of the art and the peak of progress in engineering design, and at how these massive stones were transported to high places without scaffolding, and how all these stones were joined to one another for all these long years without using cement or any other fixing material, but rather this was done by evacuating the air. How could this wondrous engineering evacuate the air between two huge, massive stones so that they stick together in a firm bond without any adhesive, and no one can shift them? If the civilization of the Pharaohs reached this engineering art by using air evacuation between heavy loads, then it is a very refined civilization. Moreover, if you look at the art of building alone, and likewise if we look at the embalming of bodies, whose secret no one knows until now, and how the mummies could be preserved for thousands of years without decay. Likewise, if you look at the colours with which the temples and drawings were painted and which remained bright despite all that long time, and at the grains that were embalmed and remained for thousands of years without any damage, and even fit for food: this civilization which kept the secrets of these things, mankind has not yet reached them. It must have been a strong and lofty civilization, yet despite its strength and loftiness it could not protect itself from collapse, so that it became a trace and remains only traces.

Where did the makers of this civilization go, when they had reached a great height and possessed the reins of the world in their era? There must therefore be a power higher than them, which crushed them. And why did Allah mention the people of Pharaoh by name in this verse, while mentioning the earlier civilizations in general terms? He said, Exalted is He:

﴿As was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them﴾ (part of 8:52). Because the traces of the people of Pharaoh were uncovered by Allah, and He made all of mankind eager to see them, so that they would come and see that tremendous civilization which could not protect itself, and that Pharaoh who claimed to be a god yet could not ensure his own survival. Allah, glory be to Him, willed that the traces of this civilization remain so that all people might witness them, and then see that Allah, mighty and majestic, destroyed its people and they became a story after they had been a reality; so that they might know that all power belongs to Allah, that divinity belongs to Allah alone, and that everything perishes except Allah. For this reason the civilization of the people of Pharaoh was mentioned specifically, and this mention of the traces of the people of Pharaoh is one of the miracles of the Qur'an, because it mentioned this civilization specifically and then the Truthful Lord related the accounts of the other civilizations in general terms: the people of Noah, 'Ad, Iram and Thamud. All of them: ﴿they denied the signs of Allah﴾. We know that the word "ayat" (signs) is used in three senses: the cosmic signs which establish the existence of the Supreme Creator, such as His saying:

﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon﴾ (41:37).

Likewise the miracles which Allah gives to His messengers to establish the truthfulness of their message from Allah, such as the splitting of the sea for Moses, peace be upon him, and the healing of the blind and the leper and the raising of the dead by Allah's permission for Jesus, peace be upon him. Then the verses of the noble Qur'an, which are the firm, clear method of Allah on earth.

As for the Truthful Lord's words, ﴿they denied the signs of Allah﴾, we learn from it that they denied the existence of the Creator. The root meaning of kufr (disbelief) is concealment, and kafara means "he covered." That is why the farmer is called, in the linguistic sense, "kafir," because he brings the seed and covers it with earth; and the night is called, linguistically, "kafir," because it covers things. The poet says:

"For you there is the reward of one who strives, if it is true that the night is a concealer."

The meaning of "kafaru" is that they concealed the existence of Allah, may He be exalted. So Allah, mighty and majestic, exists, His existence established before they covered it with disbelief, because faith is the origin of the existence of creation, and creation came into being upon faith; then people came who concealed that faith. Thus the word kufr, whose meaning is concealment, is itself evidence of the proofs of faith; for if Allah did not exist, how could they conceal what has no existence? If someone says to you that it is disbelief, God forbid, you say: disbelief is concealment, so what did you conceal? You must have concealed something that exists. And the saying of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him, ﴿they denied the signs of Allah﴾:

that is, they disbelieved in His cosmic signs and did not believe despite the manifest signs that fill the universe; they disbelieved in the signs of the messengers, denying their messengers although they brought them miracles that break the laws of life; and they did not accept the signs of the Book sent down from heaven to show them the method of Allah, exalted is He.

And His saying, exalted is He:

﴿As was the case with the people of Pharaoh and those before them, they denied the signs of Allah﴾ (part of 8:52) is a concise, expressive statement that tells you why Allah seized them for their sins:

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed Allah is Strong, Severe in punishment﴾ (part of 8:52).

The seizing in His saying ﴿So He seized them﴾ was because of the sins they committed and the corruption they wrought on earth. When a person finds evil surrounding him and painful punishment coming upon him, he tries to flee from it, and therefore the Truthful Lord says in another verse:

﴿A seizing by the Mighty, the Omnipotent﴾ (54:42).

That is, the power of Allah, exalted is He, grips the disbeliever with a firm grip, so he cannot escape or flee.

And His saying, glory be to Him, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed Allah is Strong, Severe in punishment﴾ (part of 8:52): that is, Allah is stronger than everything you do in His universe, and His punishment, exalted is He, is severe and painful. We know that punishment does not befall people except in proportion to their sins; so the fact that Allah is severe in punishment does not mean that the severity of torment strikes one who commits a small sin, but rather each receives his recompense according to the measure of his sin. And this punishment, however small it may be, is severe and painful, because punishment from Allah occurs only by the power of Allah; so however small it is, it is severe and painful. And the saying of the Truthful Lord, glory be to Him:

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾

This statement does not fall under the doctrine of compulsion (jabr) of which the poet says:

He threw him into the sea, bound, and said to him:
"Beware, beware of being wet with water!"

And whoever thinks that Allah has written by compulsion that someone should be a disbeliever and then cast him into the fire of Hell is mistaken; no, because such a matter contradicts the justice of Allah, glory be to Him. You, O human, are free to choose between obedience and disobedience, between faith and disbelief. On this basis we understand the saying of the Truthful Lord:

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins﴾ (part of 8:52): that is, because of their sins. And since the Truthful, blessed and exalted, has threatened them with severe punishment, this is evidence of the severity of their wrongdoing.

Then the Truthful Lord gives us the reason for this, so He says, exalted is He:

﴿That is because Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves. And indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ (8:53).

That (ذلك) refers to what has been mentioned before. If you look at the beginning of humankind, you find that God Most High created Adam to make him a khalifah (vicegerent) on earth, and He created Eve to perpetuate the human species.

Before Adam descended to the earth, God, glory be to Him, gave him the manhaj (the method, the way of life). From Adam and Eve, their offspring began, and had they followed the manhaj that Adam taught to this progeny, humanity would have arrived at happiness. But the progeny changed; they denied the blessing and rejected that blessing has a Creator. Would God then keep for them security, safety and blessings while they have changed? No. Rather, it is necessary then that God change His blessings upon them; otherwise there would be no logic at all to religion, because man came after the blessings were already in place. That is to say, God did not create man and then create blessings for him. Rather, He created the blessings first, and then man came into a universe that had been completely prepared for him, containing everything needed for life and its continuation. Man remained for a long period in the infancy of life, frolicking in God's blessings, before he knew agriculture; he found the fruits that he ate. And before he knew how to search for water, he found the water that he drank, and God taught him how to live. He subjected to him from among the animals those that give him milk and meat. All these blessings and others must be received by man with gratitude and continued loyalty to God, the Creator, the Benefactor.

But man denied the blessing of God and denied the Benefactor. Will he then retain happiness and a tranquil life on earth? Certainly not. And as long as man has changed, the Truth must change the blessing into a curse. And from His mercy, glory be to Him, He willed that man be the initiator, for the Truth, glory be to Him, is exalted above being the initiator of injustice; rather, man began to wrong himself. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿That is because Allah never changes a favor He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves. And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ (part of verse 53, Surat al-Anfal).

So the offspring of Adam first began by changing the blessing of faith into disbelief, and from gratitude into denial. Thus God requited them with the flood, with thunderbolts, and with destruction; because they changed what was in themselves. And had they returned to thanking God and worshipping Him, God would have restored to them the blessings of security, stability and a good life.

The Lord, glory be to Him, draws our attention to the fact that following the manhaj increases blessings and does not diminish them, so He says:

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened to them blessings from the heaven and the earth.﴾ (part of verse 96, Surat al-A'raf).

And in accordance with this divine law, we find that people's change from faith to disbelief must be met with a change in God's blessing upon them; otherwise the manhaj of God would become worthless. An example: every student enters an examination, but only the one who studied passes, while the one who did not study fails; so that the world does not descend into chaos. And if God, glory be to Him, gave those who followed the manhaj the same bounty He gives to those who do not follow the manhaj, what would be the value of the manhaj?

Therefore, man must enter into faith, and this faith must be deeply rooted in your depths and not merely an outward matter. Do not claim reform while you are corrupt, nor claim honour and trustworthiness while you steal, nor claim justice while you wrong the poor and favour the rich; for the Truth, glory be to Him, does not give His apparent and hidden blessings except to those who follow His manhaj. And if you see a people among whom corruption has spread, know that their souls have not changed, despite their pretending to follow the divine manhaj.

And if we complain of our bad condition, then let us first know what we have done, and then change it to what pleases God, Mighty and Majestic, and God will change our condition. Therefore, if you find all people complaining, know that this has happened because God has changed His blessings upon them, since they changed what was in themselves. That is to say, their earlier state was that they were in blessing and in harmony with the manhaj of God; they changed their harmony and obedience, so the blessing changed. There are thus two fundamental changes: that God changes a blessing He bestowed upon a people, and this does not happen until they change what is in themselves.

As for His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing (53)﴾ (part of verse 53, Surat al-Anfal): That is, God, Exalted is He, knows the reality of what they do and hears their secret and their open speech. Therefore, when they change, God, glory be to Him, hears and knows, because change is either by speech or by action. If the change is by speech, the Truth, glory be to Him, hears it, even if it is merely thoughts in the souls; and if the change is by deed, the Truth sees it and knows it, even if it is at the farthest end of the earth.

Almighty Allah returns to the family of Pharaoh, saying:

﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins and drowned the people of Pharaoh; and they were all wrongdoers.﴾ (8:54)

Some ask: why did Allah return to the family of Pharaoh and not include them with the first verse? We say: because there is a subtle difference between the two. In the first verse, the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿disbelieved in the signs of Allah﴾, while in the second verse He says:

﴿they denied the signs of their Lord﴾ (part of 8:54). The first verse indicates that they disbelieved in the cosmic signs that establish the existence of Allah the Exalted, the signs of the messengers, and the signs of the scriptures revealed to them. In this verse, they "denied the signs of their Lord," meaning they did not safeguard the blessings Allah had given them. The blessings of Allah are a gift of lordship (rububiyyah), and His commandments and His method are a gift of divinity (uluhiyyah). In the first verse they denied the gift of divinity, that is, they disbelieved in Allah. In the second verse they denied the gift of lordship, that is, the blessings of Allah. The gift of lordship is the gift of the Lord who created from non-existence and sustained what was non-existent, so that the human being's requirements for life may be completed. Allah gives the gift of lordship equally to the believer and the disbeliever, and to the disobedient and the obedient; He does not distinguish between them on account of faith or disbelief.

Here the Exalted says:

﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh, and they were all wrongdoers﴾ (part of 8:54): that is, there was no division among them between a believer and a disbeliever such that a distinction would be made by saving the believers and drowning the disbelievers. Rather, they all wronged themselves through disbelief. Therefore the Exalted Allah said: ﴿and they were all wrongdoers﴾. Allah mentioned the family of Pharaoh specifically, because they are the only nation whose civilization remains, indicating the extent of their advancement, an advancement whose every secret we have not yet reached. Such a civilization cannot come to an end except by a power greater than its own. It is as if Allah wanted to draw our attention specifically to the family of Pharaoh, because it was decreed for humanity to discover the remains of Pharaoh, and their remains are striking to the whole world. He placed in the hearts of people a love to come and see the civilization of the family of Pharaoh and to marvel at how they reached this lofty level of civilization. Then this civilization collapsed as evidence of the existence of a higher power, which is Allah the Exalted. Allah destroyed them because they disbelieved in divinity, took Pharaoh as a god and lord besides Allah, and disbelieved in the blessing of lordship that Allah had given them, part of which Allah mentions in His noble saying:

﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station, and a luxury in which they took delight﴾ (Surah al-Dukhan 44:25–27).

Thus Allah gave them crops and water, and did not give them sparingly but abundantly and generously; therefore Allah said: ﴿gardens and springs﴾. He gave them wealth and power that preserved their dignity and made them the masters of the earth in their era, and He granted them a noble station, and no one dared to humiliate them or to attack them. They possessed the treasures of the earth, and the power that preserved their honor, in His saying:

﴿and crops and a noble station, and a luxury in which they took delight﴾ (Surah al-Dukhan 44:26–27).

He also gave them of knowledge what provided them with luxury and a good, abundant, comfortable life in everything. But they disbelieved in these blessings of lordship, just as they disbelieved in the blessing of divinity, so they deserved punishment. Their remains still testify to them: we find in them gold and treasures, which were buried with their dead, and we find in them civilization and strength in the battles that they depicted on their temples with clarity and precision. We see in them the immense blessing in which Pharaoh and his people lived, yet they did not render its due and disbelieved in the Creator, the Giver of blessings.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, for they will not believe.﴾ [8:55]

﴿Ad-dawabb﴾ is the plural of dabbah (a creature that moves, or crawls, on the face of the earth). If this were the meaning alone, then a human being would be included in this definition. However, linguistic usage has restricted the term dabbah to the four-legged ones, i.e., animals. The Creator, glory be to Him, has honoured man by making him not walk on four, and so he is not included in this definition. The saying of Almighty Allah:

﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve﴾ (part of verse 55, Surat al-Anfal).

shows us that Allah, glory be to Him, has attached the disbelievers to the animals and made an exception only of the believers. He, glory be to Him, created the animals and the rest of the species of the universe subjugated, performing their task in life by instinct and without choice. What happens by instinct does not differ among minds, and therefore we find that many things we, the people of intellect, learn from animals and insects which have no intellect, because animals act by instinct, and instinct never errs. When we read the saying of Almighty Allah:

﴿Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the shame of his brother﴾ (part of verse 31, Surat al-Ma'idah).

we find that the crow, which has no choice and no intellect, taught the human being who has intellect and choice. This happened because the crow is governed by instinct. Therefore, everything an animal does in its conduct is by the choice of Allah, glory be to Him, because the animal is compelled regarding its duties. It is part of the mercy of Allah, Exalted, that all creatures, except man, were created compelled: they do everything by instinct and not by intellect. But man, whom Allah honoured with intellect, thinks and disobeys, although Almighty Allah has bestowed upon man the blessing of choice.

It is remarkable that we find the animal governed by instinct does not depart from its conduct in the system it is made to follow, and performs its task exactly as it was drawn for it. The female animal, for example, gives birth and they take its young to slaughter it, and it does not react, because its task in life is to give meat to man. The dove sits on its eggs, and when the little chick hatches, it cares for it for a very brief period until it knows how to fly and how to eat, and then it leaves it to perform its task, because it is governed by instinct. Instincts do not err, and the animal acts by them without being taught.

When we come to man, we find that the forms of conduct governed by instinct in him are not learned: when he is hungry he seeks food without anyone teaching him how to feel hunger; if he is thirsty he seeks water without anyone teaching him the meaning of thirst or how to drink. Each of us is equal to the other in instincts. We find the rich, the poor, the ruler and the guard, when they feel hunger, seek food, and when they feel thirst, seek water. Thus everything governed by instincts has no change in it.

It is remarkable, for example, that when a donkey wants to cross a watercourse, it looks at it, and at a single glance it can tell whether it will cross or not. If it is able, it leaps one leap to cross; if it is not able, it searches for another way. You cannot force a donkey to cross a watercourse it cannot cross, and however much you beat it, it will not respond to you by crossing. But as for man, if you ask him to cross a water channel, he may say to himself: "I will gather all my strength and make one enormous leap," and if his measurement is not correct, he falls into the water. That is because he erred, and the faculty of choice portrayed to him that he can do what he is not able to do. Therefore, the one governed by instinct is the more aware.

When we come to eating, we find the animal governed by instinct more aware, for it eats, and when it is satisfied it tastes nothing, even if you bring it the most delicious foods. You cannot make the animal eat a single stalk of clover, a handful of straw, or a grain of beans after it has become satisfied; you will find it trampling with its feet whatever exceeds its need. Come to a person who has filled his belly, become satisfied and washed his hands, and then they tell him, for example: "You forgot the fruit," or "You forgot the sweets," and you will find him returning to eat again though he is full; so he damages his stomach and damages his body. For this reason you find man afflicted with many diseases that do not afflict animals, because he is extravagant in many things. Indeed, you find that most of the diseases afflicting animals arise from the pollution of the animal's environment caused by what man does.

Almighty Allah wants to inform us that the creature governed by instinct is better than the disbeliever, because the creature performs its task in life perfectly, whereas the disbeliever does not perform his task on earth, but rather corrupts in it and sheds blood, and thereby becomes worse than the animal. We have said: the animal carries you from place to place and does not complain, and bears your burdens and does not resent. It keeps walking for a long time while you sit upon it, and it does not strain under you or throw you to the ground. It was created for this task and performs it as it was created for it, without complaint or weariness, because it is governed by a precise system that it follows and carries out. But man invented the car and developed it, and he may sit at the driving seat, become tired, doze off, fall into an accident, be injured in it, and injure others too.

It was incumbent upon man to follow in his life the methodology of his Lord which He sent down to him, but among mankind there are those who disbelieve and begin to act wantonly in the universe, and thereby become worse than the animal, because the disbeliever uses his intellect on the priorities of existence. Had he used his intellect, he would have known that he has come upon a universe that has been prepared with precise preparation: a sun that illuminates half the universe to give it daylight, and sets so that a moon may appear, shining at night, keeping him company in darkness; stars that guide him on the way on land and sea; and rain that falls so that crops may grow; and an animal subjugated to him that gives him milk and carries his burdens. It was necessary, then, for man, the possessor of intellect, to reflect: Who created all these blessings for him? For this is among the foremost tasks of the intellect that reflects and leads us to the Creator. In that case, man ought to know through his intellect that One who made all these blessings for him and subjected them to him must intend good for him. Therefore, when the methodology comes to him from heaven, he must follow it, because he knows that this methodology is the best that suits him, since it came from his Creator.

In that case, the affairs of the universe would have been set right. But some of the children of Adam concealed the existence of Allah and disbelieved in Him, and therefore Almighty Allah makes clear to us that they are worse than the animals, because they do not believe.

Then the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear (Allah).﴾ (8:56)

After the Almighty spoke of the disbelievers who fought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), He now moves on to speak of the group that had made a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would refrain from harming him, and that the Messenger would not confront them. These were the Jews. Did they remain faithful to the covenant? No. Rather, they broke the covenant.

The Banu Qurayza, for example, covenanted with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would not assist anyone against him. When the Battle of Badr came, they supplied the disbelievers with weapons and broke the covenant. Then they returned, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them a second covenant. When the Battle of the Trench came, they agreed that the soldiers of Quraysh should not enter through the area they controlled, so that they could strike the army of the Muslims from behind, at its back. So Allah sent His Messenger a wind that scattered the shamlof the disbelievers. Thus the saying of the Almighty:

﴿Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time﴾ (part of 8:56), and they did so because they had abandoned the way of Allah and feared the Messenger of Allah, so they tried to deceive him by breaking the treaties.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they do not fear (Allah)﴾, they do not fear Allah, mighty and majestic, whom they believe in as a god, even though they are People of the Book. The Torah came to them, and a messenger came to them, Moses (peace be upon him). They are not a people to whom no scripture came; rather a heavenly scripture, the Torah, was revealed to them. Yet despite this, they do not follow what is in their scripture and do not fear Allah, exalted is He. First, they break the covenant. Breaking (naqd) is the opposite of strengthening (ibram), and ibram is to make a thing firm, just as one twists (yubrim) a thread, that is, strengthens it. When you strengthen a thread, you wind it upon itself so that it becomes sturdy. A thread two spans long, when you twist it, becomes one span long and becomes strong; if you unravel it, that is, break it, it becomes weak. For this reason the Lord, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And do not be like her who unravels her spun thread after it had been strong, into fibers﴾ (part of 16:92).

The Almighty gives the ruling concerning these people, those who do not believe, do not fear Allah, and break their covenant; the True Word comes concerning them:

﴿So if you gain dominance over them in war, then drive away with them those behind them, that they may take heed.﴾ (8:57)

Meaning: if you come upon them in war, then scatter those behind them with them. And we should note that the word "imma" (إما) is the conditional "in" merged with "ma"; if we remove the "ma" from it, we find it becomes "in," as if he is saying: "in ma," and the nun of "in" was assimilated into "ma," just as when we say: "in jaaka Zaydun fa-akrimhu" (if Zayd comes to you, then honor him). This is a conditional sentence with a condition, a response, and a conditional particle, but once it occurs one time, it has ended. However, "ma" with the conditional "in" tells us that whenever that happens, we do to them what God Almighty has commanded, just as we say: "kullama jaaka Zaydun fa-akrimhu" (whenever Zayd comes to you, honor him), because this "ma" carries a meaning of continuity, like "kullama." So whenever he comes, you honor him, even if he comes a hundred times; and if "ma" had not come, it would have sufficed for you to do it once.

And His saying, Exalted is He: "tathqafannahum fi'l-harb" (تثقفنهم في الحرب): "thaqifa" means "wajada" (to find), meaning: whenever you find them in war, then scatter those behind them with them, that is, make them an instrument for scattering those behind them. You must discipline them with a discipline that makes those who are behind them fear you and keep away from you, and whenever they see you, fear and panic overtake them. As the colloquial proverb says: "idrib al-marbut yakhaf al-saib" (strike the tethered one, and the loose one fears). That is, what is required is that we fight them with strength and without mercy, so that those who come behind them to support or back them by joining them in fighting do not think of backing them, and their own souls do not make them wish to continue in the battle. So "fa-sharrid bihim": "tashrid" is dispersal, separation and removal, but with severity. So wherever they wish to go, prevent them and disperse them against their intention. And the saying of the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He: "La'allahum yadhdhakkarun" (لعلهم يذكرون), that is: so that this experience may be a lesson for them, so that they do not think again of waging war against you, because they will remember what happened to them and keep away from confronting you.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 8, verse 58:

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous.﴾ (8:58):

He, glory be to Him, begins this verse with His words "wa-immā" (and if), like "fa-immā" in the preceding verse, and that has already been explained. Here He speaks of others who are not confronted with war, but who plot treachery against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

We say: Is this treachery certain, or have you acted on mere suspicion? Allah, glory be to Him, here distinguishes in His justice among His creation between certain treachery and uncertain treachery. Certain treachery has one ruling, and suspected treachery has another ruling. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ (part of 8:58): that is, if it reaches you that they will betray you, what will you do with them?

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms﴾ (part of 8:58).

That is, since a covenant is the property of both parties, this one has made a pact with that one and that one has made a pact with this one, beware of seizing them unawares. Rather, "throw back" to them. Al-nabdh (throwing back) means casting off and dismissing. That is, you must cancel the covenant between you and them, end it, and dismiss it with notice. So at the moment you fear treachery, dismiss them, but do not fight them before you inform them that you have cancelled it for a clear and known reason.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew that the tribe of Khuza'ah, who had become his allies after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, were being attacked, and the treaty required that Quraysh not attack the allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not attack the allies of Quraysh. Some members of Quraysh went to the tribe of Khuza'ah and struck them. That is, Quraysh broke the covenant and violated the pact that existed between it and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by aiding the Banu Bakr in attacking Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger (ﷺ). What did the survivors of Khuza'ah do? They sent 'Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i, who cried out before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina, and said: "Quraysh has broken its promise to you and violated your covenant." When this happened, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not keep the matter secret, but informed Quraysh of what had occurred, and that he had cast off the covenant made at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah between him and Quraysh.

When Abu Sufyan came to Medina to try to justify what had happened, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to meet him.

So if you find from the people with whom you have a covenant signs of treachery, then throw back the covenant; but if you are certain that they have indeed betrayed you and treachery has occurred, then surprise them with war, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did with the Jews after they betrayed him at the Battle of the Trench and broke the covenant and pact.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾ (part of 8:58).

So it is as if Allah is free of treachery, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is free of it, and the Muslims are free of betraying even those who disbelieve. This confirms for us that Islam came to balance the scales on earth, not only for its own believers but for all people. Therefore, if you read the Truth's words, glory be to Him:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ (part of 4:105).

We note that the verse did not say "between the believers" but said "between the people," so that there is no distinction in justice between believer and non-believer. The non-believer is a creature of Allah, whom Allah summoned into this existence, and He has prepared a place for him in this world. Therefore you must observe justice with him in all matters, and not wrong him, but give him his due, for in doing so you become one of the supports of Allah's support. This just conduct, which he was commanded to follow, was a cause for a large number to enter Islam. And we find the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And do not be a pleader for the treacherous﴾ (part of 4:105): that is, do not support, O Muhammad, the treacherous, even if they are among your followers. This verse was revealed when a shield was stolen from Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, who was one of the Ansar, and suspicion fell upon a man of the Ansar from a household called the Banu Ubayriq. The owner of the shield came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq stole my shield." When the thief learned of what had happened, he put the shield in a bag of flour, hurried off, and threw it into the house of a Jewish man named Zayd ibn al-Samin. He told his clan: "I have placed the shield in the house of the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samin." So they went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, our companion is innocent, and the one who stole the shield is that Jew." The Companions went and found the shield in the bag of flour in the Jew's house. But the Jew denied that he had stolen the shield and said: "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq brought it to me." Ta'mah did not notice, while the bag of flour was being carried, that there was a small hole in it, through which the flour leaked and left a mark on the ground, due to his carelessness; for Allah always leaves a sign of the truth by which the judge may be guided, so that the truth is not lost. The Muslims followed the trail of flour until it led them to the house of Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, and the case became that the thief was a Muslim. But he had falsely accused the Jew of the theft. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you rule in favour of the Jew against the Muslim, the Muslims will be in baseness, meanness and embarrassment." Then revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to protect him from the pull of his own inclinations in this matter:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be a pleader for the treacherous﴾ (4:105): that is, do not be a defender, for the sake and in the interest of the treacherous, of any one of them, even if that treacherous person is a Muslim. Thus was the justice of Islam: the judgment of Allah does not support a Muslim in falsehood, nor wrong a Jew. Do they not see this religion and the strength of truth within it? Does this not move them to turn to this Islamic religion, the religion of justice and fairness, so that they may be embraced by it?

And here the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms﴾ (part of 8:58): that is, say to them: "I have cancelled this covenant between me and you, and I am free of it."

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾ show that He, glory be to Him, does not love the treacherous, even if they are among those who are ascribed to Islam.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that they have outstripped [Us]. Indeed, they will not cause [Allah] to fail.﴾ (8:59)

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered into battle with the disbelievers, a group of the disbelievers was killed, another group of them was taken captive, and a third group fled. As for those who were killed and those who were taken captive, they received their recompense. Those who fled were saved from killing and from captivity, so it was as if they had outstripped [the Muslims], and the Muslims who wanted to kill them or take them captive did not catch up with them. Sabq (outstripping, precedence) means that a thing is present which wants to catch up with something in front of it, so it outstrips it and is unable to reach it. Thus, when the disbelievers fled, it was as if they had outstripped the Muslims, who, had they caught up with them, would have killed them or taken them captive.

Allah, glorified and exalted, wants us to know that this is the apparent outcome of what happened. But the reality which Allah, mighty and majestic, wants us to understand is that these disbelievers who fled and outstripped, and whom the hands of the Muslims did not reach, will not cause Allah, exalted is He, to fail, nor will they escape His power, glorified and exalted is He. The punishment will come to them at a later time, either by the expiry of their term or in a second battle.

Usually we find that each of the one who outstrips and the one who is outstripped exerts his utmost strength: the first to flee, the second to catch up with him. Therefore, when you see the two of them, you may be amazed at the strength with which each of them runs, and this is human nature. In ordinary circumstances a person has strength and capability; in sudden events, a person has other faculties. If, for example, a ship sinks in the sea and one of its passengers clings to a piece of wood from the wreckage of the ship, you find him swimming for a long time without feeling tired. But when he reaches the shore, his strength gives way.

We have come to know the secret of this when the science of physiology discovered that a person has a gland above the kidneys, which is the adrenal gland. When he falls into a sudden predicament, it secretes a substance called "adrenaline," and this is a substance that can give him ten times his strength. But when the danger passes, the gland stops secreting this substance except in the amount the body needs. Therefore you find the person who rivals the waves in the sea being supplied with fuel by this gland; when he reaches the shore, the gland stops the excess secretion appropriate to danger, so his strength fails and he may remain asleep for three days from exhaustion.

There is a symbolic fictional story told of a hunter who sent his dog running after a gazelle to bring it to him. The dog runs wanting to catch the gazelle, and the gazelle runs seeking safety. Suddenly the gazelle turned to the dog and said to it: "You will not catch me, because I run for my own sake, and you run for the sake of your master."

So whoever does something to save himself becomes strong. And the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, they will not cause [Allah] to fail﴾ (part of verse 8:58): that is, they are within the grasp of His will and do not escape the power of Allah, who will bring them forth and hold them to account.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 60:

After the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, spoke of those who wage war, those who make a covenant and then betray it, those who flee and escape, and those who wish to join them, He desired to alert us to an important truth: that we should not fall short in preparing the strength that helps us meet the enemy at the time of war, or even before war comes upon us, for we may be taken by surprise and then be unable to prepare. Therefore our preparation for fighting should not be limited to the very hour of combat. No, rather we must prepare both in peace and in war. For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know, [but] Allah knows them. And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.﴾

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And prepare against them﴾ means that the preparation should be for everyone of whom He has spoken: those who fought and killed and whose people are obliged to seek vengeance for their slain, those who took captives, and those who broke the covenant, whether by a definite or a probable breach. For all of these you must prepare what the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, has brought: ﴿whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war﴾. This is an obligation from Allah, exalted is He, upon His believing servants who strive to raise His word, that they must always prepare, to the extent of their capacity, whatever power they are able to.

And why "to the extent of their capacity"?

Because man is limited by his capacity, and behind the power of the believers stands the power of Allah, glorified is He. Therefore you prepare to the extent of what you are able, and then you ask Allah to help you. And when you have done what is within your capacity, beware of saying: this capability will not bring me to confront what my adversary possesses of equipment with which he may attack me. For your opponent has no reinforcement from the heavens, whereas you have heavenly reinforcement. And as long as you have this reinforcement, your strength, by the help of Allah, makes you the stronger whatever your enemy may be. For this reason, when Allah the Exalted addresses the believers, He makes clear to them: beware of fearing the multitude of your enemy; what is required of you is to prepare against them whatever strength you can. And so that I may reassure you that I am with you, remember one verse which I have sent down:

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾ (part of verse 151, Surat Al 'Imran)

When Allah, mighty and majestic is He, casts terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, they will lay down their weapons and flee the field of battle even if they fight with the strongest arms, and the believers will prevail over them and be victorious over them with whatever strength they have prepared.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿whatever you are able of power﴾. This strength may be inward, in the soul, such that one fears nothing: the body of every fighter is strong, full of health, and has a mind that works with competence and eagerness to fight with courage. In addition to the strength of weaponry, namely modern, advanced weapons of long range, the believers should be keen to possess everything connected to strength. The aim, in the past and in the present, has been that the fighter possess a strength that enables him to reach his enemy while not allowing his enemy to reach him. In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the range of arrow-shooting was the symbol of strength. A war would begin with them striking the enemy with arrows; if the enemy advanced and drew near, they would use spears; and if close combat took place, it was with swords. The best strength in war was the arrows with which you strike your opponent and reach him while he is far from you, and he cannot reach you or come near you. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained the meaning of strength, he said, as related from him by Uqbah ibn 'Amir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was on the pulpit saying: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾, then he said: "Indeed, power is archery; indeed, power is archery." (1) Because by archery you are able to reach your enemy and he cannot reach you; so if you excel in archery, you will be the victor over him.

But how does this apply to warfare in the modern age after deadly weapons have developed?
