For a period of time artillery became the weapon, because it secures victory by its long range; then aircraft came to be the strongest weapon, because they can cover a long distance, drop their bombs, and return. Air power became what determines the victor in war, because it inflicts grave losses upon the enemy without the enemy being able to respond, so long as he is not superior in the air. Then after that came missiles, and intercontinental missiles, and the rest of the advanced weapons that states now race to invent, all of them long-range weapons, the aim being that each state reaches the land of its enemy while he cannot reach its land. The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, adds:

﴿and of steeds of war﴾ (part of verse 60, Surat Al-Anfal).

The steeds of war are the strength that seizes the land. However great your capacity in archery, you cannot take possession of your enemy's land; but riders of horses used to enter the battle after the shooting in order to occupy the ground. This operation is carried out today by armoured vehicles. The battle begins first with the shooting of missiles and aircraft, and when they have crushed the strength of your enemy, the armoured vehicles advance to occupy the ground. The aircraft and missiles destroy the enemy and shatter him, but they do not take the land. What enables us to hold the land and seize it is: the steeds of war, or armoured vehicles. "Rabat al-khayl" (the stationing of horses) is their readiness for war, that is, the horses are prepared, fed, trained, and kept ready for war at any moment, just as armoured vehicles are brought and prepared well with ammunition, their engines repaired and their crews trained, so that you are ready for combat at any moment. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, as related from him by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best livelihood of people is a man who holds the bridle of his horse in the way of Allah, flying upon its back whenever he hears a cry or an alarm, seeking death or killing where it may be found; and a man in a flock of sheep upon one of these mountain pastures or in one of these valleys, establishing prayer, giving zakat, and worshipping his Lord until certainty comes to him; he is among people only in good." (2)

That is, he does not wait but sets out at the sound of any cry. And among the miraculous features of the Qur'anic presentation is that it gave us an order of war: war first begins with an attack that breaks the enemy's strength by missile fire, whether by rockets, aircraft, or other means, and after that the ground attack takes place; the reverse never happens. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, arranged the means of using strength during fighting: first is the shooting, by which we destroy the place firmly, and then we seize the place; and this was accomplished by the steeds of war, which armoured vehicles now take the place of. We find that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, in the noble Qur'an gave a statement that knows what the days will bring of the creations' inventions; and we find in our own time that every power of a car, an armoured vehicle, or a tank is measured in reference to horses, so it is said: power of five horses, or five hundred horses.

And the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾ (part of verse 60, Surat Al-Anfal).

So the purpose, then, of preparing this strength is to terrify the enemy so that he will not covet you; for the mere preparation of strength is something that causes dread in the enemy. For this reason military parades are held, so that the adversary may see the extent of the state's strength; and when you show your adversary the strength you possess, he will not dare against you, and this achieves what we call in the language of the age "peaceful balance" (al-tawazun al-silmi).

What now preserves the world after the fall of the Soviet Union is the peaceful balance between groups of states, in addition to the economic factor that makes war costly. Strength now is not limited to weapons alone; strength depends on many elements, including the economy, the media, and others. Fear of the reaction has become one of the strong reasons preventing war. Every state fears what the other state conceals or displays.

Thus preparation for war has come to negate the outbreak of war.

﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾ (part of verse 60, Surat Al-Anfal).

And do not suppose that those who confront you are only the enemies of Allah, whom He has given you power over; rather you must know that the enemies of Allah are also your enemies, because they corrupt life for the believers. The enemy of Allah always seeks to harm the believers, to punish them, to compel them, if he can, to disbelief, and to entice them to it. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, does not become angry because they have not believed in Him, but because they do not implement the method that makes man happy on earth; glorified and exalted is He, He does not compel them, but He punishes them because of corruption on the earth and their transgression and tyranny.

﴿And others besides them whom you do not know, [but] Allah knows them﴾ (part of verse 60, Surat Al-Anfal). This is a notice from the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, that the enemies of the Muslims are not only those who appeared during the mission, such as the Quraysh disbelievers, the Jews, the hypocrites, and others; rather there are many people who will come after that whom you do not know now, but Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows them. He also draws our attention to the fact that the enemies of the Muslims are not only those who appear on the battlefield to fight the Muslims; there are many who do not appear on the battlefield yet fight the religion of Allah and fight the Muslims. The meaning of this noble verse has become manifest and continues to become manifest to the Muslims: the enmity of the Persians and the Romans and their war against the Muslims became manifest, and the enmity of the Crusaders and others became manifest. Over time there will appear those whom Allah knows and we do not know. The events of life have come to confirm the precision of the expression of the noble Qur'an.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, addresses the anxieties of the human soul as it listens to these verses about military preparation. What first comes to mind is that such preparation requires money, requires effort, and requires time beyond the time needed for managing one's affairs and needs. So beware of shrinking back from preparation, for everything you spend in the way of Allah is recorded with Allah. And beware of saying: preparing the strength of the community requires money and will restrict the children; but Allah provides for you. Glorified and exalted is He says:

﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾ (part of verse 60, Surat Al-Anfal). That is: whatever you spend, of what is called "a thing," whether little or much, will be returned to you. The expression "min shay'" (of a thing) occurs in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And know that whatever you gain of a thing﴾ (Surat Al-Anfal 8:41), meaning of what is called a thing. Had the verse said "whatever you gain of a thing" (shay'an), it would not have included trivial things; but with His saying "min shay'" (of a thing), meaning from the very beginning of what is called a thing, to the point that they said: even the thread found with the enemy must go to the spoils. And the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And whatever you spend of a thing in the way of Allah﴾ (part of verse 60, Surat Al-Anfal)

means that whatever you spend in the way of Allah, exalted is He, is stored up for you, so long as you spent it while having in mind nothing but Allah, mighty and majestic is He. As for spending whose outward form is for Allah but whose reality is for fame, or for obtaining praise, or for boasting, or for the fulfilment of interests, all of this kind of spending is outside spending in the way of Allah. But spending in the way of Allah, Allah will return to you, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾, meaning that what you spend in the way of Allah does not diminish what you have in the least.

(1) Narrated by Imam Muslim and others.
(2) Narrated by Muslim and al-Nasa'i, and it appears in al-Targhib, vol. 2, p. 247.

Al-Sha'rawi says that God wants us to follow the path of justice, not the path of fabrication. For this reason He asks us not to let this readiness for war make us oppressors of God's creation. As long as we have the capacity and have prepared our strength and weapons, that does not mean we should be afflicted with arrogance and become audacious toward God's creatures. This is why Almighty God alerts us to this with His saying:

﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it, and rely upon God. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (61)

That is, God has not required us to be strong so that we may fabricate charges against others. He does not want us to prepare strength for aggression and hostility, but He wants strength to prevent war, so that peace may prevail and pervade the universe. Therefore, glorified and exalted is He, He forbids us to make our readiness for fighting a means of attacking people and fabricating against them. Thus, when the adversary seeks peace and reconciliation, it becomes obligatory for us to make peace with them. Beware of saying, "This is a deception, and they want to deceive us," because you achieve nothing by your strength, but by relying upon Almighty God and being certain that He is with you. Almighty God wants the universe to support one another, not to oppose one another. He, glorified and exalted, asks you for strength so that you may frighten the adversaries, not so that you may wrong them with it and fight them without cause.

As for the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted:

﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾ (part of verse 61, Surat al-Anfal): that is, if they lean toward peace and call you to it, then you too turn toward peace. There is no need for you to accuse them of deception or fear that they will suddenly turn against you, because God, exalted is He, is with you in protection and victory, and after that you keep your readiness constantly with what you have prepared of strength.

And the saying of the Truth: ﴿and rely upon God﴾ (part of verse 61, Surat al-Anfal): that is, beware of relying or depending on anything of the strength you have prepared, because the ultimate matter is that you end up relying upon God, for He protects you. Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted, gives us the reason for that, saying:

﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (part of verse 61, Surat al-Anfal): that is, nothing escapes His hearing if it is speech that is said, or His knowledge if it is an act that is done. Beware of confusing tawakkul (reliance upon God, trust in Him) with tawakul (passive dependence, neglecting action). Reliance is located in the heart while the limbs work; so do not abandon the work of the limbs and claim that you rely upon God. The Muslim should know that vigilance is obligatory, and if you see someone who has lost his alertness, you must alert him to the necessity of vigilance and action. Speech has a role here, and so does action. Therefore, Allah, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (part of verse 61, Surat al-Anfal)

Let us note that the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted:

﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it, and rely upon God. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (61) (Surat al-Anfal)

came after His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of God and your enemy﴾ (part of verse 60, Surat al-Anfal)

and that is a verse that urges readiness for fighting by preparing its equipment.

The Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to alert us that the strength of the believers and their military readiness must not be a tool for tyranny, nor for fighting merely for the sake of fighting. For this reason, glorified and exalted, He alerts us that if they incline toward peace, you should not oppose them and insist on war, because religion wants the peace of society, and Islam spreads not by force but by persuasion and wisdom. There is no necessity for war in spreading Islam, for it is the religion of truth that convinces people by the strength of its argument and attracts their hearts by its tolerance. All of that serves to charge the extent of the strength of faith, so that we may be fully prepared to meet the disbelievers, but without strength making us insolent or leading us to transgress the limit. So if they incline toward peace, we must incline toward peace, because Almighty God wants the safety of human society. And if you fear that their inclination toward peace is a deception on their part, so that we become complacent with them and then they surprise us with treachery, know that their plotting will come to nothing, for they plot with human reasoning, while the believers plot with the reasoning of the Truth, glorified and exalted. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed God is sufficient for you. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ (62)

If you sense that the offer of peace they put before you is merely a deception, meant to let them prepare against you and surprise you with treachery and cunning, then know that God the Exalted is aware of their scheming, and that He will expose it to you. As long as God is with you, they will not be able to deceive you. And if you want your heart to be at rest, then recall the battle of Badr, in which victory came to you from God the Exalted. Its visible causes were embodied in the readiness of the believers for battle and their entering the fight. Its unseen causes were embodied in hosts that no one saw, and in the casting of terror into the hearts of the disbelievers, and victory was yours by the will of God the Exalted.

The Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾. Deception (khada') is the display of a thing that is loved while concealing a thing that is hated. One says, "So-and-so is deceiving me," meaning that he brings me something I love while concealing from me what I dislike. Because deception is the hiding of what is disliked and the proclaiming of what is loved, [the question arises]: are you, O Muhammad, left to them? Surely you have a Lord who is your support, the firm pillar to which you take refuge? The answer comes from the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted:

﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is God. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ [Surah al-Anfal, 62].

So God the Exalted is sufficient for you, your support, and He suffices you, for He has given you victory and strengthened you. You see that this matter has its proof in itself: He gave you victory at Badr despite the small number and the scanty equipment. Ta'yid (support) is the empowering of an act with strength so that it is accomplished in the most complete manner and in the best condition. And since it is God, Mighty and Majestic, who supports, the act must come with the strongest affirmation so that it achieves its purpose and its aim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 63:

He, glorified and exalted, says after that:

﴿And He joined their hearts together. Had you spent all that is on the earth, you could not have joined their hearts together, but Allah joined them together. Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (63):

The support (ta'yid) here has three elements: Allah supports with His help, Allah supports with the believers, and Allah joins together the hearts of the believers. The joining of hearts came because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent to a people who had 'asabiyya (tribal partisanship) and hamiyya (zealous protectiveness), and they were scattered tribes among whom wars arose over the most trivial causes, because the elements of discord among them were more numerous than the elements of harmony.

When the tribe is united, it rushes to defend any individual within it, whatever the reasons and circumstances, to the extent that it is enough for one man of the Aws, for example, to insult one man of the Khazraj for war to break out between the two tribes. Had the hearts remained in their discord, these tribes could not have confronted the enemies of Islam, and their internal wars would have occupied them from supporting the religion, defending it and confronting the disbelievers. But Allah joined them together, and after they had been enemies they became beloved friends, and after they had been estranged they became affectionate toward one another.

Thus Allah joined the hearts of the Muslims, such that Islam became in their hearts, their deeds and their way of life the strongest bond linking them. The brotherhood of religion became stronger than the brotherhood of lineage. When hearts are joined together, this is the strongest bond, because every action a person performs arises from a belief in the heart.

The heart is the source of the intention which is followed by conduct. What moves a person who holds a grudge against you and stirs his limbs against you is the heart. If you find a person frowning in your face, know that there is something in his heart; if you meet him and he tries to strike you, know that there is something greater in his heart; and if he tries to kill you, there is a deeper feeling of hatred and enmity in his heart.

So the wellspring of all feelings is the heart. For this reason we see a person sacrificing everything, and perhaps sacrificing his freedom for what he believed in and what settled in his heart. We see scholars in their laboratories living for many years and depriving themselves of the pleasures of worldly life, because knowledge has turned into a belief in their hearts, whether they are Muslims or otherwise. It is as if the intention of the heart and what settles in it is the strongest thing in life.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, makes clear to us that this is a great favour from Him, that He joined the hearts of the believers together. So He says:

﴿And He joined their hearts together. Had you spent all that is on the earth, you could not have joined their hearts together, but Allah joined them together. Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Anfal).

The joining of hearts is the sum of mutual affection and support. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says in the hadith narrated from him by al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound."

The full hadith: "Indeed the lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters which many people do not know. Whoever guards against doubtful matters has cleared himself regarding his religion and his honour, and whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like the shepherd who grazes around the protected pasture, about to graze within it. Verily, every king has a protected pasture; verily, Allah's protected pasture is His prohibitions. Verily, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart." (1)

The matter of joining hearts is not a matter of needing wealth, because wealth cannot give true love. For this reason there is among people a bond of interests and a bond of hearts. The bond of interests ends as soon as those interests are shaken or come to an end, but the bond of hearts defies every crisis. You cannot make a person truly love you no matter how much money you give him, because true love cannot be bought or sold; what can be bought is hypocrisy, pretence and other superficial feelings. The Arabs whose hearts Allah joined were not concerned with wealth as much as they were concerned with hamiyya and 'asabiyya. Most of them owned wealth, but the division among them stemmed from hamiyya and 'asabiyya, which place in the hearts rancour, envy and hatred; therefore their limbs were stirred. The Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿But Allah joined them together. Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Anfal). Since Allah, glorified and exalted, possesses might, He is not overcome, and since He is Wise, He places matters in their proper position. Allah alone is able to make hearts join together, for hearts are in the hand of the Merciful, who turns them as He wills. Therefore we invoke with the supplication of the Messenger of Allah: "O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated that he said: I said to Salama, may Allah be pleased with her, "O Mother of the Believers, what was the supplication of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he most often made when he was with you?" She said: His most frequent supplication was: "O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." (2)

And He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a man and his heart﴾ (part of verse 24, Surah al-Anfal).

1. Narrated by the two Shaykhs: al-Bukhari and Muslim.
2. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said it is a hasan hadith.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted be He, gives us a matter of faith, saying:

﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you, and for those believers who follow you.ﴩ (64)

Beware lest you think that Allah, mighty and majestic, punishes the disbelievers merely because they did not believe in the messengers of Allah. Rather, it is because the universe is corrupted by their conduct. He, glorified be He, has no need for anyone to believe in Him. Moreover, the religion of truth will prevail whether or not people believe in it, and He, glorified be He, desires for His servants, through the methodology He has sent down, all good and happiness. Therefore, the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Say: Do not count your Islam as a favour upon me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith﴾ (part of verse 17, Surat al-Hujurat).

So when someone enters Islam, he should not boast to Allah that he has submitted, for his Islam will add nothing to the dominion of Allah. Let him know that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has bestowed a favour upon him by guiding him to Islam, and that it is for his own benefit. Allah wills that His Messenger not look to the number or the strength of the disbelievers, because with him is the Strongest, namely Allah, glorified and exalted be He. For this reason He says:

﴿Allah is sufficient for you﴾ (part of verse 64, Surat al-Anfal): that is, Allah suffices you.

﴿and for those believers who follow you﴾ (part of verse 64, Surat al-Anfal), and they are included in ﴿Allah is sufficient for you﴾, because it is Allah who guided these believers to faith, so they believed.

The meaning is: Allah is sufficient for you and sufficient for those believers who follow you, that is, Allah suffices you, and accordingly you should seek honour only from the Truth, glorified and exalted be He.

It may also be that the meaning is: Allah suffices you in matters you cannot accomplish through means, and the believers suffice you in matters where means are available.

Here we note that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, said: ﴿O Prophet﴾ (part of verse 64, Surat al-Anfal). This form of address (al-nida', "calling") is used in matters of conduct (al-ahdath); as for conveying (al-balagh), Allah, exalted be He, says:

﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ (part of verse 67, Surat al-Ma'idah).

Thus, when the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, addresses His Messenger as ﴿O Prophet﴾ when the matter concerns behavioural exemplarity (al-uswah al-sulukiyyah), but when the matter concerns the revelation of legislation (tanzil tashri'), He addresses him, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: ﴿O Messenger﴾. This is because the messengers came conveying the methodology from Allah, and they walk according to this methodology as a behavioural exemplar. Yet we note that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, mentioned each messenger by name in the Noble Qur'an, saying: "O Musa", and said: "O Isa son of Maryam", and said: "O Ibrahim". Except for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; He addressed him as: "O Prophet", and as "O Messenger". This is a subtle point noticed by the people of knowledge (ahl al-ma'rifah), and this form of address carries a particularity for the address to the Muhammadan Presence (al-hadrah al-Muhammadiyyah). Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿O Adam, dwell you and your wife in the Garden﴾ (part of verse 35, Surat al-Baqarah).

And He calls Sayyidina Nuh, saying, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿O Nuh, descend in peace from Us and blessings﴾ (part of verse 48, Surat Hud).

And He calls Sayyidina Musa, saying:

﴿Indeed, O Musa, I am Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (part of verse 30, Surat al-Qasas).

And He calls Sayyidina Isa, saying:

﴿O Isa son of Maryam, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"?﴾ (part of verse 116, Surat al-Ma'idah).

Thus every prophet was called by the Truth, blessed and exalted, by his name alone, except the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; He never said to him: "O Muhammad", but said: "O Prophet" and "O Messenger". And the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, in the noble verse that we are contemplating, wished to draw the attention of His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to know that Allah and the believers suffice him, however few they may be, so that they may triumph over the disbelievers.

Then comes the second address from the Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, in His saying:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ (65)

Whenever you hear that so-and-so urges (يحرض) so-and-so, it means he exhorts him, stirs up his enthusiasm, and incites him to act. The kinds of demand are many. There is a demand we call a call (نداء), that is, you call out to someone. There is a demand we call a command (أمر), that is, you do something. And there is a demand we call a prohibition (نهي), that is, you do not do something. These are all acts of demand, preceded by the call. For example, there is a demand that someone come towards you, another that he keep away from you, and a third that he fulfil a need for you. All of this means that the speaker presents to the listener that he should do such-and-such or not do such-and-such.

There is also a type of demand that does not carry obligation but is merely an offer (عرض), which is a gentle and soft request, like your saying to someone above you: "I am not commanding you, I am only offering you this." A third type of demand is conveyed by the word "ḥaḍḍ" (حض), which is a demand made with intensity, because what is offered along with it is a clear reason for going towards it. When you urge your son to study, for instance, there is a justification for turning to study, which is success. When you urge a person to do something, you neither forbid him nor command him, because you want him to turn to the thing willingly out of love. But if you command him harshly, he may come to hate that thing. You may also present a person with something he loves to do, even without any command from you.

So the saying of God, exalted is He:

﴿urge the believers﴾ (part of verse 65 of Surat al-Anfal)

means: incite them, press them, and rouse them. The verb is composed of the letters ḥ, r and ḍ, from which come "ḥaraḍa" (حرض) and "yuḥarriḍu" (يحرض). The root of this word means being close to ruin (الهلاك). We find the saying of the Truthful, may He be blessed and exalted, on the tongue of Joseph's brothers to their father:

﴿They said, "By God, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become "ḥaraḍan" (حرضا), or you become among those who perish."﴾ (Surat Yusuf, 85), meaning: you will keep on remembering Joseph until you draw near to ruin or actually perish.

But does "ḥarriḍ" (حرِّض) here mean bringing the believers close to ruin? We say no, because of what they call removal (الإزالة), namely that a verb comes in a form that removes the original meaning of its derivation. When you say "qashshartu burtuqālatan" (قشرت برتقالة), it means "I removed its peel." Similarly, when we say "marraḍa al-ṭabīb fulānan" (مرّض الطبيب فلانا), the meaning is not that the doctor brought sickness to him, but that he removed the sickness. So there are verbs that carry the meaning of removal. The meaning of removal comes sometimes by doubling the middle letter, as in "ḥarraḍa" (حرَّض) and "qashsha" (قشَّر), and sometimes by a hamza, which gives the meaning of removal. When you say "a'jama al-kitāb" (أعجم الكتاب), it means he removed its obscurity (عجمته). That is why we call dictionaries "al-ma'ājim" (المعاجم), that is, the books that remove the obscurity of the language and give us the meanings of words. Earlier we explained the meaning of "qasata" (قسط) and "aqsaṭa" (أقسط): "qasata" means injustice (الجور), that is, wrongdoing, in accordance with the saying of God, exalted:

﴿As for the unjust (القاسطون), they will be fuel for Hell.﴾ (Surat al-Jinn, 15), while "aqsaṭa" means he removed injustice. So there are letters which, when added to a word, remove the original meaning of its root. There is also doubling that removes the original derivation, such as "qashshar" (قشّر), meaning he removed the peel, and "marraḍa" (مرَّض), meaning he removed the sickness, and "ḥarraḍa" (حرَّض), meaning he removed the ḥaraḍ (the state of being near ruin).

The meaning of the noble verse is: ask them, O Muhammad, to remove their closeness to ruin through fighting. This linguistic rule explains to us many verses of the Noble Qur'an. In the saying of God, exalted:

﴿Indeed the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it.﴾ (part of verse 15 of Surat Ta-Ha)

those who take the surface meaning say: "akādu ukhfīhā" (أكاد أخفيها) means "I am nearly about to conceal it, so as not to let it appear." We say that the hamza in "akādu" is the hamza of removal, so the meaning of "akādu" is that I am almost about to remove its concealment, through the minor signs and the major signs that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) told us about. Some people have exhausted themselves explaining "akād ukhfīhā" without noticing that the removal of the derivation comes either by doubling the middle letter or by the presence of the hamza. And the saying of the Truthful, may He be blessed and exalted, here:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾ (part of verse 65 of Surat al-Anfal)

means that God, glorified and exalted, asks the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to urge the believers to strive, as if He were saying to him: call your people to remove from themselves the nearness to ruin, because if they do not strive, the people of disbelief will overcome them. The people of disbelief live on earth with a method of domination, victory and tyranny, and when the believers strive against them, it is only to bring them to a halt within their limits. For this reason the Truthful, may He be blessed and exalted, said:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾ (part of verse 65 of Surat al-Anfal)

So it is as if, if they do not fight the people of disbelief, ruin will encompass them in this world and in the Hereafter. God, glorified and exalted, wants for them a secure and dignified life in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. We notice that the Truthful, glorified and exalted, has set a standard of faith in fighting between the believer and the disbeliever, and this standard was set by their Creator, the Creator of their powers, faculties and emotions. The standard of faith is His saying, exalted:

﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve﴾ (part of verse 65 of Surat al-Anfal).

So, in brief, the standard of faith equals one to ten, meaning that the strength of faith makes the strength of the believer equal to the strength of ten disbelievers. This is the measure. Here some people come and say: the methods of the Qur'an are built on concision (الإيجاز) and inimitability (الإعجاز). So why does the Truthful, glorified and exalted, say "twenty will overcome two hundred", then say "a hundred will overcome a thousand"? Could it not have been said: one overcomes ten, and the matter ends there?

We say: you have not observed the reality of Islam, because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to go with the believers in their fighting and be present with them in some of the events of the fighting, which we call "ghazawāt" (غزوات, expeditions in which the Prophet himself took part). As for the military detachments (البعثات القتالية) in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not go out and was content to send a number of believers, these were called "sarāyā" (سرايا, raiding parties). These raiding parties were never fewer than twenty fighters nor more than a hundred. So God, exalted, mentioned them sometimes with twenty and sometimes with a hundred.

Here the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ (part of verse 65 of Surat al-Anfal)

We see that the measure here is by the number of fighters only, but they must be described as steadfast, and in another verse as steadfast and persevering. It is possible that your enemy is steadfast, so then you must match his steadfastness: if he endures a little, you endure a lot; and if he bears the hardship of fighting, you bear more. So fighting strength, in order for victory to be achieved with it and by it, must be a steadfast strength, strong in its faith, able to bear the severity and harshness of fighting.

Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted, gives the reason for this judgment of faith that He has informed us of, saying, mighty is He and exalted:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ (Surat al-Anfal)

So the reason why a believer overcomes ten of the disbelievers is that they are a people who do not understand. And since they do not understand, those opposing them among the believers are a people who understand. Here we compare the believers, who understand, with the disbelievers, who do not understand, and we say: when the disbeliever fights, he does not believe in the Hereafter, and he has nothing but this world, and he fears losing it. For this reason, when a disbeliever is on the battlefield, he wants to preserve his life even by fleeing. But for the believer, the world is a short journey, and martyrdom is the attainment of God's good pleasure and entry into Paradise without reckoning. Therefore he advances to fight with the courage of one who seeks martyrdom. We find Khalid ibn al-Walid saying to the Persians: "I have come to you with men who love death as you love life."

If the disbelievers understood, that is, if they grasped that this world is a passage and a crossing to the Hereafter, and that the Hereafter is the abode of permanence, they would possess a driving force for fighting. But they want this life, because for them it is everything. For this reason the Noble Qur'an teaches us, saying:

﴿Say: "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best outcomes?"﴾ (part of verse 52 of Surat al-Tawba)

meaning: nothing will befall us in this war except what is good. Either we will be victorious, subdue you and seize your wealth, or we will be martyred and enter Paradise, and both are good. The Truthful, glorified and exalted, continues:

﴿We await for you that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself, or by our hands. So await; indeed we are awaiting with you.﴾ (part of verse 52 of Surat al-Tawba). Meaning: you disbelievers will not be struck except by evil and disgrace, either by a severe punishment from God without any causes, or by punishment at our hands, that is, through causes. So the disbeliever, when he enters the battle, expects nothing but evil: either he will be killed and go to Hell, God forbid, or God will afflict him with a punishment that increases the fear in his heart during the battle. The disbelievers in fighting rely only on their strength, their numbers and their equipment; but the believers rely first on fear of God, the Strong, the Mighty, and trust in His victory. For this reason they advance to fight with a great store of the energy of faith, an energy that surpasses numbers and equipment, and the fighter among them is strong in his fighting and eager for it, because he feels he is supported by the victory of God. We know that every person cares about the purpose of his existence, and the purpose of the disbelievers is the limited enjoyment of the life of this world, while the purpose of the believers extends to the Hereafter. Therefore the disbeliever fights with his strength alone, stripped of faith.

We notice that the statements are in the form of information (خبرية) in the saying of the Truthful, may He be blessed and exalted:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ (Surat al-Anfal)

Statements in the form of information contain no demand, even if a demand comes in the form of a report, to give you the impression that this is a fixed fact. When some rebels some years ago entered the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) with their weapons and besieged the people in it, some superficial people said: the Qur'an says:

﴿And whoever enters it is secure﴾ (part of verse 97 of Surat Ali Imran)

and that this is a cosmic report, meaning that everyone who enters the Haram is safe. We said: the saying of the Truthful, may He be blessed and exalted, "and whoever enters it is secure," is the word of God; so whoever obeys God, let him grant security to whoever enters the Haram. You may obey and grant security to whoever enters the Haram, and you may disobey and not grant them security. So the matter is a ruling that you may obey or not obey. Likewise the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted:

﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ (part of verse 228 of Surat al-Baqara)

This is a statement in the form of information. If the divorced woman obeys God, she waits this period; if she disobeys, she does not wait. Likewise His saying, exalted:

﴿Good women are for good men, and good men are for good women﴾ (part of verse 26 of Surat al-Nur)

We may see in the universe marriages that are the opposite of this: you find a base man marrying a good woman, and a base woman marrying a good man. And you may ask: why did the good man not marry a good woman, in confirmation of His saying, exalted, and why did the wicked

The Almighty then says:

﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you a hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast.﴾ (66)

In this ruling there is a lightening of the previous ruling, in which it came that twenty steadfast would overcome two hundred. We know that there are conditions for fighting, the first of which is that the fighter be strong in body and strong in faith, and knowledgeable in the stratagems and arts of war, such that he can manoeuvre, change his position in the battle, and deceive his enemy; for the outcome of a battle is not decided by one battle alone, but there must be advance and retreat, attack and withdrawal, and deception in fighting and manoeuvres, just as Khalid ibn al-Walid did in many battles.

So, for you to ensure that twenty steadfast will overcome two hundred, there must be realised in all of them strength of body, patience and endurance. But bodily strength may not be available and endurance may be weak. Periods of weakness come to a person, and periods of strength also come to him. Among His mercy towards the believers is that He lightened it for them, because He knows that periods of weakness afflict a person; therefore He made the ratio one to two. And the Almighty said:

﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you a hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast.﴾.

Does this mean that the first verse has been abrogated (naskh)? We say: no, but the second verse took account of circumstances of change and human weakness and reckoned with them. Therefore we find the first ruling standing, and it is the upper limit; and the second ruling too stands, and it is the lower limit. If a believer meets three disbelievers and flees from them, he is not counted as a deserter on the day of battle, and Allah does not hold him to account for it. But if two confront him and he withdraws and leaves them, he is considered a deserter, because the lower limit is one against two, not two against one... [the remainder of this sentence and the passage follows in the original and is not included here].

And after that the words of the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, were revealed:

﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre in the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (67)

"Asra" (captives) is the plural of "asir" (captive). The definition of the captive is one who is bound with fetters by the one who has taken him, so that he is in the grip of his hand. In Islam, the captive is the source of servitude and slavery, because the captive falls into the grip of an enemy stronger than him, and the enemy is able to kill him or take him as a slave.

So in this situation, one does not compare a captive who has become an enemy with a free person. Rather, we compare killing the captive with keeping him alive. Which is more beneficial for the captive: that he remain alive and become a captive, or that he be killed?

His remaining alive is something required and desired for him. Thus, the legislation of Allah, glorified and exalted, regarding the possession of captives, Allah intended by it to preserve their blood and keep their lives; for the captive is in a position where he can be killed, and it was possible to leave the captives so that they would be killed and the problem would end. But the Truthful, glorified and exalted, wanted to preserve even the blood of the disbeliever, because Allah is the One who summoned him to this life and made him a successor, and therefore He preserves him. And perhaps after that he will be guided and believe. We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) cursed whoever demolishes the structure of Allah except for a just cause.

Moreover, Islam has been falsely accused of having legislated slavery, but the truth is that it did not initiate or create captivity and slavery. Rather, it was an existing system at the time Islam appeared, and the sources of slavery were many, rightly or wrongly, by war or without war. One might commit a wrong against another and be unable to compensate him, so he says: "Take me as your slave," or "Take my daughter as a slave-girl." Another might be a debtor and say: "Take my son as your slave, or my daughter as your slave-girl." So the sources of slavery were numerous, and there was only one means of manumission, namely the master's will to free his slave or emancipate him.

This means that the number of slaves and servants kept increasing and never decreased, because its sources were many, and there was only one door through which to exit. When Islam came and found the situation thus, it wanted to address the problem of slavery and work to eliminate it. Among the characteristics of Islam is that it deals with such matters gradually, not abruptly. Islam abolished all sources of slavery except one, namely lawful war declared by the Imam or ruler. Any enslavement outside lawful war is forbidden, and it is not permitted to enslave by any means other than that. At the same time, Islam multiplied the doors of manumission, and made it an expiation for many sins which are not expiated for, nor forgiven by, Allah, glorified and exalted, except by freeing a slave. Indeed, He added to that the great reward that one who frees a slave out of love for Allah and faith in Him obtains. Allah, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿But he has not attempted the steep path. And what can make you know what the steep path is? It is the freeing of a slave﴾ (Surat al-Balad)

If a person has not committed a sin that requires freeing a slave, and has not freed a slave with the zeal of faith, then in that case he must treat the captive as a brother in Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, as narrated from him by our master Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him): "Your brothers are your servants; Allah has placed them under your authority. So whoever has his brother under his authority, let him feed him from what he eats, clothe him from what he wears, and not burden him with what overwhelms him; and if he burdens him with what overwhelms him, let him help him."(1)

Thus this noble hadith made equal between slave and master, and removed the distinction between them; it made the slave wear what his master wears and eat what he eats, or eat with him; in work he helps him and places his hand with his; and he addresses him only as "my young man" or "my young woman."

So Islam came while slavery existed, its doors were many, and its outlet was one. It closed all the doors except one, and opened the outlets of slavery so that it would be completely eliminated gradually. As for women, the heavenly legislation came in the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿And if you fear that you will not deal justly, then one only, or what your right hands possess﴾ (part of verse 3, Surat an-Nisa')

This was a new door among the doors for eliminating slavery, because if a female slave married a male slave like herself, she would remain in her servitude and her children would be slaves. But if a man took her to his household and she became the mother of his child, her children would be free. Thus Islam continued the elimination of slavery; at the same time, it removed from the female the sexual deprivation that could lead her to deviate, being far from her family and cut off from her environment, seeing around her wives enjoying care, tenderness and the love of husbands—a matter that stirs emotions. So it permitted a man, if their feelings were mutually agreeable, to have relations with her as with his free wife, and to father children by her while she was a slave-girl. In that there is an elevation of her status, because by bearing children she becomes a wife, and at the same time an elimination of slavery.

This matter has provoked much controversy about Islam, and things have been said about it that are entirely lies and fabrication. Now, after slavery has been abolished politically by international treaties, these ended at the same principles Islam brought, namely the exchange of captives and reciprocity. This principle was first brought by Islam: it is not reasonable that an enemy of mine take my children and enslave them as he wishes while I release his captive children in my custody. Rather, reciprocity: if he bestows, we bestow; if he ransoms, we ransom. The Truthful, glorified and exalted, willed to restrict enslavement from captivity in His saying:

﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre in the land﴾ (part of verse 67, Surat al-Anfal).

We say: there is a difference between a ruling that precedes the event, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not contradict, and a ruling that comes with the event. We must distinguish between the two rulings. If a ruling that precedes the event is contravened, there is a violation; but a ruling that comes with the event is a different matter. Let us suppose you are sitting and someone comes to you and says that your relative so-and-so went to such-and-such a place, that he is spending on such-and-such, and gave a promissory note on himself for such-and-such an amount; go to him and stop him. You go to him and stop him. Here the ruling came with the event, so there is no violation.

And the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted:

﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre in the land﴾ (part of verse 67, Surat al-Anfal).

This ruling came after the capture of the disbelievers of Quraysh and their being taken to Medina, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted the Companions regarding them and they reached a decision. So the ruling came after the matter had concluded, and the evidence for this is that Allah, glorified and exalted, did not change the ruling, so captivity and ransom remained. So: "It is not for a Prophet to have captives" means: it is not fitting for a Prophet to have captives until he is harsh toward the disbelievers in fighting.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, wants here to alert the believers that if they desired captives for the goods of this world—such as someone who covets one who serves him, or covets a woman to satisfy his need from her, or wealth by which he seeks a comfortable life—all of that is rejected, because Allah, glorified and exalted, does not want the believer to make this world his greatest concern. Rather, the Truthful wants the believers to learn and to do well in succession on the earth, so as to establish justice to the extent of their ability, and so that Allah may then reward them with the everlasting, blessed life in Paradise.

Therefore the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted said:

﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre in the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ (Surat al-Anfal), and He, glorified, is the Mighty who is not overcome, and the Wise who places everything in its proper place.

(1) Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Majah.

Next comes His saying, glory be to Him and exalted is He:

﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.﴾

This noble verse explains and makes clear that Allah, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, does not hold anyone accountable except after legislation has been revealed that sets out the premises and their consequences, and defines the offences and the penalties. Had it not been so, a great punishment would have befallen the believers for taking the captives, before the call had become firmly established. Since Allah, blessed and exalted is He, sends no punishment except for a transgression that has been preceded by legislation defining it, had it not been for that, punishment would have come down upon the believers. But since this act had not been made a crime beforehand, there is no punishment for it.

Now the Exalted turns to the spoils that the believers obtained in the Battle of Badr, so He says, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿So eat of what you have taken as spoils, [being] lawful and good, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (69)

That is: beware lest you spend what you have seized wastefully on anything that is not necessary. Rather, fear Allah regarding what He has given you and granted you of spoils, whether they are movable goods, wealth, or captives whom you make to perform tasks whose benefit and return come back to you. Fear Allah in all of this, and do not spend it foolishly. As for His statement, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, it means that Allah the Exalted has forgiven you for what you did before this noble verse was revealed.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 8, verse 70:

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, addresses the captives after that, saying:

﴿O Prophet, say to those captives who are in your hands: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you. And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ (8:70)

That is: if the words of al-Abbas concerning his Islam are true, and that he had concealed his Islam, then Allah knows what is in his heart, and He will give him better than what was taken from him. And indeed, Allah the Exalted gave al-Abbas good in return. Al-Tabari transmitted from al-Abbas that he said: "This verse was revealed concerning me, when I informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of my Islam and asked him to reckon for me the twenty ounces (of gold) that were taken from me before the ransom, but he refused and said: 'That is spoils (fay'),' so Allah replaced that for me with twenty slaves, each of whom trades with my wealth."

In the narration mentioned by Ibn Kathir (al-Abbas said): "Allah gave me in Islam, in place of the twenty ounces, twenty slaves, each of whom has wealth in his hand with which he trades, in addition to what I hope for of the forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic(1)." Thus was fulfilled the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you...﴾ (8:70) (Surat al-Anfal)

After this noble verse was revealed, and it agreed with the decisions the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had taken, he (ﷺ) informed the captives of the final judgment from Allah: "You will not be released except by ransom or by having your necks struck." At this point our master Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "O Messenger of Allah, except Suhayl ibn Bayda', for I know him to mention Islam and to do such-and-such." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent, and I never feared more that stones would fall upon me from the sky than I feared on that day, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Except Suhayl ibn Bayda'."

And the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And He will forgive you. And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ (part of 8:70, Surat al-Anfal)

That is: as long as there is good in your hearts, and you have believed or will enter Islam, then Allah knows what is in your hearts, and He will forgive you, for He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

1. Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir.

And when the matter was settled, some of the captives said: "O Messenger of God, we have wealth in Makkah. Permit us to go there and bring you the ransom." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) feared that this might be a deception and a scheme. What should he do? Should he release them and trust them to bring the ransom, or is this a ruse, with treachery and betrayal concealed within?

Then the word of the Truth, may He be exalted, was revealed:

﴿And if they intend to betray you, they have already betrayed God before, so He gave you power over them. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise (71).﴾

The Truth, may He be exalted, makes clear to His Messenger (ﷺ): Do not agree to what they want. If they conceal treachery against you, they have already betrayed God before, and He has given you power over them. So do not feel secure with them. He, may He be exalted, knows what is in their breasts.

After He, may He be exalted, had spoken of the story of Badr and the captives of Badr, and of the positions taken by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions in this story, He wished to classify the Islamic community contemporary with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) into its components. We know that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) proclaimed the Islamic call in Makkah, and Makkah was the seat of Arab dominance. The tribe of Quraysh was the lord of all the Arab tribes and the lord of the whole Arabian Peninsula, because Quraysh were the masters of Makkah, and in Makkah stands the Sacred House of God. Every Arab tribe had some of its members within the sphere of Quraysh's authority during the Hajj. And as long as every tribe went to Makkah, it sought the protection of Quraysh. No tribe was hostile to Quraysh or dared to attack them, because it knew that a day would come when it would be under Quraysh's protection and at their mercy during the Hajj to the Sacred House of God.

Thus the dominance of Quraysh arose from the existence of the House. Had this House not existed, the position of Quraysh would have been like the position of any other Arab tribe. And had the House been destroyed by Abraha, the dominance of Quraysh would have ended. Therefore we find the Truth, may He be exalted, saying in Surat al-Fil:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plot go astray? And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of baked clay, and made them like eaten straw (1–5).﴾ (Surat al-Fil)

Immediately after it comes the noble surah that clarifies for us that God, may He be exalted, when He preserved His House and destroyed the armies of the aggressors, making them like eaten straw, confirmed this dominance for Quraysh. He, blessed and exalted, says in the surah named after them:

﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh (1), their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer (2). So let them worship the Lord of this House (3), who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear (4).﴾ (Surat Quraysh)

Thus it is the Sacred House of God that gave Quraysh their dominance. For this reason their caravans went with trade to Yemen and Syria, and no tribe dared to molest them. Had the Sacred House of God not been in Makkah, and Quraysh not been the masters of Makkah, they would not have had this distinguished status and lofty rank. So the might of Quraysh lies in the Sacred House of God, and their security and dominance lie in the fact that they sit at ease while their caravans travel to Syria and Yemen and return laden with goods and profit, while they remain secure and at peace. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) announced his call, that announcement was made in Makkah, and he (ﷺ) proclaimed it in the face of the tyrants and the powerful of the whole Arabian Peninsula. Had the Messenger of God (ﷺ) begun his call among a weak tribe outside Makkah, they would have said: he has made weak people his dupes and deceived them, or they would have said: he wants dominion through it. That is, as a weak tribe they would not have accepted the message of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), but they would have taken it peacefully in order to rule the Arabian Peninsula through it. But God, blessed and exalted, willed that the birth of the message should be in Makkah, and that the first to hear it should be the lords of Quraysh, so that it would appear at the seat of dominance, and its purpose would be the Truth and its elevation in the face of the lords of the Arabian Peninsula.

Then the battle took place between the lords of Quraysh and Islam. They harmed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and those with him, and tried to halt the call by every means and every stratagem. But did they prevail? And did Islam spread and expand from Makkah? No. Rather, there was the Hijrah to Madinah, and from there Islam spread.

Thus Islam began from a place of dominance in the Arabian Peninsula, but it spread from a place with no dominance. Why? Because had Islam spread from Makkah, they would have said: a people accustomed to dominance over others, who showed partisanship for one of their own, in order to extend their dominance from the Arabian Peninsula to other places in the world. But victory came from Madinah so that the whole world would know that faith in Muhammad is what created solidarity for Muhammad, and it is what achieved victory for Muhammad. It did not create solidarity for the Messenger of God merely because he was of Quraysh, or because he was of a tribe accustomed to the dominance of the Arabian Peninsula.

The Truth, may He be exalted, also classifies for us the believers in the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Among them are the Muhajirun (emigrants), and among them are the Ansar (helpers), and among them is a community of believers who did not emigrate with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) but emigrated afterwards, and among them is a community who believed but did not emigrate from Makkah, and remained there until the Conquest (al-Fath).

So: there are four groups: those who emigrated with the Messenger to Madinah, and the Ansar who received them and sheltered them; a group who did not emigrate with the Messenger of God but emigrated after that; and a group who remained in Makkah until the Conquest.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-Anfal (8), verse 72:

The Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped — those are allies of one another. And those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe them no duty of protection until they emigrate. But if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help them, except against a people between whom and you there is a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (8:72)

The first group in this verse are the Emigrants (muhajirun), of whom the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾ (part of 8:72).

The second group are the Helpers (ansar), of whom the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿and those who gave shelter and helped﴾ (part of 8:72).

Then Allah unites the Emigrants and the Helpers, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿Those are allies of one another﴾ (part of 8:72).

Some scholars interpreted the words of the Almighty, ﴿allies of one another﴾, as including complete solidarity, to the point that they used to inherit from one another at first — according to the scholars — until the verses of inheritance were revealed, which cancelled that inheritance that existed between them.

And the words of the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿But blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ (part of 8:75)

set aside this meaning. Some scholars said: the wilaya (allegiance/guardianship) is support, it is affection, it is honouring, it is esteem. They said: these are the attributes of wilaya. There is another verse about the Helpers in which the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿And those who had already settled in the abode and in faith before them love those who emigrate to them, and find in their breasts no need for what they have been given, and prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves are in privation﴾ (part of 59:9).

We have learned much about the altruism of the Helpers, which reached a level that no human attains except through sincere faith. For a man who lives in blessing and has a friend or beloved wishes to honour him by sharing his blessing: if he has a car, for example, he gives it to him to use; if he has a beautiful house, he may invite him to stay in it for a while; if he has a fine garment or a rare fruit, he may give him some of it. Except for a wife — she is the blessing which a man disdains to share with anyone.

But when the Emigrants arrived in Medina and had left their women in Mecca, a Helper would come to an Emigrant and say: "Look at my wives, and whichever of them pleases you, I will divorce her so that you may marry her." This is a matter that only complete faith can produce, and when faith produces it, that faith cuts off the nose of jealousy and prevents it from stirring, and there is no one who has more than one wife while another is deprived of a woman.

The Almighty has defined for us the distinction of each category of believers and explained their rulings. The first category is the Emigrants, who believed and abandoned the religion they had grown up in, then emigrated and left their homelands, their houses, their wealth, their wives, their children, their camels and their crops. Then they worked to support themselves with wealth they earned, and from it they also spent on jihad; even though they had left their property and everything they owned in Mecca, they were as if they had sacrificed both wealth and self. They entered battle while they were few — however few they were, they numbered no more than three hundred — and they entered a fight against the mass of polytheists, not certain of victory, but seeking martyrdom.

So, they believed (one), they emigrated (two), they strove with their wealth (three), and they strove with their lives (four). They were exemplars, because they were the first to faith and jihad, and they encouraged others to believe; for them is the reward of whoever establishes a good practice and the reward of whoever acts upon it. These are the foremost early ones, and they have a high and great station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

The second category is the Helpers, who are those who gave shelter (one), helped (two), and loved those who emigrated to them (three). Allah has joined these in wilaya — that is, support, affection, esteem and honouring. Then the word of the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, comes:

﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe them no duty of protection at all until they emigrate﴾ (part of 8:72).

These are the third category: those who believed and abandoned the religion they had grown up in, but did not emigrate, did not leave their homelands, their children, their wives or their wealth. So in them there is one praiseworthy trait and a second trait that is not in their favour; their position is in-between. But because they did not emigrate, the ruling from Allah comes:

﴿You owe them no duty of protection at all until they emigrate﴾ (part of 8:72).

So this category believed but did not emigrate, yet their not emigrating does not give them guardianship over you. However, the words of the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿You owe them no duty of protection at all until they emigrate﴾ (part of 8:72)

contain an encouragement for them to emigrate, like saying to your son: "You will get no reward from me until you study." This is an encouragement to him to study. And Allah, glory be to Him, did not cut off the path to emigration before them, lest they think that emigration was only for the first groups, since He said: "Those who believed and emigrated" — meaning the door is open.

The word "hajaru" (they emigrated) derives from the quadriliteral verb "hajara", the noun "hijra" and the verb "haajara". "Hajara" is not the same as "haajara". A person may leave a place in which he lives, and this means "hajara", that is, to abandon, and it is out of scarcity and constraint that drives one to flee. But "haajara" requires an interaction between two parties that compelled him to emigrate. So there are two processes: the persecution of the unbelievers against the Muslims — for if they had not persecuted them and they had lived in safety, openly declaring their faith and Islam, emigration would not have happened. But the persecution the Muslims faced was an interaction that led to their emigration. Al-Mutanabbi says:

"If you depart from a people while they have decided that you should never leave them, it is they who are the departing ones."

That is, if you leave a people without their compelling you to do so, then you are the one who departed from them. But the emigration undertaken by the Muslims was because the unbelievers forced them to it. So "hajara" is from one side, while the noun "hijra" derives from "haajara", meaning that Allah, glory be to Him, is saying: the dwelling in which you were persecuted was one that it would have been right for you to leave. The Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, makes clear:

﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe them no duty of protection at all until they emigrate, but if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help them﴾ (part of 8:72)

That is, there must be a bond of faith, without the full wilaya owed to believers who did not emigrate. Faith has its due in the words of the Exalted:

﴿but if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help them﴾ (part of 8:72).

But the help here is conditioned by another condition:

﴿except against a people between whom and you there is a treaty﴾ (part of 8:72).

So safeguard this treaty, for breaking covenants is not among the teachings of the Islamic religion. As long as there is a treaty between you and them, settlement must be reached through understanding. You must honour what you have agreed upon and pledged. Then the Almighty, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ (8:72).

That is, He knows and sees what you do. Allah, glory be to Him, has gathered them as believers in one verse, and they are all in ranks of faith, one category.

Then the discourse turns to the second, opposing category, and He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. Unless you do this, there will be fitnah (turmoil) on earth and great corruption.﴾ (8:73)

The disbelievers, as we know, and as the noble verse tells us, are allies of one another.

If the believers do not gather together, bonding closely and being of one heart, then the disbelievers will gather by the very nature of their disbelief and their hostility to Islam. And if the Muslims do not gather in mutual bonds, we find the word of the Truth warning them against this:

﴿Unless you do this, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption.﴾ (part of 8:73)

So He, glorified be He, wants us to know that if we do not live as Muslims who are united, supporting one another as a cohesive community, bound together in harmony and faith, if we do not do that, then there will be severe fitnah and great corruption. Why? Because if the believers do not gather together, they will dissolve into the disbelievers, and there will be oscillation and imbalance in the faith balance generation after generation. If such dissolution happens, children and young people will be raised in a society where falsehood is mixed with faith, so they will take from this and take from that, and they will not recognize the original values of their religion, and Muslims may weaken before the allure of this world and follow the disbelievers. But if the Muslims live in solidarity and mutual cooperation, there will be a safeguard against the diseases of disbelief, and their adversaries will not dare to attack them.

However, if they do not gather and do not unite, their adversaries may dare to act against them, they will become a few here and a few there, and their prestige will be lost. But if they unite, they will be strong, not only through their faith but through their faith-based capacity that attracts non-Muslims to this religion. Great corruption arises when Muslims do not support one another, so non-Muslims dare against them, and they become humiliated although they are a majority, and no one fears them despite their great numbers, and they do not become a behavioral model; rather, they become a bad example for Islam. The Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾ (part of 8:73)

Is this a directive from Allah, mighty and majestic, to them, or a report about the reality of their state?

Allah, glorified and exalted, has commanded the believers to be allies of one another. But is His saying, ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾, a command to the disbelievers, as His command to the believers is? We say: No, because those who disbelieve do not read the words of Allah, mighty and majestic, and if they read them, they do not act upon them.

Thus this is a report of a cosmic reality concerning the disbelievers. When Allah, glorified and exalted, commands the believers to be allies of one another, this is a legislation which Allah wants the believers to be keen upon; but when He says that the disbelievers are allies of one another, this is a report of a cosmic reality concerning them.

Islam came to the people of the idols of Quraysh, and the Jews in Medina were People of the Book. Likewise, the Aws and the Khazraj were disbelievers like Quraysh; but Islam united them and made some of them allies of one another. Before Islam, there had been enmity between the Aws and the Khazraj and the Jews, though it did not reach the point of war, because they needed the Jews' wealth and their knowledge in other matters. The Jews would threaten the Aws and the Khazraj with the coming of the Prophet Muhammad, who is mentioned among them in the Torah, saying to them: The time of a prophet whom we will follow has drawn near, and we will kill you with the killing of 'Ad and Iram.

So the Jews used to threaten the disbelievers, because of the doctrinal and religious enmity between them. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, the Jews disbelieved in his message and allied with the disbelievers of Quraysh, and they said: ﴿These are better guided than those who believed in the way﴾ (4:51), meaning that the disbelievers of Quraysh are better guided than those who believed in Muhammad. So the alliance between the disbelievers and the Jews came after they had been enemies, but they united afterward against the believers. If this has happened between the disbelievers and the Jews, then it is obligatory upon the believers that some of them be allies of one another, because they have gathered upon something that all oppose.

This negates the matter of inheritance which some scholars have derived, that the believers are allies of one another meaning that they inherit from one another; for if this were correct, it would be as though Allah were legislating for the disbelievers too that they inherit from one another, since He used the word "allies" for them as well. And Allah, glorified and exalted, has not legislated for the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 8, verse 74:

Having explained the categories of believers who lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and having found that they are four, we have mentioned three of them: the Muhajirun (the emigrants), the Ansar (the helpers), and those who believed but did not emigrate. There remains from these categories those who believed and emigrated afterwards. The Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, says:

﴿And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped – those are the believers in truth. For them is forgiveness and an honourable provision.﴾

That is: beware lest you say that they did not emigrate with you, and deny that they are of you. Rather, they are of you and your allies, for they have followed you with excellence.

What made the Exalted One mention this again? He, glory be to Him, spoke of those who believed, strove in the way of Allah, and those who helped. Let us be mindful that this is not a repetition, for He, glory be to Him, is telling us here that they strove with wealth and with their selves. This verse came to confirm the legal ruling. Look at the final part of each verse, so that you may know. In the final part of this verse:

﴿Those are the believers in truth. For them is forgiveness and an honourable provision.﴾ (Surat al-Anfal)

The legal ruling concerning them is that they be allies of one another, and this is what Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned in the previous verse, where He says:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped – those are allies of one another.﴾ (part of verse 72, Surat al-Anfal)

That is, He gave us the legal ruling on the alliance of some of them with others, and clarified that these must be allies, and this is the ruling required of them. But in this noble verse:

﴿And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped – those are the believers in truth.﴾ (part of verse 74, Surat al-Anfal)

the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, does not speak here about alliance and does not give a ruling on it. Rather, He says: ﴿those are the believers in truth﴾, and this is a restriction which they call qasr (restriction), meaning that others are not truly believers. It is like when we say: "So-and-so is the man", meaning that others' manhood is not considered complete in its aspects. This is an exaggeration in faith.

Then the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, concludes the noble verse which is the subject of our reflections with His noble saying: ﴿For them is forgiveness and an honourable provision﴾ (part of verse 74, Surat al-Anfal). Here the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted speaks of recompense. Recompense is either in this world, and therefore Allah has judged that they are the believers in truth, or the recompense is in the Hereafter. The recompense of the Hereafter erases evil deeds and raises ranks. So His saying ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾ means their evil deeds are erased. And His saying, exalted be He, ﴿and an honourable provision﴾ means their good deeds are multiplied in Paradise. Thus the first verse was intended for the ruling of alliance, which is a required ruling from them, and the second verse spoke of recompense and clarified their recompense in this world and the Hereafter. The recompense in this world is that they are the believers in truth; as for the recompense in the Hereafter, it is the erasure of sins so that they are not punished, and the raising of their ranks by giving them reward, which is an honourable provision.

The forgiveness granted to them is for minor sins, because no one is free from stumbling in some matters, and no one is infallible like the messengers; they alone are those whom Allah protected from falling into disobedience. Therefore the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted forgives those mentioned in this verse their minor lapses, and He also has an honourable provision. Provision is that from which a person benefits, although people look at provision as being only material: wealth, land, property, food and clothing. But the truth is that provision is a combination of many things, some material and some immaterial.

Uprightness is provision, virtue is provision, knowledge is provision, piety is provision, and whenever the benefit of provision extends, it is described as good and beautiful. Here Allah described the provision as honourable (karim). Honour (karam) is the combination of the things in which there are excellences. When provision comes without toil, it is honourable: air is provision in which you have no work; it passes over you and you breathe.
