Water is provision in which you have no work, because it descends upon you from the sky. Food is provision in which you have a small amount of work: you sow, you water, and you wait until the fruit comes.

So there is provision in which you have no work at all, and it is provision in the utmost honour; and there is provision in which you have a slight work, and it is an honourable provision because it exceeds the work. When you give a person his wage, this is not a favour from you or generosity, because it is in return for work; but generosity is to give without return. The provision of Paradise is without return, because the moment a thing occurs to your mind and you desire it, you find it before you.

So it is provision in the utmost honour, and the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted has made honour one of the attributes of provision. Provision knows your address and your place, while you do not know its address or its place, because you exert great effort in cultivating your land, then a blight comes and strikes the crop, and it gives you no provision. You may go to a place with your mind empty, and a deal comes to you containing abundant provision.

So provision knows your place and comes to you, but you do not know where it is. Allah, glory be to Him, has determined provision and divided it among His servants, and every provision decreed for you will reach you and will not go to anyone else. You may eat a food you enjoy, then your stomach becomes upset and you empty your stomach of it, and a bird comes to peck at some of it; this is the provision of the bird, which you dislike. And you may eat food which turns into components in your blood, then you go and donate this blood to someone else.

So this food which you ate and which turned into blood in your body is not your provision, but the provision of the one to whom the blood was transferred. Therefore, when you read the Qur'an you find that the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted says:

﴿And Allah presents a parable: a town which was secure and at peace, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place﴾ (part of verse 112, Surat al-Nahl). Provision comes to you and you do not go to it; and if provision is tied in this world to the causes of work, then provision in the Hereafter comes to you without work.

Almighty Allah says after that:

﴿And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and strove alongside you — those are of you. And relatives are more entitled to one another in the Decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ :

So whoever believed after those first ones, emigrated and strove, also has forgiveness and a noble provision.

Thus Almighty Allah has defined the categories of believers and given each category its station. Those who believed have all been attached to Allah with a primary attachment. For this reason we find that Almighty Allah created man subjugated (maqhur) in some things and free to choose in others, in what he does or does not do. The believer chooses what Allah wills for him; he does what He said to him, "Do," and does not do what He said to him, "Do not do," so it is as if he has chosen the things Allah desires in legislation.

The meaning of faith is that it settles in your heart, and that you believe that Allah, with all the attributes of His perfection, created this universe for us and created us, and that we came to this universe and found it prepared for us in excellent preparation: everything in it is subjected to serve man. Allah the Exalted has given us choice in some things, and by His mercy has made us subjugated in other things.

For example, the beating of the heart, the circulation of the blood, and your inner body parts are subjugated to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; your choice has no part in them. Likewise breathing: you breathe while you are asleep and do not know how that happens. But the actions that proceed from you after thought, those are the actions in which Allah has given you choice. Had the Creator willed you to be subjugated in action, He would have done so; had He willed that all people believe, He would have done so. But He, Glorified and Exalted, left them the choice: "whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve," so that He might know which of His servants loved Allah and obeyed Him in the obligation, and which of the creation disobeyed Him.

So the primary attachment of the Muslim is the attachment of faith. Man has other attachments: he belongs to his homeland, his family, his children, and his wealth. But the primary attachment must be to Allah the Exalted, such that people leave their homelands, their wealth, and their families if faith requires that. The believing man is the one who sets aside his own choice and chooses what Almighty Allah has commanded, and makes all that he owns serve that: he strives with his person because Allah commanded him to, and strives with his wealth because Allah commanded him to. Thus the true believer has no attachment except to Allah. Those who emigrated, and those who sheltered and helped, left their wealth, their children, and everything they possessed out of love for Allah and obedience to Him.

As for the Ansar, they did not emigrate, but they placed all their capacities at the service of sheltering the emigrants out of love for Allah; they gave up homes and wealth of their own, and gave up their wives for the sake of Allah. Each of them is a true believer. As for the second category, there is a deficiency in their faith: they did not emigrate despite their Islam, and preferred to remain with their children and families. Therefore Allah the Exalted said of them:

﴿You owe them nothing of their guardianship until they emigrate﴾ (part of verse 74, Surat al-Anfal): that is, it is not required that you take them as allies, but if they seek your help in religion, then you must help them. Why? Because they have not abandoned the other attachments such as wealth, children, family, and place of residence. The third category are those who came after that. There was no emigration for them to make, but whoever among them believed, strove, gave up his own choice, and submitted fully to the choice of Allah, becomes like the earlier believers, because they abandoned all attachments for the sake of Allah the Exalted.

Then Allah, Glorified, concludes Surat al-Anfal with this noble verse:

﴿And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and strove alongside you — those are of you. And relatives are more entitled to one another in the Decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).
